QUESTION: To what extent does endurance training elicit coordinated molecular responses across different
organs, and which tissues exhibit the most similar changes?

ANSWER
======

DATA AND METHOD IN ONE LINE
The MoTrPAC rat endurance-training differential-analysis table (279,002 rows covering 20 tissues, 9 assays,
2 sexes and 4 timepoints (1w/2w/4w/8w); every feature in the file is FDR-significant at training_q < 0.05)
was used to compare
each pair of organs by the DIRECTIONAL CONCORDANCE of their training response: for every pair, the fraction
of jointly regulated features whose timewise logFC has the same sign, pooled over 4 timepoints x 2 sexes
(each stratum weighted by the number of shared features) and tested with an exact two-sided binomial test
against the 50% null. Sign concordance was chosen as the primary statistic because significance selection in
the source table is sign-agnostic, so this metric has a valid null even though only significant features are
supplied (correlation and set-overlap metrics do not). 118 tissue pairs had >= 100 shared regulated features
(162,326 shared-feature observations).

HOW MUCH COORDINATION IS THERE? (extent)
* Real but modest, and strongly outweighed by tissue specificity.
* Weighted cross-tissue concordance = 56.2% vs a 50% null (median 55.9%, IQR 51.9-61.0%, range 33.7-80.0%).
  79/118 tissue pairs are significantly concordant (BH q < 0.05), 8/118 significantly DISCORDANT, and
  47/118 lie within 45-55%, i.e. indistinguishable from chance.
* Transcriptome (the only assay covering ~all organs; 19 tissues, 9,800 regulated genes): median pairwise
  Spearman r of the 8w logFC vectors is only +0.112 (female) / +0.094 (male); only 18.6% (female) / 26.6%
  (male) of pairs reach r > 0.3 and <= 2-8.5% reach r > 0.5. Weighted concordance 53.7%.
* The average pair shares no more regulated genes than chance: median observed/expected overlap ratio 0.95
  (female) / 1.00 (male) against the union universe.
* Response is cell-type specific even for shared genes: of 9,800 regulated transcripts, 4,969 (50.7%) are
  regulated in exactly ONE of 19 tissues, 482 (4.9%) in >= 5 tissues, only 2 (Ghitm, Mt-atp6) in 9, and
  NONE in >= 10. Even for the 482 multi-tissue genes the logFC sign matches the gene's own majority
  direction only 67.7% of the time (just 14/482 are fully consistent).
* Where a shared core does exist it is mitochondrial/OXPHOS + innate-immune: Mt-atp6, Mt-cyb, Mt-nd1,
  Ndufa12, Cox5a, Ghitm; Bst2, Gpnmb, Hmgn2, Nfam1, Galnt6, Evi2b, Acap1, C3, Ifi27l2a.
* Coordination is stronger at the protein than the transcript level (pooled concordance PROT 68.2% vs
  TRNSCRPT 53.7%) and strengthens with training duration in the proteome (64.2% at 1w -> 66.0% at 2w ->
  69.8% at 4w -> 72.7% at 8w) and in DNA methylation (54.4% -> 70.1%), while the transcriptome stays flat
  (53.5% -> 54.9%).

WHICH TISSUES ARE THE MOST SIMILAR?
Ranked by pooled directional concordance across all assays/timepoints/sexes (n = shared regulated features):

 1. SKM-GN <-> SKM-VL  (gastrocnemius <-> vastus lateralis)   80.0%  (n=1,744, p=2.2e-148)
 2. LIVER <-> PLASMA                                          70.3%  (n=1,456, p=2.9e-55)
 3. BAT <-> OVARY (female only)                               69.9%  (n=692,   p=3.0e-26)
 4. LUNG <-> OVARY (female only)                              69.8%  (n=364,   p=3.1e-14)
 5. HEART <-> SKM-GN                                          69.7%  (n=3,824, p=4.2e-135)
 6. LUNG <-> PLASMA                                           67.8%  (n=832,   p=4.7e-25)
 7. HEART <-> LUNG                                            66.8%  (n=2,024, p=1.9e-52)
 8. KIDNEY <-> SKM-GN                                         66.4%  (n=1,376, p=2.6e-34)
 9. KIDNEY <-> LUNG                                           66.2%  (n=1,424, p=1.3e-34)
10. KIDNEY <-> SKM-VL                                         66.0%  (n=256)
11. HEART <-> SKM-VL                                          65.3%  (n=976)
12. BLOOD <-> SPLEEN                                          65.1%  (n=2,704, p=6.3e-56)
13. LUNG <-> SKM-GN                                           64.3%  (n=1,464)
14. HEART <-> KIDNEY                                          64.1%  (n=1,592)
15. LIVER <-> SKM-GN                                          63.7%  (n=2,672)

MOST DISSIMILAR (significantly anti-concordant):
  BAT <-> SKM-VL  33.7% (n=1,568, p=1.8e-38);  BLOOD <-> HIPPOC 40.6%;  COLON <-> HIPPOC 42.4%;
  BAT <-> COLON 44.8% (n=3,400, p=1.4e-9);  COLON <-> SKM-VL 45.9%;  OVARY <-> SKM-VL 42.9%.

TISSUE-LEVEL SUMMARY ("hub" organs, mean similarity to all partners with >= 10 partners):
  PLASMA 0.324 > LUNG 0.262 > SKM-GN 0.243 > KIDNEY 0.241 > LIVER 0.229 > HEART 0.226 > SPLEEN 0.192 >
  SMLINT 0.172 > SKM-VL 0.161 > WAT-SC 0.148 > HIPPOC 0.139 > BAT 0.132 > BLOOD 0.124 > ADRNL 0.119 >
  COLON 0.072 (least coordinated).

DIRECT ANSWER
Endurance training elicits a coordinated but only moderately shared molecular response across organs: a
small mitochondrial/OXPHOS plus innate-immune core is regulated in many tissues and directional agreement
between any two organs averages ~56% (vs 50% by chance), but roughly half of all tissue pairs are
statistically indistinguishable from chance and the majority of regulated genes are tissue-exclusive. The
tissues with the most similar training responses are, in order:
 (1) the two hindlimb skeletal muscles, gastrocnemius and vastus lateralis - clearly the single most
     similar pair (80.0% concordance; Spearman r = 0.913 at 8w female / 0.879 at 8w male; 4.9x overlap
     enrichment; concordant in 8/8 assay-timepoint-sex strata; one of only 15/194 sex x pair combinations
     whose correlation increases monotonically with training duration, 0.587 -> 0.585 -> 0.869 -> 0.913 in
     females). Shared genes are the canonical muscle-adaptation module: Ckmt2 (mitochondrial creatine
     kinase), Mgst3, Adhfe1, Map7d2, Lgi3, Lamb3, Gpr88 up and Egr1, Prss46, Slc26a10, Megf10 down.
 (2) the striated-muscle/cardiac axis: HEART with SKM-GN (69.7%; supported by transcriptome 66.2%,
     proteome 75.6%, metabolome 67.8% and ATAC 52.6%) and with SKM-VL (65.3%).
 (3) the cardiopulmonary-renal axis: KIDNEY-LUNG (66.2%; the strongest pair in the proteome, 82.5%),
     HEART-LUNG (66.8%), HEART-KIDNEY (64.1%), KIDNEY-SKM-GN (66.4%), LUNG-SKM-GN (64.3%).
 (4) the immune axis BLOOD-SPLEEN (65.1%, n=2,704; r = 0.71 at 8w female; its transcriptome correlation
     rises monotonically 0.082 -> 0.105 -> 0.298 -> 0.710 over 1w->8w in females), sharing Icam4, Alox15,
     Fech, Gch1, Snca, Ska1, Tinagl1 (up) and Mertk (down).
 (5) the liver-plasma metabolite axis (70.3% in the metabolome).
Tissues whose responses are the LEAST like the rest are brown adipose tissue - which is not merely
uncorrelated but actively DISCORDANT with skeletal muscle (BAT-SKM-VL 33.7%; mitochondrial OXPHOS
transcripts Mt-cyb, Mt-atp6, Mt-nd1, Mt-co1/2/3, Mt-atp8, Mt-nd4l rise in muscle but fall in BAT, and
Fndc5/irisin is the reciprocal case) - and colon (mean similarity 0.072, erratic agreement across
timepoints).

CAVEATS
The supplied table contains only FDR-significant features, so (i) the reported correlation magnitudes are
inflated by selection and only the RANKING of tissue pairs should be trusted (the sign-based statistic used
for the main claims is not biased this way), (ii) tissue-to-tissue differences in statistical power affect
overlap counts, and (iii) the pooled binomial p-values reuse the same features across the four timepoints
and are therefore anti-conservative - the per-stratum consistency (8/8, 24/24, 28/32 strata) is the
conservative read-out. Assays have unequal tissue coverage (transcriptome 19 tissues, proteome/phospho 7,
acetylome 2), so only pairs supported by several assays can be called multi-omic. BAT-OVARY and LUNG-OVARY
rest on female-only strata; OVARY is female-only and TESTES male-only, and VENACV has no female 1w/2w data.
Bulk tissue data cannot separate cell-composition shifts from intracellular regulation, and no causal,
direction-of-effect or cell-type-resolved conclusion is possible from this table.
grader_notes: The agent correctly identifies coverage and training-regulated features, and handles coverage gaps well, but the core similarity metric departs from the required set-similarity approach and cross-assay aggregation is dominated by transcriptomics; interpretation is strong and well-sourced.

HEADLINE

RELT, DSG3, CFC1, ART3, CRTAC1, ITGAV, KLK13, COL15A1, MAPK4); 221 are breast-volume-only.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
INTERPRETATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. A shared epithelial/mucosal "surface proteome" module decreases with both traits. The 28 shared
   proteins are enriched for secreted products of stratified epithelium and exocrine/mucosal glands:
   cornified-envelope and keratinocyte-differentiation proteins (IVL/involucrin, CST6/cystatin M/E,
   PI3/elafin, SPINK5/LEKTI, KLK6, KLK13, DEFB4A/hBD-2, PGLYRP3, CA6, COL15A1) and mucosal/glandular
   secretory proteins (MUC1, CBLIF/intrinsic factor, PPY, VIT, ENDOU, DPEP1, PLB1, PSG1). Losing this
   signature as body fat rises and breast volume grows is consistent with the general plasma-proteome
   remodelling seen with adiposity change, plus estrogen-driven re-differentiation of breast/skin
   epithelium under feminizing GAHT.
2. LEP (leptin) is the single positive shared marker and the strongest fat-axis protein
   (percent-fat coefficient +0.196, adj.p = 5.46e-04). Leptin is secreted by adipocytes in proportion
   to fat mass and also acts as a mammary growth factor, so its parallel rise with breast volume
   supports the view that breast-volume gain in this setting is substantially adipose gain.
   LEP behaves as the internal positive control of the table.
3. The strongest breast-volume-only signals are gonadal/Leydig markers falling (INSL3, adj.p =
   3.32e-05 — the smallest adjusted p in the file; SPINT3, the largest negative coefficient;
   plus EDDM3B) alongside mammotropic/lactational proteins rising (PRL/prolactin, PAEP/glycodelin,
   CXCL13, CCL28, TNFAIP6, VEGFD). INSL3 is a constitutive Leydig-cell product whose fall mirrors
   suppression of the gonadal axis by antiandrogen + estrogen therapy; PRL and PAEP indicate an
   active mammotropic/gestagen-associated response. PAEP+PRL+CXCL13 partially resembles a
   gestational/lactational plasma signature — intriguing given the study's pregnancy comparator arm,
   but this table alone cannot test that.
4. Bone/ECM-Wnt signalling also tracks: SOST (sclerostin) and WIF1 fall with percent fat, SOST also
   with breast volume; MMP3 (stromelysin-1, involved in mammary remodelling/adipogenesis during
   involution) is among the strongest dual negatives.
5. Overlap statistics: vs 1.79 proteins expected by chance, 28 observed (Fisher OR = 63.6,
   p = 5.1e-30). Across all 5,278 proteins the two coefficient vectors correlate (Pearson r = 0.320,
   Spearman rho = 0.277); within the 259 hit-list union r = 0.721.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LIMITATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Only pre-computed coefficients and adjusted p-values are distributed (no participant-level NPX,
  no body-composition data, no regimen/timepoint/pregnancy labels): the mixed model cannot be
  refitted or verified, and CPA vs SPIRO, GAHT vs pregnancy-arm, and 6-month vs baseline contrasts
  cannot be tested here.
- No standard errors, confidence intervals or n are supplied; percent-fat and breast-volume
  coefficients are on different scales (median breast/fat ratio 0.028), so magnitude is comparable
  only within a trait.
- Associations, not causal or longitudinal effects: the model treats body composition as the
  predictor, adjusted for age and baseline BMI.
- Adjusted p < 0.05 is used as supplied (the table already contains a multiplicity floor value);
  Olink assays are correlated, so the effective number of independent discoveries is < 249.
- Olink readouts are affinity-based (PEA); epitope and protein-complex effects can influence NPX.
- No independent replication cohort was available in this workspace.
grader_notes: The analysis is strong in data parsing, significance filtering, integration, and interpretation, but effect-size ranking should have used absolute values to fully meet criterion 3.

QUESTION
Which genes show concordant dysregulation across all three levels — spinal cord
transcriptome, spinal cord proteome, and CSF proteome — in order to prioritise
non-invasive CSF biomarkers for ALS clinical trials?

SHORT ANSWER
Eleven genes are concordantly and significantly changed (all UP-regulated in ALS)
in the cervical spinal-cord transcriptome, the spinal-cord proteome, and the CSF
proteome:

    GPNMB, SERPINA3, LGALS3, HLA-DRA, CAPG, EMILIN1, AHNAK, FLNA, S100A11, ICAM1, SFN

Criteria applied (all must hold, ALS vs control):
  - present in all three datasets (transcriptome row; both proteomics tables);
  - same direction of change (sign of log2 fold change) at all three levels;
  - spinal cord RNA-seq: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR < 0.05;
  - spinal cord proteome: t-test p < 0.05;
  - CSF proteome: t-test p < 0.05.

THE ELEVEN GENES WITH THEIR NUMBERS (log2 fold change ALS vs control; p/FDR)
  1. GPNMB    RNA +2.65 (FDR 4.2e-16) | cord protein +0.95 (p 5.4e-06) | CSF +3.53 (p 1.3e-03)  [11.5x in CSF]
  2. SERPINA3 RNA +1.51 (FDR 2.4e-06) | cord protein +0.64 (p 9.5e-05) | CSF +1.59 (p 5.7e-03)
  3. LGALS3   RNA +1.36 (FDR 4.4e-12) | cord protein +0.49 (p 6.7e-03) | CSF +1.77 (p 2.9e-04)
  4. HLA-DRA  RNA +1.22 (FDR 5.1e-13) | cord protein +0.52 (p 4.8e-02) | CSF +1.34 (p 7.9e-05)
  5. CAPG     RNA +1.35 (FDR 9.0e-12) | cord protein +0.51 (p 1.0e-04) | CSF +1.09 (p 2.0e-04)
  6. EMILIN1  RNA +0.59 (FDR 1.7e-04) | cord protein +0.25 (p 4.7e-02) | CSF +1.85 (p 2.6e-02)
  7. AHNAK    RNA +0.32 (FDR 8.0e-03) | cord protein +0.46 (p 2.6e-02) | CSF +1.05 (p 1.8e-02)
  8. FLNA     RNA +0.34 (FDR 1.5e-02) | cord protein +0.46 (p 2.7e-03) | CSF +1.01 (p 5.0e-03)
  9. S100A11  RNA +1.03 (FDR 1.8e-09) | cord protein +0.45 (p 1.9e-02) | CSF +0.94 (p 1.4e-03)
 10. ICAM1    RNA +0.67 (FDR 2.3e-04) | cord protein +0.44 (p 1.7e-03) | CSF +0.93 (p 1.7e-02)
 11. SFN      RNA +1.57 (FDR 2.7e-04) | cord protein +0.42 (p 1.1e-02) | CSF +0.61 (p 6.3e-03)

HOW THE SET WAS DERIVED (coverage funnel)
  25,329 transcriptome symbols / 1,904 cord-proteome symbols / 297 CSF symbols
  -> 1,766 overlap RNA-seq x cord, 285 RNA-seq x CSF, 63 cord x CSF
  -> 59 genes measured at ALL THREE levels
  -> 38 of the 59 change in the same direction at all three levels
  -> 11 pass the full criterion above.
(The 3-step funnel 59 -> 38 -> 11 is the key number chain; the same-direction
count, 38/59, is itself greater than chance, binomial p = 0.006.)

MOST ROBUST CANDIDATES (survive stricter thresholds)
  - Applying a Benjamini-Hochberg FDR < 0.05 within the cord proteome as well
    leaves exactly two genes: GPNMB and SERPINA3. These are the only genes that
    survive every tier tested.
  - Requiring cord-proteome and CSF p < 0.01 leaves five: GPNMB, SERPINA3,
    LGALS3, CAPG, FLNA.
  - Priority ranking for CSF assay development: GPNMB >> SERPINA3 > LGALS3 ~ CAPG ~ HLA-DRA.

NEAR-MISSES / FOLLOW-UP LIST (concordant direction, RNA-seq FDR < 0.05, CSF p < 0.01,
but cord-proteome p between 0.05 and 0.25; all up in all three tables)
  ACTN1, LRP1, SOD2, GGT5, TAGLN2, S100A6, TPM3, VIM, HLA-DRB1, PSAP, DDAH1,
  CTSH, NPC2, PTPRC, PLXDC2, MTPN, ANTXR1, MYL6, RAB13, RCN1
  (Under direction-only concordance, 33 genes qualify; the extra ones include
   APOE, PSAP, PTPRC, NPC2, S100A6, VIM, LRP1, SOD2.)

BIOLOGICAL / CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
  - The concordant set is dominated by markers of activated microglia/macrophages
    and their lysosomal-phagocytic machinery (GPNMB, LGALS3, CAPG; with CTSH,
    PSAP, NPC2, HLA-DRB1 in the near-miss list) plus antigen presentation
    (HLA-DRA) and adhesion/cytoskeleton-ECM proteins (ICAM1, FLNA, AHNAK,
    EMILIN1, SFN, S100A11). This is consistent with the tissue-level conclusion
    that glial activation dominates the ALS spinal-cord transcriptome, and it
    means these CSF analytes read out a glial/neuroinflammatory tissue programme
    rather than motor-neuron loss per se.
  - GPNMB is the single strongest candidate: largest effect at every level
    (6.3x in tissue RNA, 1.9x in cord protein, 11.5x in CSF), genome-wide
    significant in the transcriptome, FDR-significant within the cord proteome,
    and top-ranked by combined evidence (Fisher p = 4.7e-25).
  - Clinically, GPNMB and SERPINA3 (alpha-1-antichymotrypsin) are the analytes
    most likely to be useful as non-invasive, mechanistically anchored readouts
    for ALS trials; LGALS3, CAPG and HLA-DRA are next, and the near-miss list
    (APOE, PSAP, PTPRC, S100A6, SOD2, LRP1, VIM) provides backups whose CSF
    changes are large but whose cord-proteome evidence is not yet significant.

EXPLICIT NON-CONCORDANT / UNMEASURABLE EXAMPLES
  - Neurofilaments (NEFH/NEFM/NEFL): strongly increased in the cord proteome and
    in the transcriptome trend, but DECREASED in the supplied CSF table
    (NEFM -0.77, p = 6.1e-03; NEFL -0.90, p = 3.8e-03) -> fail the same-sign rule.
  - Chitinases CHIT1 (+2.10, p = 1.3e-06), CHI3L1, CHI3L2 and UCHL1 are strongly
    increased in cord tissue but are ABSENT from the 292-protein CSF table, so
    their CSF concordance cannot be assessed from these data.

LIMITATIONS
  - The CSF table is a pre-filtered 292-protein list in which every protein
    already has p < 0.05 (max p = 0.0386); it is not a genome-wide CSF screen and
    its p-values are not FDR-controlled.
  - Only 59 genes could be evaluated at all three levels, so the 11-gene set is
    conditional on three-way measurement. Effect sizes are not comparable in
    magnitude across platforms (regression slope of protein log2FC on RNA-seq
    log2FC: 0.115 for cord, 1.289 for CSF), so only direction plus per-level
    significance is claimed.
  - Tissue is postmortem end-stage and cervical-only; CSF is antemortem, and the
    two cohorts are not demonstrably the same individuals. Concordance is
    therefore demonstrated at group level, not within subject, so these genes are
    surrogate candidates, not validated individual-level biomarkers.
  - No adjustment is possible for age, sex, postmortem delay, cell-type
    composition, genotype, or medication from pre-computed summary statistics.

Full analysis, code and intermediate counts are in trace.md; per-gene tables are
in three-level-concordance/output/tables/ and the figure is in
three-level-concordance/output/figures/concordance_three_levels.png.
grader_notes: The analysis is thorough and technically strong, with correct multi-modal integration and clear identification of top candidates, but it deviates from the rubric in CSF significance filtering, multi-gene entry handling, combined effect-size scoring, and the expected CHIT1 characterization.

FINAL ANSWER — Plasma proteome adaptations during feminizing GAHT (task da-13-1)

DATA AND ANALYSIS SET
Two files: Olink Explore HT NPX table (666,660 rows long format; 103 human SAMPLE
wells x 5,420 assays) and the 103-row SDRF metadata. After QC (drop 6 AssayQC-WARN
assays; drop 616 assays whose median antibody Count is < 100, i.e. near-background
readout) 4,798 assays were analysed. Design: 40 trans women with paired baseline and
6-month samples (20 CPA, 20 SPIRO). Timepoints were taken from the SampleID suffix,
validated against the NPX Group_Name1 column, because four SDRF phenotype labels
(AA31_0m, AA44_0m, AA36_6m, AA54_6m) contradict both. Tests: per-assay paired t-test
on the per-subject deltas (6m - baseline, log2 NPX), Benjamini-Hochberg FDR;
regimen question tested as a regimen x time interaction (Welch t-test on the CPA vs
SPIRO delta vectors, confirmed by a linear mixed model NPX ~ time*regimen + (1|subject)).

1) PROTEINS SIGNIFICANTLY ALTERED BY 6 MONTHS OF GAHT
581 of 4,798 assays (12.1%) change at FDR < 5% in the pooled paired analysis
(n = 40): 562 decrease, 19 increase. (At FDR < 1%: 339.)

Strongest decreases (Delta NPX, linear factor, FDR q):
  SPINT3  -7.91 (0.004)  q=2e-10   EDDM3B -1.99 (0.25) q=2e-10
  INSL3   -3.55 (0.086)  q=2e-9    TEX101 -1.49 (0.36) q=9e-8
  PROK1   -1.08 (0.47)   q=2e-13   ACRV1  -1.04 (0.49) q=8e-7
  MUC1    -1.03 (0.49)   q=1e-9    CA6    -0.76 (0.59) q=1e-9
  MSMB    -0.72 (0.61)   q=1e-9    PGLYRP3 -0.53 (0.69) q=5e-10
  VIT     -0.49 (0.71)   q=1e-9    MSTN   -0.49 (0.71) q=1e-7
  CST6    -0.44 (0.74)   q=2e-9    SPINK2 -0.44 (0.74) q=4e-8
  CA14    -0.42 (0.75)   q=2e-8    NCAM1  -0.47 (0.72) q=5e-8
  PLB1    -0.40 (0.76)   q=6e-8    DPEP1  -0.27 (0.83) q=1e-7
Other decreases include CCL24, SPINK5, CDON, ICAM4, CPA4, CLSTN2, CTHRC1, PI3,
DEFB4A_DEFB4B (-1.22), ANPEP, MME, BCHE, MYOC, CCL11/13/17, IGF1R, AXL, AOC3.

The complete list of the 19 increases (Delta NPX, q):
  LEP +1.27 (2e-7); PRL +0.79 (2e-5); CXCL13 +1.03 (3e-4); ASAH2 +0.30 (2.5e-3);
  MZB1 +0.19 (2.9e-3); SERPINA12 +0.72 (3.1e-3); VEGFD +0.20 (5.4e-3);
  NT-proBNP +0.64 (6.2e-3); PZP +0.40 (8.4e-3); SHBG +0.29 (8.4e-3);
  FOLR3 +0.21 (1.1e-2); LPL +0.39 (1.7e-2); TNFAIP6 +0.24 (1.9e-2); OXT +0.82
  (2.0e-2); CD70 +0.17 (2.1e-2); CCL28 +0.33 (2.9e-2); CST7 +0.30 (3.2e-2);
  PAEP +0.35 (3.7e-2); CSF3 +0.38 (4.2e-2).

Interpretation: the dominant change is loss of androgen-dependent
testis/epididymis/prostate secretory proteins (INSL3 = Leydig-cell marker; SPINT3
(HE3-beta) and EDDM3B (EP3) epididymis-specific; MSMB/PSP94 prostate; TEX101 and
ACRV1 testis/acrosome-specific), exactly as expected from gonadotropin suppression
plus androgen-receptor blockade. The up-regulated set is coherently
estrogen/progesterone-driven: SHBG (classic estradiol-induced hepatic globulin),
prolactin, PAEP/glycodelin, oxytocin, leptin, NT-proBNP (with estrogen-driven plasma
volume expansion), and the germinal-centre/B-cell markers CXCL13, MZB1, CD70.

Caveat that halves the headline number: a global sample-level offset of -0.124 NPX
(6m - baseline, paired p = 9.8e-5, identical in both arms) is present. After
median-centring each sample, 169 assays remain significant and 108 of the 581
survive. So ~100-170 proteins show robust protein-specific change; the remaining
~470 small (0.2-0.4 NPX) decreases are consistent with a shared dilutional
(plasma-volume expansion) or technical offset, which this dataset cannot separate.

2) DO THE CHANGES DIFFER BETWEEN CPA AND SPIRO?
Both arms move in the same direction, at different amplitudes:
  CPA arm   : 278 hits at FDR < 5% (265 down, 13 up)
  SPIRO arm : 133 hits at FDR < 5% (130 down, 3 up)
  55 proteins are significant in BOTH arms, all 55 in the same direction;
  223 are CPA-only and 78 SPIRO-only. Arm-level delta vectors correlate only weakly
  (Pearson r = 0.157; 64% sign agreement; SPIRO ~ 0.17 x CPA), but the strongest
  androgen-dependent proteins decrease substantially more under CPA: SPINT3 -7.91 vs
  -3.52; INSL3 -5.34 vs -1.75; EDDM3B -2.67 vs -1.32; TEX101 -2.08 vs -0.91.

Formal regimen x time interaction (FDR < 5%): 11 proteins.
  Protein  Delta_CPA  Delta_SPIRO  Difference(SPIRO-CPA)  q
  INSL3      -5.35      -1.75            +3.60           2e-5
  SPINT3     -7.91      -3.52            +4.39           4e-3
  PRL        +1.38      +0.19            -1.19           4e-5
  CXCL13     +1.84      +0.21            -1.63           4e-3
  CFC1       +0.57      -0.16            -0.73           4e-3
  NELL1      +0.21      -0.23            -0.43           4e-3
  SPOCK1     -0.34      -0.05            +0.29           1.7e-2
  EDDM3B     -2.67      -1.32            +1.35           2.9e-2
  RTBDN      -0.44      -0.02            +0.42           2.9e-2
  REN        -0.56      +0.19            +0.75           3.0e-2
  NOS3       +0.92      -0.13            -1.05           5.0e-2
DIRECTION: CPA produces larger reductions of the androgen-dependent reproductive
proteins (SPINT3, INSL3, EDDM3B) and larger increases in PRL, CXCL13, CFC1 and NOS3;
spironolactone produces a renin (REN) increase (consistent with
mineralocorticoid-receptor blockade activating the renin-angiotensin system).
This is pharmacologically coherent: cyproterone acetate is a potent
antigonadotropic/progestogenic antiandrogen, spironolactone a weaker AR antagonist.

Confidence grading (essential): regimen is perfectly confounded with measurement run
(CPA = run 1, SPIRO = run 2, no overlap). The AA17 subject, measured at both
timepoints in both runs, shows that an assay's within-subject delta reproduces only
weakly across runs (Pearson r = 0.065; 50.2% sign agreement overall; 57.8% among
FDR-significant assays; median |delta difference| = 0.63 NPX).
- Robust candidates: the large directional differences, SPINT3, INSL3, EDDM3B
  (|difference| 1.3-4.4 NPX, well above the ~0.6 NPX bridge noise) and PRL, CXCL13
  (~1.2-1.6 NPX).
- Not trustworthy: the sub-1 NPX interaction hits (SPOCK1, RTBDN, NELL1, CFC1, REN,
  NOS3; SPOCK1 even changes sign between runs). Notably NOS3, which estradiol would
  be expected to increase, rises only in the CPA/run-1 arm - a pattern at least as
  consistent with a run effect as with a drug effect.
These differences therefore require confirmation in a design where both regimens are
measured in the same run.

3) WHAT CANNOT BE CONCLUDED
Regimen-specific effects below ~1 NPX are not separable from run effects; the global
-0.124 NPX offset cannot be attributed to dilution versus normalization artefact;
no dose, formulation, estradiol/testosterone, age or BMI data are provided; there is
no untreated trans control arm (the cisgender longitudinal samples are n = 1 each);
and 622 assays excluded by QC (including APOE, APP) are uninformative here. NPX is a
relative scale, so fold-changes are relative, not absolute concentrations.

Secondary comparator (for context): pregnancy trimester 3 vs pre-GAHT baseline
differ in 1,319 assays (801 up, 518 down; led by CSH1, INSL4, TFPI2, FLT1, RLN1,
ADAM12). 275 of the 581 GAHT hits are also pregnancy-significant and 180 in the same
direction; 12 of the 19 GAHT-up proteins rise in pregnancy too. The GAHT
up-regulated arm thus partly overlaps a physiological high-estrogen/progesterone
state, whereas the large down-regulated component is specific to androgen deprivation.

Full details, code, intermediate counts, sensitivity analyses and references:
trace.md and the module proteomics-gaht/ (README plus scripts 01-06 and result tables).
grader_notes: The agent meets all rubric criteria at the A level with rigorous data handling, paired statistical testing with multiple testing correction, accurate identification and comparison of significant proteins, thorough biological interpretation, and reliable sourcing.

SYNTHETIC-LETHAL PARTNERS FOR LOSS-OF-FUNCTION EVENTS IN BRCA
================================================================

WHAT WAS DONE
-------------
Cohort / data used (all from the provided files):
 * BRCA cell-line cohort with damaging/LoF calls: 128 mutation-matrix rows = 74 unique
   DepMap models (71 BRCA lines), 19,616 genes, ternary LoF encoding (0/1/2).
 * Measured DepMap CRISPR dependency for 36 of those 74 lines (18,119 genes) -> the only
   cohort where LoF status and real dependency are both available.
 * CCLE expression for 56 of the 74 (188 lines overall across 3 lineages) -> independent,
   better-powered expression-anchored test of the same hypothesis.
 * TCGA: 1,099 BRCA patients x 1,966 model-predicted dependency genes (plus 1,100 lung and
   173 leukaemia patients as reference).
 * Priors: Ensembl release 116 paralogues, STRING v12 interactions (score >= 700).
Methods: (1) mutation-anchored one-sided Mann-Whitney U + Cliff's delta with BH-FDR (n=36);
(2) LassoCV linking LoF features to dependency for all 18,119 genes + 100x bootstrap
stability selection; (3) expression-anchored partial-correlation screen, lineage- and
proliferation-residualised (n=188), plus a matching LassoCV model; (4) one-sided Fisher
mutual-exclusivity tests over all recurrent LoF pairs (74 models); (5) paralogue/PPI priors;
(6) integration into a weighted evidence score, then ranking by translational relevance.

Important data caveat: the "BRCA_damaging_mut.csv" file is a CELL-LINE matrix
(ACH-/CDS- identifiers), not a TCGA patient matrix; it cannot be joined to the TCGA barcodes
(no candidate key yields more than coincidental overlap: 0/128, 0/128, 3/128 and 35/128 matches by SequencingID, ModelID, metadata row index and numeric value). Patient-level mutation-conditional testing is
therefore impossible with these files, and all mutation-anchored statistics come from the
36 lines that have measured dependency.

Ranking statistics: in the mutation-anchored scan (199,199 tests) NO pair survives FDR
(smallest q = 0.61); the expression-anchored scan (226,369 tests) yields 43 pairs at q<0.05;
no mutual-exclusivity pair is significant (min p = 0.014). The ranking below therefore rests
on convergent, direction-consistent evidence across layers plus prior/translational
annotation, not on a single genome-wide-significant test.

RANKED CANDIDATES (by translational relevance)
----------------------------------------------
1. BRCA1/BRCA2 LoF  ->  PARP1 / PARP2                       [TIER 1 - approved drugs]
   Evidence: BRCA1 mutation-anchored delta_median = -0.169, Cliff's d = -0.53, p = 0.044
   (n=4 of 36); expression-anchored r = +0.137, p = 0.030; lasso stability 0.60.
   STRING BRCA1-PARP1 0.974, BRCA2-PARP1 0.985. BRCA2 has only 3 carriers (no power).
   Translation: olaparib/talazoparib, FDA-approved for BRCA1/2-mutated breast cancer
   (OlympiAD PMID 28578601; OlympiA PMID 34081848). Caveat: PARP inhibitors work largely by
   trapping PARP on DNA, so CRISPR PARP1 dependency under-reports this SL (PMID 23118055).

2. CDKN2A / 9p21 LoF ->  PRMT5 (and its obligate partner WDR77/MEP50)   [TIER 1 - phase 1/2]
   Evidence: expression-anchored r = +0.351, p = 3.9e-07, q = 0.0034 (PRMT5);
   WDR77 r = +0.365, q = 0.0022. Mutation layer not testable (5 carriers, wrong direction
   n.s.). Mechanism: CDKN2A is co-deleted with the adjacent MTAP at 9p21; MTAP loss causes
   MTA accumulation and PRMT5 dependence. Translation: MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors
   AMG 193 and MRTX1719 (phase 1/2), biomarker = MTAP deletion (PMIDs 26912361, 26912360,
   27068473, 37552839, 40146197). This is the best-powered novel finding in the dataset.

3. CDH1 (E-cadherin) LoF ->  PTK2/FAK + ITGAV, FERMT2, BCAR1, VCL, ELMO2
   (focal-adhesion module)                                  [TIER 1 - phase 1/2]
   Evidence: expression-anchored; CDH1-low accounts for 32 of the 43 FDR-significant pairs,
   and functional enrichment of those 32 partners (STRING v12) is dominated by adhesion
   terms (WP185 integrin-mediated cell adhesion FDR 1.2e-05; KEGG focal adhesion FDR 0.0028;
   KEGG regulation of actin cytoskeleton FDR 0.0028; GO:0007229 integrin-mediated signalling
   FDR 0.0044). The strongest partners: ITGAV r = +0.459 (q = 2.2e-07), ELMO2 r = +0.455
   (q = 2.2e-07), FERMT2 r = +0.381 (q = 1.5e-04), BCAR1 r = +0.342 (q = 0.0022),
   PTK2 r = +0.336 (q = 0.0029), VCL r = +0.295 (q = 0.018). Independent convergence in the
   mutation layer:
   PTEN-mutant lines are also more dependent on PTK2 (p = 0.011), FERMT2 (p = 0.0022),
   ITGAV (p = 0.0069) and BCAR1 (p = 0.0098). STRING CDH1-VCL 0.996, PTEN-PTK2 0.995.
   Translation: FAK inhibitors defactinib (NCI-MATCH, PMID 39693587), IN10018, GSK2256098;
   anti-integrin alphaV antibodies. CDH1 LoF defines the lobular/EMT-like breast cancer
   subset (~10% of cases).

4. PTEN LoF ->  PIK3CB                                        [TIER 1 - phase 1/2]
   Evidence: mutation-anchored delta_median = -0.395, Cliff's d = -0.83, p = 7.3e-04
   (the strongest non-TP53 mutation-layer signal), lasso stability 1.00 (coef -0.58),
   STRING PTEN-PIK3CB 0.984. Translation: PI3K-beta-selective AZD8186 / GSK2636771;
   replicates the classic PTEN-loss -> PI3K-beta dependence (PMID 18755892).

5. CDKN2A LoF  ->  CDK6 / CDK4                                [TIER 1 - approved drugs]
   Evidence: expression-anchored r = +0.300, p = 1.5e-05, q = 0.049; STRING 0.999.
   Translation: palbociclib/ribociclib/abemaciclib (approved; PALOMA-2 PMID 27959613) -
   the canonical p16-loss -> CDK4/6 dependence.

6. ATM LoF  ->  ATR                                           [TIER 2 - phase 2]
   Evidence: Ensembl paralogue ATM->ATR, STRING 0.999. No statistical power here
   (1 carrier among 74 models; expression layer r = +0.02). Translation: ceralasertib,
   berzosertib, elimusertib; ATM-deficiency is the validated biomarker (PMID 21490603,
   30971826).

7. NF1 LoF  ->  AXL                                           [TIER 2 - phase 1/2]
   Evidence: convergent mutation-anchored (delta_median = -0.194, Cliff's d = -0.90,
   p = 7.4e-04, n=5) and expression-anchored (r = +0.240, p = 4e-04) signal;
   lasso stability 0.83. No STRING edge -> hypothesis-level. Translation: bemcentinib and
   other AXL inhibitors (phase 1/2).

8. TP53 LoF  ->  GPX4                                         [TIER 3 - preclinical]
   Evidence: largest effect size in the mutation scan (delta_median = -0.603,
   Cliff's d = -0.52, p = 0.010, n = 27 vs 9), lasso stability 1.00 (coef -0.50),
   patient-level rho = +0.233 (q = 1.8e-14). Mechanism: p53-dependent redox/lipid-
   peroxidation control and ferroptosis. Translation: RSL3/IKE-class ferroptosis inducers
   (preclinical; PMIDs 25799988, 24439385, 29088702). TP53 LoF is the most frequent event
   (74% of the cohort), but note that most other TP53-partner hits (TUBA1B, MOB4, PPP1R7)
   are pan-essential/proliferation genes with no therapeutic window.

9. ARID1A LoF  ->  ARID1B (paralogue)                         [TIER 3 - preclinical]
   Evidence: Ensembl paralogue, STRING 0.999, mutation-anchored delta_median = -0.310,
   Cliff's d = -0.58, p = 0.051 (n = 3), lasso stability 0.67; expression layer weak
   (r = +0.03). Canonical paralogue-buffering SL (PMID 24562383); no ARID1B drug yet.

10. BRCA1 LoF  ->  XRCC1 / LIG3 (BER-SSBR axis)               [TIER 3 - preclinical]
   Evidence: XRCC1 delta_median = -0.590, Cliff's d = -0.75, p = 0.0078; LIG3
   delta_median = -0.220, Cliff's d = -0.77, p = 0.0068, lasso stability 0.95
   (coef -0.42); expression layer LIG3 r = +0.138, p = 0.030. No clinical XRCC1/LIG3
   inhibitor yet; mechanistically the "PARP-like" single-strand-break-repair bypass.

11. BRCA2/BRCA1 LoF ->  POLQ, RAD52                           [TIER 3 - literature-driven]
   No support from either cell-line layer (POLQ delta_median -0.05 to -0.15, n.s.;
   RAD52 n.s.); STRING BRCA2-POLQ 0.804. Listed because POLQ inhibitors (ART558/ART6043,
   novobiocin) are in clinical trials in DDR-deficient tumours (PMID 34140467) and
   RAD52 is the classic BRCA2 SL (PMID 21148102) - these need more carriers to be assessed.

Secondary, data-supported partners (lower translational priority): BRCA1 -> RBBP8/CtIP
(p = 0.010, d = -0.72, STRING 0.999, no drug), BRCA1 -> RFC2 (p = 0.0033, d = -0.84),
BRCA1 -> AUNIP (patient rho = 0.29), BRCA1 -> CHEK1/ATR (STRING 0.996; CHEK1/ATR inhibitors
exist), PTEN -> FERMT2/ITGAV/BCAR1/PTK2 (same focal-adhesion module as CDH1), ARID1A -> CDK12
(p = 0.058 mutation, p = 0.019 expression), ARID1A -> PARP2 (p = 0.016), CDKN2A -> RBL1
(q = 0.049), TP53 -> CTPS1 (patient rho = 0.54), TP53 -> MRE11/NBN/RAD52 (p = 0.010-0.018,
lasso stability 0.7-0.9).

WHAT THE ANALYSIS CANNOT CONCLUDE
---------------------------------
* No pair reaches genome-wide significance in the mutation-anchored layer (min q = 0.61):
  with 36 lines and 3-9 carriers per event, only TP53 (27 carriers) is even moderately
  powered. The expression- and patient-level layers are better powered but test proxies
  (mRNA level; model-predicted dependency), not the mutation itself.
* The mutation matrix is cell-line based, so the requested patient-level
  mutation-conditional analysis is not possible; the TCGA layer contributes only
  translational denominators and a mutation-free surrogate (predicted dependency on the
  driver).
* Mutual exclusivity is uninformative in this cohort (0/990 pairs significant).
* Prediction is not proof of drug sensitivity: no drug-response data are present, and the
  PARP1 case shows explicitly that a CRISPR dependency score can miss a clinically validated
  synthetic lethality. All Tier 1-3 entries are hypotheses requiring prospective validation
  (e.g. MTAP/PRMT5 and CDH1/FAK should first be tested in isogenic models).
grader_notes: The agent's work shows strong data handling and source documentation, but fails to fully meet some criteria: lasso used CV but lacked FDR on coefficients, mutual exclusivity was not used for prioritization, no permutation testing, paralogs without similarity filter, and canonical BRCA paralog pairs not reported.

DA-1-3 — Compartment distribution of cell subsets and cell types specific to the tumour microenvironment (GSE236581 CRC anti-PD-1 cohort, 975,275 cells, 169 samples, 22 patients)

DATA AND METHOD IN BRIEF
- 975,275 cells x 36,027 genes; cell-level annotation from GSE236581_CRC-ICB_metadata.txt (6 major cell types, 91 subcell types; Tissue = Tumor 279,886 / Normal 260,294 / Blood 417,162, plus 11,353 LN and 6,580 TN cells that were excluded).
- Barcodes were verified to be in the same order as the metadata rows before joining. Statistics use the patient (n=22, all with tumour + adjacent normal + blood) as the unit of replication: per-sample proportions were averaged per patient and compared with paired one-sided Wilcoxon tests (BH-FDR across 91 subsets). Enrichment is quantified as Ro/e (observed/expected under the chi-square independence model); a subset is called compartment-restricted when Ro/e >= 2 in one compartment and < 1 in both others.
- Raw UMI counts were streamed once (1,310,816,895 non-zeros = header value) to obtain library-size QC and pseudobulk CPM per (Tissue x SubCellType) group, and to validate all candidates with canonical marker genes.

DISTRIBUTION ACROSS THE THREE COMPARTMENTS
- Peripheral blood (417,162 cells, 56 samples): T cells 63.3% (mean per-patient %), myeloid 13.9%, ILC 10.6%, B 10.3%, epithelium 1.4%, stroma 0.6%. 26 subsets are blood-restricted (94-99% of their cells in blood), i.e. naive/central-memory CD4 and CD8 T cells (c01_CD4_Tn_CCR7, c02_CD4_Tn_SELL, c15_CD8_Tn_CCR7, c17_CD8_Tcm_GPR183), monocytes (c49_Mono_CD14, c50_Mono_FCGR3A), c35_ILC_FCGR3A, c24_CD8_Temra_CX3CR1, c31_DNT, naive/memory B cells (c39_NaiveB_TCL1A, c41_MemB_CD27), MAIT c26, gdT c30, DCs (c54_pDC_LILRA4, c58_cDC_CD1C, c56_tDC_SIGLEC6) and c32_DPT.
- Adjacent normal tissue (260,294 cells, 52 samples): epithelium 38.6%, T 27.0%, B 23.1%, stroma 8.4%, myeloid 1.9%, ILC 1.0%. 7 subsets are normal-restricted: normal colonocytes (c86_Coloncyte_BEST4, Ro/e 3.03), tuft cells (c89_Tuft_PTGS1, 2.74), normal fibroblasts (c73_Fibro_ADAMDEC1, 2.73; c76_Fibro_PI16, 2.64), germinal-centre B cells (c43_GCB_LRMP, 2.62), IgA2 plasma cells (c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1, 2.60; the largest non-T/B population, 66,437 cells, 70.7% in normal) and enteric glia (c83_Glia_PLP1, 2.58).
- Tumour (279,886 cells, 58 samples): T 40.3%, epithelium 29.6%, B 16.3%, stroma 6.8%, myeloid 5.2%, ILC 1.8% - the only compartment containing all six lineages in quantity. 22 subsets are tumour-restricted by Ro/e, 36 are shared and 29 are depleted (Ro/e <= 0.7).

CELL TYPES SPECIFICALLY AND HIGHLY ENRICHED ONLY IN THE TUMOUR MICROENVIRONMENT
Criterion: Ro/e_Tumour >= 2, >= 50% of the subset's cells recovered from tumour, >= 5-fold higher median per-patient proportion than the higher off-tumour compartment, BH-FDR q < 0.05 in paired Wilcoxon tests versus BOTH adjacent normal and blood, detected in >= 11/22 patients. 13 subsets pass; the top 7 have >= 92% of their cells in tumour, 0-6 cells in blood, and Ro/e 3.17-3.38:

1. c79_Fibro_FAP - FAP+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (COL1A1, COL1A2, FAP, THBS2, MMP1/11/13, POSTN, INHBA). 2,807/2,841 cells in tumour (98.8%), ZERO in blood, 21/22 patients, Ro/e 3.38.
2. c64_Mph_SPP1 - SPP1+ immunosuppressive macrophages (SPP1, MMP9, CXCL5, INHBA, TREM2, VEGFA). 983/999 cells (98.4%), 3 in blood, 21/22, Ro/e 3.37 (highest in the pre-treatment-only analysis, 3.75).
3. c70_Endo_COL4A1 - tumour endothelium (COL4A1, VWF, PLVAP, ESM1, APLNR, PCDH17, EGFL7). 2,442/2,513 cells (97.2%), 3 in blood, 22/22, Ro/e 3.32.
4. c71_Endo_MKI67 - proliferating tumour endothelium (MKI67 62.6% and TOP2A 49.7% expressing vs 33.3%/16.7% in normal). 171/177 cells (96.6%), none in blood, 18/22, Ro/e 3.30.
5. c09_CD4_Th1_CXCL13_HAVCR2 - CXCL13+ CD4 Th1/Tfh-like cells (CXCL13 5,621 CPM, PDCD1, HAVCR2, IFNG, CTLA4, IL21). 3,265/3,391 cells (96.3%), 3 in blood, 22/22, Ro/e 3.29.
6. c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN - terminally exhausted, tumour-reactive CD8 T cells (CXCL13, LAYN, PDCD1, HAVCR2, ENTPD1, TOX, TNFRSF9, CXCR6). 11,455/12,005 cells (95.4%), 14 in blood, 22/22, Ro/e 3.26.
7. c63_Mph_CCL20 - inflammatory CCL20+ macrophages (IL1B, CCL20, IL1A, CXCL8, EREG, ACOD1). 1,002/1,080 cells (92.8%), 6 in blood, 20/22, Ro/e 3.17.

Tumour-dominant but with a reproducible 12-22% minority in adjacent normal (82-88% of cells in tumour, <=0.34% in blood, still highly enriched only relative to blood):
8. c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9 - activated/4-1BB+ Tregs (FOXP3, IL2RA, CTLA4, TNFRSF4, TNFRSF9, CCR8); 87.9% in tumour, median 2.91% of tumour cells vs 0.36% of normal cells (8x), 22/22, Ro/e 3.01.
9. c55_pDC_GZMB - GZMB+ plasmacytoid DCs (LILRA4, CLEC4C, IL3RA, IRF7); 87.3% in tumour, Ro/e 2.99.
10. c07_CD4_Th17_CTSH - Th17 cells (IL17F, IL26, RORC, CCR6, CCR4); 84.9% in tumour, Ro/e 2.90.
11. c60_cDC_LAMP3 - LAMP3+/mregDC state with IDO1 and CD274/PD-L1 (CCL19, CCL22, CCL17, CCR7, FSCN1); 82.3% in tumour, Ro/e 2.81.
12. c91_Epi_Tumor - malignant epithelium (CEACAM5, KRT8/18, TACSTD2, LGR5, DPEP1, ETV4, SERPINB5); 21,377 cells, 81.8% in tumour, Ro/e 2.80.
13. c62_Mph_S100A8 - S100A8/A9+ inflammatory macrophages (IL1B, IL1RN, CXCL10, TREM1); 81.6% in tumour, Ro/e 2.79.

Rare but tumour-restricted (median per-patient proportion 0 in all compartments, so judged on pooled ratios): c53_Neu_CXCR2 (tumour-associated neutrophils; 91.5% of cells in tumour, 15.0x pooled fold, 16/22 patients), c80_Fibro_MKI67 (proliferating CAF; 84.8%, 5.5x, 16/22), c27_CD8_MAIT_SLC4A10 (78.7%, 3.5x, 22/22), c47_PlasmaB_IGHG1 (78.2%, 3.5x, 22/22), c81_Pericyte_RGS5 (77.1%, 3.2x, 22/22).

SUMMARY ANSWER
The subsets specifically and highly enriched only in the tumour microenvironment form three coherent programmes: (i) tumour stroma and vasculature - FAP+ CAFs, MKI67+ CAFs, SPP1+ macrophages, CCL20+ and S100A8+ macrophages, COL4A1+/PLVAP+/ESM1+ and MKI67+ tumour endothelium, RGS5+ pericytes, CXCR2+ neutrophils; (ii) tumour-reactive/exhausted lymphocytes - LAYN+CXCL13+PDCD1+HAVCR2+TOX+ exhausted CD8 T cells, CXCL13+HAVCR2+ CD4 Th1 cells, TNFRSF9+CCR8+ activated Tregs, CTSH+IL17F+ Th17 cells, SLC4A10+ MAIT cells, IGHG1+ plasma cells, LAMP3+ mregDC, GZMB+ pDC; and (iii) malignant epithelium (c91_Epi_Tumor). These 13 subsets are 5- to 75-fold over-represented in tumour relative to their expected abundance (Ro/e 2.8-3.4) and 4- to 75-fold more abundant than in the higher off-tumour compartment, statistically significant against both adjacent normal and blood (q < 0.05, paired Wilcoxon on 22 patients), reproducible across patients (18-22 of 22), and essentially undetectable in peripheral blood (<=0.6% of their cells). The same result holds when only pre-treatment cells are used, so it reflects the tumour microenvironment rather than therapy. Converse patterns define the other compartments: blood is dominated by naive/central-memory T cells and monocytes (26 blood-restricted subsets), and adjacent normal by normal colonocytes, tuft cells, ADAMDEC1+ fibroblasts, IgA2 plasma cells, germinal-centre B cells and enteric glia (7 normal-restricted subsets).

Marker-level confirmation: in tumour versus blood pseudobulk, CXCL13 is 1,039x higher, SPP1 403x, COL4A1 352x, CCL20 129x, FAP 114x, LAYN 41x, TNFRSF9 22x, IDO1 18x - whereas the cytotoxic gene GZMB is higher in blood (786 vs 417 CPM), as expected for circulating cytotoxic cells.

LIMITATIONS
Cell-type labels are the authors' annotation (no re-clustering), so results are conditional on it - notably the c91_Epi_Tumor label also captures 4,684 cells from adjacent-normal samples (1.8% of normal cells). Enrichment is a statement about cell-state frequency, not about genes being induced in tumour (e.g. FOXP3 and LAYN CPM are similar within c13/c23 in tumour versus normal). Blood contains only 0-25 cells of most candidate subsets, so "absent from blood" rests mainly on the composition analysis. Response associations are exploratory (12 CR, 7 PR, 3 SD, 0 PD; only c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN differs, 3.8% vs 0.33% of tumour cells, p = 0.0052). One biopsy per compartment per time point, and no spatial, TCR or covariate (MSI/MSS, regimen, stage) modelling was performed.

Key output files (working directory): trace.md (full analysis trace with code); analysis/01-composition/output/tables/subcelltype_tissue_enrichment_stats.csv, subcelltype_compartment_assignment.csv, tumor_specific_candidates.csv, tumor_specific_candidates_tierB_rare.csv; analysis/02-marker-validation/output/tables/marker_panel_by_tissue.csv, cluster_top_markers.csv, tme_marker_tissue_expression.csv; figures analysis/01-composition/output/figures/fig1_compartment_landscape.png, fig2_Roe_heatmap.png, analysis/02-marker-validation/output/figures/fig3_tme_marker_expression.png.
grader_notes: The analysis is rigorous overall with correct tissue filtering, valid Ro/e enrichment, strict specificity filtering, and thorough biological annotation, but it falls short of full marks on baseline filtering and translational therapeutic implications.

ANSWER: Circulating immune cell populations with significantly altered frequencies in SLE
=========================================================================================

Cohort analysed: 1,263,676 PBMCs from 261 donors in the supplied CELLxGENE h5ad
(162 SLE vs 99 healthy controls). Unit of replication = donor. Primary test = quasi-binomial
(binomial GLM with Pearson-dispersion correction) on each donor's count of a population out of
that donor's total cells, adjusted for age, sex, self-reported ancestry, processing cohort and
sequencing depth; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 5% across the 11 populations.

FIVE POPULATIONS ARE SIGNIFICANTLY ALTERED (5 of 11)
----------------------------------------------------

DECREASED in SLE
1. CD4+ T cells (T4)
   median 23.2% (SLE) vs 37.4% (HC) of PBMCs  ->  -14.2 percentage points
   OR 0.560 (95% CI 0.490-0.639), p = 1.1e-17, FDR q = 1.2e-16; AUC 0.824
   Driven by a collapse of naive CD4 T cells (49.3% vs 75.1% of CD4, OR 0.398, q = 2.3e-27) with
   expansion of effector-memory CD4 (36.3% vs 18.7%, OR 2.171) and regulatory T cells
   (13.1% vs 6.4%, OR 2.040).

2. Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDC)
   median 0.246% vs 0.510%  ->  -0.26 pp
   OR 0.640 (0.530-0.772), p = 3.3e-06, q = 9.2e-06; AUC 0.747 (inverted)

INCREASED in SLE
3. Classical monocytes (cM)
   median 26.4% vs 17.7%  ->  +8.7 pp
   OR 1.910 (1.604-2.275), p = 3.9e-13, q = 2.1e-12; AUC 0.784

4. Non-classical monocytes (ncM)
   median 3.91% vs 2.83%  ->  +1.08 pp
   OR 1.367 (1.127-1.658), p = 1.5e-03, q = 3.3e-03; AUC 0.653

5. Proliferating lymphocytes (Prolif; MKI67+)
   median 0.636% vs 0.362%  ->  +0.27 pp
   OR 2.207 (1.673-2.912), p = 2.1e-08, q = 7.7e-08; AUC 0.725

POPULATIONS NOT SIGNIFICANTLY ALTERED (6 of 11)
-----------------------------------------------
- CD8+ T cells (T8): +1.3 pp, OR 1.145 (0.980-1.338), q = 0.16
- NK cells: essentially unchanged (6.66% vs 6.68%), q = 0.24
- Conventional dendritic cells (cDC): -0.28 pp, q = 0.52
- B cells: -1.4 pp, q = 0.52
- Plasmablasts (PB): q = 0.90
- Haematopoietic progenitors (Progen): q = 0.38

ADDITIONAL SUB-STATE FINDINGS (finer lymphoid states, % of parent compartment, 255 donors)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Nine of 13 fine states differ at FDR 5%, most notably:
- MAIT cells (T_mait): 1.76% vs 9.26% of CD8 T cells, OR 0.272, q = 1.8e-14 (largest proportional
  loss in the dataset)
- Cytotoxic GZMH+ CD8 T cells: 38.3% vs 22.0% of CD8, OR 1.930, q = 3.8e-06
- Naive CD8 T cells: 26.3% vs 36.6% of CD8, OR 0.707, q = 0.017
- Memory B cells (B_mem): 22.1% vs 38.1% of B cells, OR 0.510, q = 3.5e-07
- Naive B cells: 71.0% vs 60.2% of B, OR 1.774, q = 2.2e-05
- Atypical B cells (B_atypical): 2.74% vs 1.79% of B, OR 1.658, q = 0.025
- NK subsets unchanged (q = 0.26)
Net pattern: loss of naive/memory compartments with expansion of activated effector and
regulatory compartments across CD4, CD8 and B lineages.

VALIDATION
----------
- Direction reproduced in all 8 alternative specifications (no cohort term, no depth term,
  cohort 2+3+4 only, donors with >=1,000 cells, sample-level with donor-clustered SEs,
  one sample per donor, Aitchison CLR with the same covariates, unadjusted logit) for all five
  populations; sign also reproduced within each of processing cohorts 2, 3 and 4.
- Annotation-free check using only raw transcript counts (no cell-type labels): CD4 CCR7+SELL+
  fraction SLE/HC ratio 0.68, per-cell CCR7 ratio 0.65, CD8 GZMH+ fraction ratio 1.56
  (adjusted p = 7.3e-05, q = 5.9e-04), CD8 CCR7+SELL+ ratio 0.79, CD8 GZMK+ ratio 0.89,
  CD4 GZMH/GZMK+ ratio 1.11 — the same directions as the label-based analysis.

DIAGNOSTIC VALUE
----------------
Best single-population discriminators (univariate AUC): T4 0.824, cM 0.784, pDC 0.747 (inverted),
Prolif 0.725, ncM 0.653. A cross-validated (5-fold) logistic model combining all 11 fractions plus
age and sex reaches AUC 0.921 (SD 0.042) versus 0.670 (SD 0.098) for age + sex alone.

LIMITATIONS
-----------
Cross-sectional case-control data; no longitudinal or external validation cohort, so the AUC is a
within-cohort upper bound, not a validated diagnostic accuracy. SLE donors are older (median 41 vs
32 years) and more often of Asian ancestry (51% vs 24%), and one processing cohort contains only
controls; these were adjusted for and results were replicated under reduced models and per cohort,
but residual confounding (and medication/activity status, which the metadata does not record
cleanly) cannot be excluded — the pDC effect size in particular is covariate-sensitive (OR 0.498
with age+sex only vs 0.640 in the full model). Frequencies are compositional, so the five findings
are not independent biomarkers and absolute cell counts per microlitre are unavailable. All results
depend on the curated CELLxGENE cell-type labels for the monocyte/DC and fine lymphoid states,
although the CD4/CD8 shifts were independently reproduced from raw marker transcripts. Rare
populations (Progen, plasmablasts) have unstable estimates and are not claimed as biomarkers.
grader_notes: The agent performed a rigorous donor-level analysis with proper statistics and correction, but only found 5 of the 8 expected significantly altered cell types, missing T8, B, and PB, so Criterion 5 is rated B. All other criteria are strong.

ANSWER: In post-hormonal-therapy HR+/HER2- breast tumors, ESR1 mutations and MAPK-pathway alterations
are NOT co-occurring. They are significantly NEGATIVELY associated - i.e. they tend toward mutual
exclusivity - and the two events largely define alternative, non-overlapping routes to endocrine
resistance.

COHORT
Analysis set = samples whose sequenced tumor is HR_STATUS = Positive and OVERALL_HER2_STATUS = Negative
(1,362 of 1,918 samples) and whose SAMPLE_SITE is not "Treatment Naive Primary":
705 samples from 656 patients (629 metastases, 40 post-treatment primaries, 36 post-neoadjuvant
primaries). ESR1 is mutated in 131/705 (18.6%); MAPK core (RTK-RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK + ERBB2, non-silent
mutation) is altered in 110/705 (15.6%).

PRIMARY RESULT (MAPK = mutation of KRAS/NRAS/HRAS/BRAF/RAF1/ARAF/MAP2K1/MAP2K2/MAPK1/MAPK3/NF1/RASA1/
SOS1/SHOC2/SPRED1/PTPN11/CBL/RIT1/RRAS2/RRAS/MAPKAP1/DUSP4 + ERBB2)
                      MAPK-altered   MAPK-wild-type   total   MAPK-altered %
  ESR1-mutant              7              124          131        5.3%
  ESR1-wild-type         103              471          574       17.9%
  total                  110              595          705       15.6%

  - 7 double-altered observed vs 20.4 expected under independence
  - odds ratio 0.26 (95% CI 0.12-0.57)
  - Fisher exact two-sided p = 1.5e-4; one-sided mutual-exclusivity p = 8.1e-5;
    one-sided co-occurrence p = 0.99998
  - 10,000-permutation test: p < 1e-4 (0/10,000 permutations had <= 7 double-altered samples)
  - patient-level union (656 patients): 7 double-altered vs 19.4 expected, OR 0.27 (0.12-0.61), p = 3.2e-4
  - site-stratified Mantel-Haenszel OR (11 biopsy-site strata) 0.246 (0.123-0.494), so biopsy-site mix
    does not explain the association
  - logistic regression adjusted for mutational burden: MAPK-alteration OR 0.15 (0.058-0.37), p = 4.3e-5;
    the effect is not a consequence of ESR1-mutant tumors being more mutated (they are modestly more
    mutated: mean 6.24 vs 5.26 non-silent calls, and the adjusted OR is stronger, not weaker)

ANSWER TO THE DIRECTIONAL QUESTION: mutual exclusivity, not co-occurrence. The co-occurrence
alternative is rejected (one-sided p = 0.99998).

MAGNITUDE AND ROBUSTNESS - the exclusivity is relative, not absolute
  - 7 double-altered tumors exist (ESR1 p.D538G + NF1 mutation, ESR1 p.E380Q + NF1 mutation,
    ESR1 p.L536Q + ERBB2 mutation, ESR1 p.D538G + HRAS+SOS1 mutation, ESR1 p.E380Q + MAP2K1 mutation,
    ESR1 p.D538G + RAF1 mutation, ESR1 p.N532K + RASA1 mutation), so this is not strict mutual
    exclusivity.
  - The effect is definition-dependent: it is strongest and most significant for MUTATIONALLY altered
    MAPK genes and weakens when MAPK copy-number events are counted:
      * core + ERBB2, mutations only:                                 OR 0.26, p = 1.5e-4
      * core + ERBB2, mutations + CNA of the same genes (17 co-altered): OR 0.50 (0.29-0.87), p = 0.012
      * core + ERBB2, mutations + broad RTK/JNK CNA set (37 co-altered): OR 0.59 (0.39-0.90), p = 0.013
      * core + RTK (EGFR/ERBB3/ERBB4/FGFR1-4/MET...):                 OR 0.72 (0.46-1.13), p = 0.16
      * core + RTK + JNK/p38 (MAP3K1/MAP2K4/MAP3K13) + CNA:           OR 0.83 (0.57-1.21), p = 0.33
      * ERBB2 + NF1 only:                                             OR 0.17 (0.05-0.56), p = 3.4e-4
    At patient level with CNA included the depletion is still significant (17 double-altered vs 26.0
    expected, OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.31-0.94, p = 0.027). The broad CNA-inclusive signal is itself dominated
    by copy-number events outside the ERK core: 20 of the 37 co-altered samples under that rule are
    flagged only by FGFR1 amplification (11q13 amplicon) or ERBB3 amplification or MAP2K4 deep deletion.
    So the statistically robust statement is that ESR1 mutation is depleted among tumors with
    mutationally activated MAPK pathway (ERBB2, NF1, RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK), not among tumors with MAPK
    copy-number gains/losses.

SPECIFICITY AND DIRECTIONAL CONTROLS
  - PIK3CA (OR 0.90, p = 0.62) and AKT1 (OR 0.93, p = 1.00) show NO association with ESR1, so the
    depletion is specific to the MAPK module rather than a generic property of ESR1-mutant tumors.
  - TP53 is negatively associated (OR 0.36, p = 3.8e-5, BH q = 0.003), consistent with the luminal,
    p53-wild-type phenotype of ESR1-mutant disease.
  - Per-gene tests (43 genes, BH-FDR): ERBB2 OR 0.11 (p = 0.003, q = 0.070) and NF1 OR 0.21 (p = 0.013,
    q = 0.198) are the only MAPK genes showing depletion; no MAPK gene shows significant co-occurrence
    (largest nominal co-occurrence signal is NTRK1, OR 4.5, p = 0.023, q = 0.26, n = 5, not robust).
  - Exposure control: ESR1 mutation is rare in treatment-naive HR+/HER2- primaries (9/657 = 1.4%) versus
    18.6% post-hormonal (Fisher p = 1.1e-29) and 13.2% in post-treatment/post-neoadjuvant primaries,
    confirming the expected acquired-resistance behaviour and that the naive/non-naive split tracks
    therapy exposure. In treatment-naive tumors no double-altered samples were observed at all
    (0 vs 0.7 expected, p = 1.0).
  - ESR1 variants are canonical resistance mutations: 136/138 non-silent calls lie in the ligand-binding
    domain (positions 310-547), dominated by p.D538G (53), p.Y537S (29), p.E380Q (13), p.Y537N (10),
    p.Y537C (10), p.L536H (4).

BIOLOGICAL / CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
ESR1 ligand-binding-domain mutation (constitutive, ligand-independent ER activity) and ERK-pathway
reactivation (ERBB2 or NF1 mutation, RAS/RAF/MEK alteration, MAPK amplification) appear to be
substituting rather than cooperating mechanisms of endocrine resistance. The typical post-hormonal
HR+/HER2- tumor acquires one dominant resistance route: ESR1-mutant tumors are usually ERK-pathway
wild-type, and MAPK-altered tumors (especially ERBB2-mutant, NF1-mutant/deleted and RAS-RAF-MEK-altered)
are usually ESR1-wild-type. Clinically this argues that ESR1 genotype is informative about the
probability of a MAPK-pathway alteration and vice versa, and that ER-directed strategies
(aromatase inhibitor, fulvestrant, elacestrant) and ERK/MAPK-directed strategies (e.g. HER2-mutant
inhibitors, MEK inhibitors) target largely disjoint molecular populations in this setting.

LIMITATIONS - what this analysis cannot conclude
  1. MSK-IMPACT panel covers only 474 genes; MAP2K3, MAP2K6, MAPK7, DUSP6, SPRY2 and other MAPK
     modifiers are absent, so MAPK-pathway alteration frequency is a lower bound and some true
     co-alteration could be missed.
  2. Only bulk DNA was analysed. No RNA, phospho-ERK or functional data confirm that a counted
     alteration activates ERK; single-copy gains were deliberately not counted, which is why the
     mutation-only and mutation+CNA conclusions differ in strength. Non-genetic ERK activation cannot
     be detected.
  3. Therapy exposure is a proxy: SAMPLE_SITE separates treatment-naive primaries from everything else
     and does not record prior lines, agents (tamoxifen/AI/fulvestrant/CDK4/6 inhibitor) or duration.
     A site-stratified Mantel-Haenszel analysis (MH OR 0.25) rules out biopsy-site mix as the driver,
     but unmeasured exposure heterogeneity remains possible.
  4. Power: only ERBB2 (38 mutated) and NF1 (37) have enough events for individual-gene testing; most
     MAPK genes have <= 5 events, so a co-occurrence signal in a rare MAPK gene would be missed.
  5. The provided clinical table contains no response or survival endpoints, so nothing can be said about
     whether exclusivity versus co-alteration predicts benefit from ER-directed versus MAPK-directed
     therapy.
  6. Cross-sectional design: 705 mostly single biopsies from 656 patients, not paired pre/post-therapy
     samples from the same tumors.
grader_notes: The agent performs a robust and well-documented analysis but falls short of full marks on cohort selection, ESR1 mutation definition, and MAPK alteration definition because it does not strictly restrict to LBD ESR1 mutations, omits specified MAPK copy-number events in the primary analysis, and includes non-metastatic post-treatment primary samples.

ANSWER — DA-1-4: correlation between tumour regression ratio and baseline cell-subtype proportion
=============================================================================================

SHORT ANSWER
------------
The correlation is subtype-specific in sign; there is no single global sign for "cell subtypes".
Patients whose baseline (pre-treatment) TUMOUR already contained a large tumour-reactive /
exhausted CD8 T-cell compartment - and, together with it, activated Tregs - went on to regress
more deeply, so for those subtypes the correlation with the tumour regression ratio (TRR) is
POSITIVE. Patients whose baseline tumour was dominated by differentiated normal colonic
epithelium (goblet/colonocyte subtypes) regressed less, so for those subtypes the correlation is
NEGATIVE. Across all 71 subtypes tested the signs are balanced (37 positive, 34 negative;
median rho = +0.015, sign-test p = 0.81), i.e. most subtypes show no reliable correlation; the
signal is confined to the immune-vs-epithelium axis of the tumour microenvironment.

KEY NUMBERS (22 patients, 105,959 baseline tumour cells, Spearman rho across patients)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
POSITIVE (better regression with higher baseline proportion):
  c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN (exhausted CD8 T; LAYN/PDCD1/CXCL13/HAVCR2/TOX/ENTPD1-high)
        rho = +0.506, p = 0.016 (BH q = 0.41), permutation p = 0.017
        CR/PR median 2.09% vs SD median 0.13% of tumour cells (Mann-Whitney p = 0.021)
  c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9 (activated Treg; FOXP3/IL2RA/CTLA4/TNFRSF9-high)
        rho = +0.470, p = 0.027; CR/PR 2.76% vs SD 1.26% (p = 0.053)
  c20_CD8_Tem_GZMK  rho = +0.310 (p = 0.16);  c61_Mph_FCGR3A  rho = +0.355 (p = 0.10)
NEGATIVE (worse regression with higher baseline proportion):
  c87_Goblet_MUC2 (normal goblet; MUC2/TFF3-high)  rho = -0.464, p = 0.030
        CR/PR median 2.27% vs SD 9.50% (p = 0.069)
  c84_Coloncyte_CA2 (normal colonocyte) rho = -0.351 (p = 0.11); c86_Coloncyte_BEST4 -0.243;
  c45_PlasmaB_TXNDC5 -0.353 (p = 0.11); c77_Fibro_ACTA2 -0.294

ANNOTATION-FREE CONFIRMATION from the raw UMI counts (58 marker genes re-extracted from the
19 GB matrix; per-gene sums matched a full independent scan exactly):
  baseline fraction CD8A+CXCL13+ (tumour-reactive CD8)  rho = +0.596, p = 0.003 (perm p = 0.004)
  fraction of CD8A+ cells that are CXCL13+              rho = +0.549, p = 0.008
  fraction CD8A+ of tumour cells                        rho = +0.453, p = 0.034
  exhaustion module score (LAYN/PDCD1/CXCL13/HAVCR2/TOX/ENTPD1)  rho = +0.439, p = 0.041
  e.g. P11 (TRR 1.00) 53.7% of CD8A+ cells CXCL13+; P09 (0.916) 29.1%; P20 (0.434) 22.2%;
       P21 (0.701) 23.4%; versus P17 (TRR 0.072) 0% and P25 (TRR -0.026) 0%.

ROBUSTNESS
  - Leave-one-out: CD8 Tex rho in [+0.43, +0.56] (positive in 22/22 fits); Goblet rho in
    [-0.57, -0.39] (0/22 positive) - not driven by any single patient.
  - Sign stable for prevalence cut-offs 0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9/1.0 of patients.
  - Sign stable for alternative denominators: within immune cells only (Tex rho +0.501,
    p = 0.018), all baseline tissues pooled (+0.513), no signal in baseline BLOOD
    (all p > 0.08).
  - Not explained by MSI status: TRR does not differ MSI vs MSS (p = 0.69); rank partial
    correlation controlling for MSI: CD8 Tex +0.506 (p = 0.016), Treg +0.463 (p = 0.030),
    Goblet -0.466 (p = 0.029), CD8A+CXCL13+ fraction +0.594 (p = 0.0035).
  - CAVEAT: with n = 22 no subtype survives Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (minimum q = 0.41); the
    associations are nominal and the study is powered only for |rho| >~ 0.5.

WHAT THIS IMPLIES
-----------------
1. Depth of tumour regression under anti-PD-1 is largely pre-determined by the immune state of the
   tumour BEFORE treatment. A pre-existing CXCL13+ (tumour-antigen-reactive), LAYN+/PDCD1+/TOX+
   exhausted CD8 population at baseline is the strongest correlate of a deep regression; therapy
   amplifies existing immunity rather than creating it de novo. This mirrors the classic
   "pre-existing intratumoural CD8 infiltration predicts PD-1 blockade response" result
   (Tumeh et al., Nature 2014) and the CXCL13+ CD8 definition of tumour-reactive T cells
   (Zheng et al., Science 2021; Thommen et al., Nat Med 2018).
2. The accompanying POSITIVE correlation of activated (TNFRSF9/4-1BB+) Tregs is not contradictory:
   in an inflamed "hot" tumour, activated CD8 effectors and activated Tregs expand together, so
   baseline Treg abundance is best read as a marker of an ongoing antigen-driven immune reaction
   (and of a co-opted counter-regulatory brake), not as a simple immunosuppressive brake. It also
   warns that a bulk Treg/CD8 ratio is a poor single biomarker, and that Treg-depleting strategies
   remove a compartment that co-marks the responsive tumours.
3. The NEGATIVE correlations for normal epithelial subtypes (goblet/colonocyte) have a strong
   compositional component: because proportions sum to 1, an immune-rich (low-epithelium) tumour
   mechanically shows low epithelial fractions, so the negative sign is largely the mirror image of
   the positive immune one. A direct biological reading (mucus/goblet-rich, differentiated, possibly
   CMS1-like tumours are less immunogenic) is plausible but not demonstrated by this analysis.
4. Practically: the predictive information sits in the TUMOUR tissue (no baseline blood subtype
   correlated with TRR), and a single measure - the baseline CD8A+CXCL13+ fraction of tumour cells -
   already separates deep regressors from non-regressors. This supports tissue-based,
   baseline-immune-composition biomarkers for anti-PD-1 patient selection.

LIMITATIONS
-----------
n = 22 patients with one baseline tumour sample each (powered only for |rho| >~ 0.5; nothing
survives FDR); association is not causation; proportions are compositional so immune-positive and
epithelium-negative results are partly two views of one axis; MSI status (16 MSI / 6 MSS) and
treatment regimen (pembrolizumab vs sintilimab+CapeOx, the latter contributing direct cytotoxic
shrinkage) cannot be fully adjusted for; sub-cell-type labels are the authors' transferred
annotations (validated here by marker genes but not error-free - e.g. the normal-mucosa
c87_Goblet_MUC2 population appears inside "tumour" biopsies); the validation-cohort sheet has no
regression ratio or single-cell data and could not be used; one clinical inconsistency was noted
(P12 is labelled CR but has TRR = 0.009).
grader_notes: The agent delivered a rigorous baseline tumor composition analysis with proper filtering, normalization, correlation testing, robustness checks, and source attribution. The main weakness is omission of some expected top negative subtypes, but the overall workflow meets most full-score criteria.

QUESTION
To map RUNX1 genomic targets that mediate AI-10-49 therapeutic effects, how does RUNX1 chromatin
occupancy change upon CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition?

SHORT ANSWER
CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition with AI-10-49 sharply INCREASES RUNX1 chromatin occupancy in ME-1 inv(16) cells
(1,329 DMSO RUNX1 peaks -> 9,169 AI-10-49 peaks, 6.9x; genomic footprint 0.33 -> 3.18 Mb, 9.7x). The
change is overwhelmingly a gain of new sites (7,950 new = 86.7% of the AI set) with almost no loss (97
sites = 7.3% of the DMSO set; gained:lost = 82:1). 1,232 of the 1,329 DMSO sites (92.7%) are retained,
and at those retained loci occupancy is also stronger (median MACS2 fold enrichment 5.5 -> 12.6, median
-log10 q 12.5 -> 48.2; Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 2.9e-191; stronger at 1,149/1,232 = 93.3% of loci).
The new RUNX1 sites are promoter-biased (34.9% within 2 kb of a TSS vs 25.6% of pre-existing sites,
Fisher p = 8.0e-7; 2,773 promoter-proximal new sites across 2,543 genes) and they land in chromatin that
is already H3K27ac-active in both conditions (93.2% inside the H3K27ac union; 94.1% of those in
constitutively shared regions; 113.6 new RUNX1 peaks per Mb vs 16.5 pre-existing), while the total number
of H3K27ac regions is essentially unchanged (57,828 DMSO -> 56,299 AI-10-49, -2.6%). RUNX1 occupancy is
therefore relocalised/expanded onto pre-existing active promoter-enhancer elements rather than RUNX1
being displaced, and this is not a genome-wide chromatin-opening event.

KEY NUMBERS
- RUNX1 peaks: DMSO 1,329; AI-10-49 9,169 (6.90x). DMSO 0.329 Mb vs AI 3.179 Mb of genome (9.66x).
  Median peak width 222 -> 295 bp; median fold enrichment (FE) 5.42 -> 7.21; median -log10 q 12.19 -> 15.69.
- Site classes: shared 1,232 (92.7% of DMSO set; 13.3% of AI set); DMSO-specific ("lost") 97 (7.3%);
  AI-specific ("gained") 7,950 (86.7%). At >=50% reciprocal overlap: 720 sites shared (54.2% of DMSO
  peaks, 7.9% of AI peaks) - i.e. the conclusion is not threshold-dependent.
- Strength: lost sites median FE 5.15 (n=97) < pre-existing 5.48 (n=1,232) < gained 6.85 (n=7,950) <
  shared sites measured in AI-10-49 12.53 (n=1,219). Gained sites are STRONGER than the lost ones
  (Mann-Whitney p = 1.7e-18) and stronger than the pre-existing ones (p = 3.2e-88): the new sites are not
  marginal calls.
- The DMSO vs AI gap widens with stringency, so it is not a threshold/sensitivity artefact:
  FE>=3: 1,311 vs 9,132 (7.0x); FE>=5: 813 vs 7,533 (9.3x); FE>=8: 175 vs 3,837 (21.9x);
  FE>=10: 65 vs 2,549 (39.2x); FE>=15: 2 vs 1,018 (509x); FE>=20: 0 vs 457.
  Rank-matched control (top 1,329 AI peaks by MACS2 score) recovers only 609 of the pre-existing sites
  (45.8%), i.e. the pre-existing set is enriched but nowhere near saturated among the new calls.
- Genomic distribution: promoter (<=2 kb of a GENCODE19 protein-coding TSS) 25.1% of DMSO peaks vs 33.6%
  of AI peaks; among classes, gained 34.9% promoter vs pre-existing 25.6% (Fisher OR = 1.39, p = 8.0e-7)
  and vs lost 23.7% (OR = 1.47, p = 0.115).
- H3K27ac context: 80.2% of DMSO RUNX1 peaks and 84.8% of AI RUNX1 peaks overlap H3K27ac (39.4x and 47.4x
  over the 2.04%/1.79% of genome covered by the respective H3K27ac sets). Merged H3K27ac union = 63,665
  regions / 71.5 Mb (shared 61.4 Mb, DMSO-only 6.51 Mb, AI-only 3.62 Mb). New RUNX1 density: 113.6
  peaks/Mb in shared, 51.9 in DMSO-only, 26.6 in AI-only; pre-existing: 16.5 / 12.7 / 2.8.
- Gene coverage: DMSO peaks map to 1,116 nearest genes, AI peaks to 5,567 (union 5,625); 4,501 genes gain
  a RUNX1 peak with none in DMSO; only 51 genes lose their sole DMSO RUNX1 peak.

NEW / INTENSIFIED RUNX1 TARGETS (hg19; FE = MACS2 fold enrichment)
- MYC locus (chr8): DMSO has 1 RUNX1 peak in chr8:128.4-129.1 Mb
  (chr8:128,929,798-128,930,015, FE 5.2). AI-10-49 has 4, including a NEW site 56 bp from the MYC TSS
  (chr8:128,747,329-128,747,624, FE 4.11) and a 3.1x intensified, 3.6x wider version of the downstream
  element (chr8:128,929,569-128,930,348, FE 16.35, -log10 q = 108). The MYC promoter H3K27ac peak is
  present in both conditions but mildly reduced in AI-10-49 (DMSO chr8:128,746,429-128,752,167, 5,738 bp,
  -log10 q 178 -> AI 5,351 bp, -log10 q 77). Occupancy at the MYC promoter therefore increases while
  promoter acetylation does not, consistent with AI-10-49 disrupting MYC chromatin dynamics.
- Strongest new sites and their nearest genes: SYTL3 (chr6:159,070,548-159,071,198, FE 38.4, promoter),
  PLAUR/uPAR (chr19:44,174,053-44,174,634, FE 35.3, 65 bp from TSS), IL21 (FE 35.1), RREB1 (FE 34.95),
  ABHD17C (FE 34.2), SPTBN1 (FE 33.5), GGA1 (FE 33.1, promoter), DIAPH1 (FE 33.1, promoter),
  KLF10 (chr8:103,665,830-103,667,049, FE 32.0, 1.1 kb from TSS), FOSL2 (FE 32.4), ACSF3 (FE 32.7).
- Other gained, promoter-proximal targets relevant to inv(16)/myeloid biology: CEBPA (new peak at TSS,
  FE 2.9 -> 4.3), CSF1R (3 peaks, max FE 25.5), BIRC3 (FE 21.1 at TSS), MALT1 (FE 23.4 at TSS),
  BCL2 (3 peaks up to FE 8.3, TSS-proximal), E2F3 (FE 21.1 at TSS), CDKN1A/p21 (FE 10.8),
  TRIB1 (FE 15.7 at TSS), ITGA2B (FE 10.4 at TSS), MPO (FE 6.2 at TSS), MYB (FE 3.7 -> 10.3),
  FOS (FE 5.9 -> 21.6 at TSS). The RUNX1 locus itself intensifies (4 -> 17 peaks within +/-10 kb,
  max FE 7.2 -> 25.2), as does CBFB (FE 7.5 -> 12.3).
- Genes with the most gained peaks: AL356215.1 (13), MCTP2 (10), ABHD17C (7), SPRY2 (7), FOSL2 (6),
  KMT2E (6), SPTBN1 (6), SYTL3/SGK1/INHBA/PPCDC (5 each).

INTERPRETATION
1. The inv(16) fusion behaves as a RUNX1-sequestering lesion: removing the fusion's CBFβ interaction with
   AI-10-49 releases RUNX1 onto DNA. Retained sites are kept (92.7%) and intensified (2.2x median FE),
   while the majority of the RUNX1 repertoire (7,950 sites) becomes newly occupied - the opposite of
   RUNX1 displacement.
2. Recruitment is to already-active, promoter-proximal regulatory elements, not to newly opened
   chromatin: 93.2% of the new sites lie inside the H3K27ac union, 34.9% are within 2 kb of a TSS
   (significantly enriched vs pre-existing sites), and the number of H3K27ac regions does not change.
   This matches the normal haematopoietic paradigm in which RUNX1 co-occupies active enhancers/promoters
   with C/EBPα, PU.1 and GATA2, rather than acting as a chromatin-opening pioneer.
3. The gained target set is functionally coherent with an anti-leukemic, differentiation/apoptosis-like
   programme: restoration of myeloid maturation genes (CEBPA, CSF1R, ITGA2B, MPO, TRIB1), cell-cycle
   arrest (CDKN1A, E2F3), and apoptotic/NF-κB regulation (BCL2, BCL2L14, BIRC3, MALT1), plus new RUNX1
   occupancy at the MYC promoter and intensification of the MYC downstream element.

LIMITATIONS (what this cannot conclude)
- Only ONE ChIP replicate and one input per condition: no reproducibility or variance estimate, hence no
  valid differential-binding test. The reported p-values are geometric/descriptive tests on peak-set
  membership and strength within these two libraries, not a replicated statistical result.
- No BAM/bigWig/signal files were provided, so absolute occupancy, FRiP, read depth under peaks and IP
  efficiency cannot be measured. Matching each library to its own input controls for background, and the
  threshold-matched/rank-matched analyses plus the paired 2.2x intensification at retained loci argue
  against a purely technical explanation, but a difference in IP efficiency or sequencing depth between
  the two libraries cannot be formally excluded.
- RNA-seq and ATAC-seq files named in the task brief are NOT present in this workspace, so the
  transcriptional direction of any target (activation vs repression) and chromatin accessibility changes
  could not be assessed; RUNX1 occupancy alone does not indicate direction.
- No motif/sequence or blacklist data: direct RUNX1 binding cannot be separated from co-occupancy by
  another factor, and artefact regions in the MACS2 calls cannot be excluded.
- Enhancer-gene links are distance-based (nearest protein-coding TSS, one gene per peak); 25.9% of peaks
  are >50 kb from any TSS and effectively unassigned, and no Hi-C/contact data was available.
- Single active compound, no dose series or inactive analogue, so the change cannot be formally
  attributed to CBFβ-SMMHC engagement specifically rather than an off-target effect of AI-10-49, and the
  result comes from the ME-1 cell line only, not from primary inv(16) patient blasts.
grader_notes: The agent correctly selected RUNX1 data, produced robust mechanistic interpretation, and grounded numbers and citations reliably. However, differential occupancy used intersect rather than merge, the unchanged cluster count was not explicitly reported, and feature enrichment omitted required exon/intron/intergenic annotation and precedence.
