DA-14-1 — Which sepsis endotyping signatures cluster together based on their
score correlations across patients?

SHORT ANSWER
Across 3,948 patient samples (27 non-redundant continuous signature scores,
Spearman correlation, signed distance d = (1 - rho)/2, average-linkage
hierarchical clustering), the endotyping signatures resolve into ONE dominant
bipolar axis plus TWO quasi-orthogonal axes. The primary partition (k = 4, the
eigenvalue criterion giving 4 eigenvalues > 1 and the best silhouette for k >= 3)
contains these clusters:

CLUSTER 1 — Adaptive / lymphoid-protective (anti-inflammatory) pole (n = 6 scores)
  mars3_score, adaptive_score, yao_IA_score, protective_score, mod4_score,
  lymphoid_protective_score
  mean within-cluster rho = +0.78 (min +0.57); mean rho to all other scores = -0.43

CLUSTER 4 — Myeloid-detrimental / inflammatory (high-dysfunction, high-SRS) pole
(n = 13 scores)
  coagulopathic_score, myeloid_score, mod2_score, detrimental_score,
  myeloid_detrimental_score, lymphoid_score, davenport_SRSq, cano_SRSq,
  som_score, inflammopathic_score, mod1_score, yao_IN_score, mars2_score
  mean within-cluster rho = +0.62 (min +0.16); mean rho to all other scores = -0.19

CLUSTER 2 — Myeloid-protective / neutrophil-monocyte axis (n = 6 scores)
  mod3_score, monocyte_protective_score, myeloid_protective_score,
  neutrophil_protective_score, mars4_score, wong_score
  mean within-cluster rho = +0.45 (min +0.12); mean rho to all other scores = +0.03

CLUSTER 3 — Interferon-like / IC axis (n = 2 scores)
  yao_IC_score, mars1_score  (rho = +0.76 with each other)
  mean rho to all other scores = -0.06

MACRO-STRUCTURE (k = 2, the global silhouette maximum, 0.540)
The score set is dominated by one bipolar axis: cluster 1 (adaptive /
lymphoid-protective: adaptive, yao_IA, mars3, protective, mod4,
lymphoid_protective) versus all remaining 21 scores (the inflammatory /
myeloid-detrimental pole and its two orthogonal satellites). The mean rho between
clusters 1 and 4 is -0.63, reaching -0.96 for mod4_score vs lymphoid_score and
-0.87 for som_score vs adaptive_score.

KEY PAIRWISE CORRELATIONS (Spearman, all 6 cohorts agree in sign)
  lymphoid_protective_score - lymphoid_score      -1.000  (a mirrored pair)
  mod4_score - lymphoid_score                     -0.962
  detrimental_score - myeloid_detrimental_score   +0.943
  davenport_SRSq - cano_SRSq                      +0.922
  myeloid_detrimental_score - myeloid_score       +0.900
  monocyte_protective_score - myeloid_protective_score +0.893
  mod4_score - protective_score                   +0.875
  som_score - adaptive_score                      -0.865
  lymphoid_score - cano_SRSq / davenport_SRSq     +0.865 / +0.861
  adaptive_score - yao_IA_score                   +0.856
  yao_IC_score - mars1_score                      +0.757
  wong_score - neutrophil_protective_score        +0.595

INTERPRETATION
- Clusters 1 and 4 are the two poles of a single dominant inflammation /
  immune-dysregulation axis, which carries almost all of the clinical signal.
  Its cluster-4 module index is 0.561 SD higher in patients who died within 30
  days, correlates +0.438 with SOFA and +0.534 with ordinal severity, and is
  +0.74 in Davenport SRS1 versus -0.93 in SRS3 (and +0.75 in Sweeney
  inflammopathic versus -0.60 in adaptive). Cluster 1 has the mirror-image
  (protective) clinical relationship: -0.610 mortality delta, -0.475 with SOFA.
  Both poles therefore describe the same biology read from opposite ends:
  Sweeney inflammopathic/coagulopathic, Davenport/Cano SRSq, yao_IN and mars2
  (cluster 4) versus Sweeney adaptive, yao_IA, mars3 and the lymphoid-protective
  / mod4 subspace (cluster 1).
- Cluster 2 is a genuinely separate axis (mean cross-rho ~ 0): the
  myeloid-protective / neutrophil-monocyte compartment, joined by wong_score and
  mars4_score. With cluster 3 it captures myeloid maturation/resolution
  biology rather than the mortality axis.
- Cluster 3 (yao_IC_score + mars1_score) is small, internally tight
  (rho = 0.757) and almost uncorrelated with everything else; it is invisible to
  outcome-driven analyses because neither score is strongly outcome-associated on
  its own (rho with SOFA +0.058 and +0.233). The varimax factor solution shows
  this IC axis in anti-phase with the myeloid-protective/mod3 dimension
  (F4: mod3 +0.86, yao_IC -0.73, mars4 +0.67, mars1 -0.63).

CAVEATS (stated in detail in trace.md)
- Sign is part of cluster identity: lymphoid_score = -lymphoid_protective_score
  (rho = -1.000) and mod4 ~ -protective, so a cluster must be read as a
  directed module. Using an unsigned 1 - |rho| distance merges the two poles and
  gives a materially different partition (ARI 0.484 vs the reported one).
- Stability: 500 bootstrap resamples give mean ARI 0.886 (min 0.703); baseline
  only and one-sample-per-patient reproduce the partition exactly (ARI 1.000);
  infected-only ARI 0.883; cohort-partial correlation ARI 0.904; dropping the
  mirrored trio ARI 0.861; Pearson ARI 0.703. Cluster 2 is the loosest
  (bootstrap co-clustering 0.723; wong_score is the weakest member, 0.414).
- 135 of the 148 pairs with |rho| > 0.5 keep their sign in all six cohorts with
  n >= 150; yao_IA_score links are the least reproducible across cohorts.
- Correlations are cross-sectional and partly inflated by shared derivation
  genes; the supplied table lacks the raw expression of the 104 signature genes,
  so gene sharing could not be adjusted for. Clustering is of scores, not of
  patients, so no patient-level endotype assignment is claimed.
grader_notes: The agent performed a thorough and technically correct correlation-clustering analysis with appropriate stability checks, transparent parameter choices, cautious biological interpretation, and clear limitation acknowledgment, meeting the highest level on all criteria.

QUESTION: Are GAHT-induced protein changes consistent with those observed during
menopause or menopausal hormone therapy (MHT)?

SHORT ANSWER
Partly, and in opposite directions depending on which comparator you mean.
GAHT-induced protein changes ARE consistent with menopausal hormone therapy
(exogenous estrogen): among proteins significant for both, 80-92% change in the
same direction. GAHT-induced changes are NOT consistent with natural menopause:
the same proteins are hit (222 of 258 GAHT hits are also menopause-associated)
but they move in the OPPOSITE direction (only 10.4% same sign). The GAHT plasma
proteome signature therefore looks like an estradiol-high / androgen-low state,
which is the mirror image of the hypo-estrogenic, hyper-gonadotropic state of
natural menopause.

DATA AND METHOD
Two pre-computed per-protein mixed-linear-model tables (Olink Explore-HT NPX,
random intercept per participant, adjusted for age and baseline BMI):
 - Supplementary Table 1 (5,279 proteins x 7 cols): CPA-GAHT and SPIRO-GAHT
   baseline vs 6 months (n = 20 paired participants per arm). Real header is on
   row 5, not row 2 as the brief stated. 0 missing values.
 - Supplementary Table 7 (2,922 proteins x 22 cols): MHT, menopause,
   hysterectomy, oophorectomy and ln(estradiol)/ln(testosterone) models,
   age-stratified at 57 years. Real header is on row 4. 0 missing values.
Shared universe = 2,791 proteins (131 Table-7 proteins have no GAHT model).
The `GAHT_proteins` flag was verified against Table 1: perfectly diagonal, 0
discrepancies. GAHT hit set = 258 proteins (212 CPA-significant, 80
SPIRO-significant, 34 both; 244/258 move DOWN with a global mean shift of
-0.130 NPX). A single GAHT effect was defined as the mean of the CPA and SPIRO
coefficients, justified by the arms' agreement (100% same sign among the 34
concordant hits; 91% among CPA-significant proteins). Concordance was assessed
two ways - hit-set overlap (Fisher exact / odds ratio) and signed directional
agreement against a 20,000-permutation null that preserves each term's marginal
sign distribution - because the naive 50% baseline is invalid when 94.6% of
GAHT hits are negative.

RESULTS (shared 2,791-protein universe; "same sign" = among proteins
significant in BOTH the term and GAHT, fraction matching the GAHT sign)

  Term                   n sig   overlap   same sign   expected   perm. p
  MHT >= 57 y             475      117     108 (92.3%)   75.1%     0.0032
  Hysterectomy            313       63      58 (92.1%)   47.0%    <0.0001
  ln estradiol (women)    533      119     101 (84.9%)   67.6%     0.0047
  MHT < 57 y              674      141     113 (80.1%)   53.8%    <0.0001
  Oophorectomy            353       73      50 (68.5%)   55.4%     0.12
  ln testosterone (men)  1,576     180      68 (37.8%)   66.1%    <0.0001
  ln testosterone (wom.)   663      114      32 (28.1%)   37.7%     0.11
  Menopause < 57 y       1,282     222      23 (10.4%)   19.3%     0.0051
  Menopause >= 57 y          3       2       2            -          -
  ln estradiol (men)         0       0       -            -          -

1. CONSISTENT WITH MHT. Shared hits agree in sign at 92.3% (MHT >= 57 y;
   Fisher OR 5.04, p = 1.7e-29) and 80.1% (MHT < 57 y; OR 4.52, p = 9.6e-29),
   each far above the marginal-matched expectation. Effect-size rank
   correlation within significant proteins is Spearman rho = +0.36 (p = 2.7e-16)
   and +0.12 (p = 0.0012). Robust across both antiandrogen arms separately
   (CPA 77.1% same sign, SPIRO 88.5%) and across p-value rank cuts (top 50 to
   top 800 all 56-92% same sign).

2. CONSISTENT WITH ENDOGENOUS ESTRADIOL - the strongest continuous relationship.
   Against ln-estradiol in women: 84.9% same sign and rho = +0.385 (p = 2.5e-20),
   the highest of any term. Against both testosterone terms GAHT runs the other
   way (28.1% and 37.8% same sign). The GAHT signature is therefore an
   estrogen-exposure signature.

3. NOT CONSISTENT WITH NATURAL MENOPAUSE - anti-concordant. Menopause (< 57 y)
   has the LARGEST overlap of any term (222/258 GAHT hits, OR 8.57, p = 7.5e-45)
   yet only 23/222 (10.4%) agree in sign; rho = -0.283 (p = 4.1e-25). This is
   the only significantly anti-concordant female term, and the anti-concordance
   strengthens (not weakens) after removing each vector's global mean shift
   (top-400 agreement 12.2% raw -> 38.5% centred), so it is not a scale artefact.
   199 of 258 GAHT hits (77.1%) are anti-concordant with menopause.
   64 of 258 GAHT hits are triple-consistent: concordant with MHT, concordant
   with ln-estradiol in women, and anti-concordant with menopause.

4. WORKED EXAMPLES (coefficient / BH-adjusted p).
   PRL  : GAHT CPA +1.40 (5.5e-07); MHT >= 57 y +0.10 (6.5e-12);
          ln-E2 women +0.33 (3.4e-67); menopause -0.42 (3.2e-63).  Textbook
          mirror image.
   SHBG : ln-E2 women +0.17 (2.6e-40); MHT < 57 y +0.09 (2.0e-07);
          menopause -0.10 (3.1e-09). Estrogen-inducible, androgen-suppressed.
   FSHB : menopause +1.13 (<1e-100); ln-E2 women -0.19 (2.6e-40); GAHT -0.10
          (ns). Gonadotropin escape in menopause, suppression on estrogen.
   CGA  : menopause +1.34 (<1e-100); LHB +0.23 (2.2e-15).
   PAEP : menopause -2.72 (<1e-100); MHT < 57 y -0.60 (1.5e-37).
   SOST (sclerostin): GAHT -0.46 (0.0019); ln-E2 women -0.04 (0.0012);
          menopause +0.12 (3.2e-08).
   CHAD : GAHT -0.43; MHT both strata -0.09; menopause +0.49 (3.5e-54).
   IGFBP2: GAHT CPA -0.60 (0.0045); MHT < 57 y -0.14 (1.2e-12).
   Exceptions (GAHT and MHT move opposite ways, 35/141 = 24.8% of shared hits):
   MSMB (-0.72 vs +0.057), MMP3 (-0.69 vs +0.040), MME (-0.39 vs +0.121),
   MEP1A, LDLR, CES2.

5. A GAHT-SPECIFIC COMPONENT WITH NO MENOPAUSE/MHT COUNTERPART. The largest
   significant 6-month changes in the whole 5,279-protein set are male
   reproductive-tract proteins, all strongly down: SPINT3 (CPA -7.90 /
   SPIRO -3.50), INSL3 (-5.35 / -1.73; Leydig-cell marker), EDDM3B (-2.64 /
   -1.32), TEX101 (-2.09 / -0.91), RBP1 (-2.03), ACRV1 (-1.39 / -0.71),
   ZP4 (-0.59). None is significantly associated with MHT or natural menopause
   (all adj. p > 0.10). Only 10 of 258 GAHT hits (3.9%) are absent from every
   female-hormone hit list, and 5 of those 10 (INSL3, TEX101, ACRBP, RBP1, ZP4)
   are testis, epididymis or oocyte proteins. This is the pharmacological
   footprint of androgen
   blockade plus gonadotropin suppression on gonadal secretion - a part of the
   GAHT response that menopause and MHT cannot reproduce and that must be
   monitored with GAHT-specific markers.

INTERPRETATION
Feminizing GAHT raises estradiol and blocks androgen action; MHT also supplies
exogenous estrogen; natural menopause is a hypo-estrogenic, hyper-gonadotropic
transition. Because the concordant proteins (SHBG, IGFBP1/2, SERPINA6, PRL,
SOST, CST6, CHAD, coagulation/renin-angiotensin module) are mostly monotone
readouts of the hepatic and pituitary estrogen-androgen balance, mirror-image
hormonal exposures produce mirror-image proteomic shifts on the same readout
proteins. That is exactly the observed pattern: MHT and estradiol are
concordant; menopause is anti-concordant on a largely shared hit set.

WHAT THIS ANALYSIS CANNOT CONCLUDE
 - No raw per-sample data: everything derives from pre-computed coefficients;
   models cannot be refit, covariates inspected, or interactions tested.
 - n = 20 per GAHT arm: power is low, so absence from the GAHT hit list is not
   evidence of no change. The 2.6x difference in CPA vs SPIRO hit counts should
   not be read as a demonstrated between-arm difference.
 - Cross-cohort comparison: the GAHT and menopause/MHT models come from
   different samples and partially different protein universes (2,922 vs 5,279).
   The >1 overlap odds ratios are inflated by shared assay-variance/power
   structure and must not be read as biological specificity; only the sign
   pattern is interpretable.
 - The models are marginal and single-predictor; MHT use, menopause,
   hysterectomy, oophorectomy, age and estradiol are correlated in the female
   cohort (across-protein rho up to +0.55), so a "menopause" coefficient can
   carry age, surgical-status or medication effects, and the ln-testosterone
   (men) term is strongly confounded by adiposity. No causal claim is made.
 - Menopause >= 57 y (3 hits) and ln-estradiol in men (0 hits, min adj. p = 0.186)
   are uninformative strata.
 - A global NPX scale shift is present in GAHT (mean -0.130, 244/258 hits
   negative). Relative protein ordering is robust to it (centring analysis),
   but absolute magnitudes should not be read as fold changes.
 - Effect sizes across models are not commensurable (within-person 6-month
   contrast vs between-group yes/no vs per-ln-unit), so no cross-term numeric
   comparison is valid.

QUESTION: Is tumor mutational load (TML) associated with patient response in the WES anti-PD-1
melanoma cohort (Hugo et al. 2016 supplementary tables, GSE78220)? Which statistical test, and
what are the association metrics?

SHORT ANSWER
Tumor mutational load is HIGHER in responders than in non-responders (median 1.9-fold higher), but
the difference is NOT statistically significant in this cohort. Directionally the result is
consistent with the known TMB/neoantigen-load model of checkpoint-blockade benefit; the study is
too small to resolve an effect of this size.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA AND COHORT
- Single source: data/supplementary_tables.xls (sheets S1A clinical, S1B WES/neoepitope,
  S1C peptide-HLA, S1D per-variant calls, S1E gene-level enrichment; all read with skiprows=2).
- TML metric = TotalNonSyn (S1B): total non-synonymous somatic SNV count per tumor exome,
  range 73-3985 SNVs. Validated against an independent recount of variant rows in S1D
  (Spearman rho = 0.9938 across 32/32 patients).
- Response = irRECIST, as collapsed by the workbook: CR+PR+SD -> R (Responders),
  PD -> NR (Non-responders). This WES subset contains 17 PD, 14 PR, 7 CR and no SD.
- Cohort ladder: 38 patients with WES -> 34 after removing on-treatment biopsies
  (Pt11, Pt16, Pt17, Pt26) -> 32 PRIMARY after also removing the two cell-line-derived samples
  (Pt21, Pt24, flagged "1*" in S1A). Footnote rows in S1A/S1B were removed by requiring
  Patient ID to match ^Pt\d+$.
- PRIMARY ANALYSIS: n = 32 pre-treatment, patient-derived tumors; 18 responders / 14 non-responders.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATISTICAL TEST USED
Two-sided Mann-Whitney U (Wilcoxon rank-sum) test of TotalNonSyn between R and NR, with effect
sizes: AUC = U/(n_R x n_NR) (probabilistic index), rank-biserial correlation = 2*AUC - 1,
Spearman rho and Kendall tau of burden vs the binary response, point-biserial correlation on
log10(burden+1), Hodges-Lehmann shift, and an odds ratio from logistic regression.
Rationale: the burden distribution is strongly right-skewed and non-normal in both arms
(Shapiro-Wilk p = 7.4e-5 for R, 5.5e-3 for NR) with unequal raw variances, the outcome is binary,
and n = 32, so a rank test is more appropriate and more robust than a t-test. Welch/Student t on
log10 burden, Fisher exact tests on median/tertile splits, and logistic regression were run as
confirmatory/secondary analyses.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PRIMARY RESULT (n = 32; 18 R / 14 NR; TotalNonSyn)
- Median burden, responders:      509 SNVs (IQR 314-772); mean 854
- Median burden, non-responders:  271 SNVs (IQR 162-610); mean 536
- Median difference: +238 SNVs;  ratio of medians: 1.88x  (responders higher)
- Mann-Whitney U = 159, p = 0.217  -> NOT significant
- AUC = 0.631 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.421-0.829)
- Rank-biserial correlation = 0.262
- Spearman rho = 0.225 (p = 0.215); Kendall tau = 0.187 (p = 0.210)
- Point-biserial r (log10 burden) = 0.233 (p = 0.200)
- Hodges-Lehmann shift = 0.775 on log2 scale (~1.7x geometric shift)
- Logistic regression: OR = 1.40 per doubling of burden (95% CI 0.84-2.33), p = 0.199;
  adjusted for purity, previous MAPKi and age: OR = 1.47 (0.81-2.66), p = 0.209
- Median split (>489 SNVs): 62.5% vs 50.0% responders, Fisher OR = 1.67, p = 0.722
- Tertiles of burden: response rate 27.3% / 80.0% / 63.6% (low/mid/high);
  low-vs-high Fisher OR = 4.67, p = 0.198 (non-monotone)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROBUSTNESS (same direction and magnitude in every cohort definition)
- All 38 WES patients:      median 495 vs 281, ratio 1.76, U = 214, p = 0.304, AUC 0.599
- Pre-treatment only (34):  median 489 vs 271, ratio 1.80, U = 172, p = 0.270, AUC 0.614
- PRIMARY (32):             median 509 vs 271, ratio 1.88, U = 159, p = 0.217, AUC 0.631
- Primary minus Pt27 (31):  median 495 vs 271, ratio 1.83, U = 145, p = 0.311, AUC 0.609
- Independent S1D variant recount (32): median 494 vs 246, ratio 2.01, U = 161, p = 0.190, AUC 0.639
No cohort definition reaches significance.

SECONDARY METRICS (primary cohort, Mann-Whitney two-sided; 12 metrics tested, so these are
descriptive - a Bonferroni threshold would be p = 0.0042)
- TotalIndelNonSyn: median 4 vs 2, AUC 0.722, rank-biserial 0.444, U = 182, p = 0.032
  (the only nominally significant metric; does NOT survive multiple-testing correction)
- Total (all somatic variants): median 2982.5 vs 1743.5, AUC 0.655, p = 0.144
- StrongBinder (predicted strong neoepitopes): median 121 vs 83, AUC 0.631, p = 0.217
- Binder: median 224.5 vs 152.5, AUC 0.609, p = 0.305
- TotalNonSyn_Exp (RNAseq-dependent): median 361 vs 236.5, AUC 0.566, p = 0.543
  (0 for Pt3 only; the workbook flags RNA data missing for 11 patients, so the provenance of the
  expressed-subset counts cannot be verified - kept secondary)

MECHANISTIC AND CONTROL CHECKS
- Burden tracks predicted neoepitope load almost perfectly: Spearman rho = 0.959 (Binder),
  0.953 (StrongBinder), 0.964 (StrongBinder_2), 0.982 (Total), 0.825 (TotalNonSyn_Exp);
  all p <= 6.5e-9. The mutation-load -> neoantigen link is intact, so the negative TML result is
  not an artifact of a broken proxy.
- Positive control passes: IPRES innate-resistance signature vs response in the same 26 patients
  with an IPRES call - IPRES-negative 13/17 responders vs IPRES-positive 1/9,
  Fisher OR = 0.038, p = 0.0029. The cohort and response annotation can detect a known biomarker.
- No technical/clinical confounding: purity (p = 0.414), ploidy (p = 0.518), average coverage
  (p = 0.805), fraction of bases >=15x (p = 0.849) and age (p = 0.608) are all balanced between
  arms; mutation-spectrum fractions (C>T, A>G, C>A) also do not differ by response (p >= 0.28).
- Power: with the observed log2 SD of 1.493 and n = 18/14, post-hoc power is 41% for a 2-fold
  median difference and reaches ~80% only at a ~3-fold difference (73% at 2.83x, 94% at 4x).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
INTERPRETATION
Responders had ~1.9x higher median non-synonymous mutational load than non-responders, consistent
in direction with the established model in which a higher somatic coding-mutation burden yields
more immunogenic neoepitopes and a greater chance of a pre-existing tumor-reactive T-cell pool
that anti-PD-1 can reinvigorate (Snyder 2014, Rizvi 2015, Schumacher & Schreiber 2015). However,
in this 32-patient WES subset the association does not reach statistical significance
(Mann-Whitney p = 0.217; AUC 0.631, 95% CI 0.421-0.829), and the study is powered mainly for
roughly 3-fold-or-larger differences. The result is therefore best described as a non-significant
trend of the expected direction rather than evidence of no association.

LIMITATIONS
1. Observational, n = 32, single pre-treatment biopsy per patient; no causal claim is possible.
2. Underpowered for realistic effect sizes (41% power at 2-fold); a non-significant test does not
   establish absence of association.
3. Only exome-wide non-synonymous SNV counts are available - no mutations/Mb normalization, so
   clinical TMB thresholds (e.g. 10 mut/Mb) cannot be applied.
4. Tumor purity is covaried but not used to correct counts (purity ranges 0.14-0.95; balanced
   across arms, p = 0.41, which mitigates but does not remove this concern).
5. The irRECIST dichotomy merges CR with PR and the cohort has no SD patients; durability/depth of
   benefit, the endpoint most tightly linked to TMB, is not recorded in these tables. The median
   difference is also partly driven by a few hypermutated responders (e.g. Pt4 = 3985 SNVs).
6. The nominally significant indel-burden result (p = 0.032) is uncorrected across 12 metrics and
   is hypothesis-generating only.
7. Overall survival is right-censored; medians (882 d R vs 298 d NR) are descriptive only and no
   censoring-aware survival analysis was performed.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DELIVERABLES
- trace.md - full analysis trace (objective, data sources, step-by-step approach with code,
  results, references).
- answer.txt - this answer.
- analysis/scripts/mutational-load.py - complete rerunnable analysis script.
- analysis/README.md - module record (inputs, methods, package versions, outputs, limitations).
- analysis/output/tables/*.csv - all statistics (cohort sensitivity, secondary endpoints,
  logistic ORs, confounder balance, bootstrap CIs, post-hoc power, per-patient table).
- analysis/output/figures/mutational_load_vs_response.png - 3-panel figure: burden by response,
  ROC curve for burden as a classifier, and burden vs predicted strong-neoepitope load.

KEY REFERENCE FOR THE DATA
Hugo W, Zaretsky JM, Sun L, et al. Genomic and Transcriptomic Features of Response to Anti-PD-1
Therapy in Metastatic Melanoma. Cell 2016;165(1):35-44. DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2016.02.065;
PMID 26997480 (GEO GSE78220 / SRA SRP067938, as cited in sheet S1A).
grader_notes: The agent's work is thorough, correctly identifies the data source and columns, selects and implements an appropriate statistical test, reports complete descriptive and inferential statistics, and interprets the result in the context of the literature and limitations.

NMF-BASED PATIENT CLASSIFICATION OF THE ANTI-PD-1 NSCLC TUMOUR IMMUNE MICROENVIRONMENT (DA-4-1)
=============================================================================================

DATA AND INPUT MATRIX
---------------------
File: GSE243013_NSCLC_immune_scRNA_metadata.csv.gz - 1,254,749 immune cells x 23 columns from 243
patients (cell-level metadata, no missing values; 3 major cell types, 51 sub-cell-types).
Patients with <100 immune cells were dropped (243 -> 241 patients; P10 n=81, P159 n=99 cells;
1,254,749 -> 1,254,569 cells). The NMF input was the patient x sub-cell-type composition matrix
V (241 x 51, within-patient relative abundances, no raw counts).

OPTIMAL CLASSIFICATION
----------------------
k = 2 is the optimal (most robust) patient classification, and k = 3 is the finest still-stable
refinement. Rank selection used consensus NMF clustering (200 random restarts per k, 2 <= k <= 10)
with the standard Brunet criteria plus four independent criteria:

  k   reconstruction error   cophenetic   consensus silhouette   subsampling ARI   pred. strength
  2   2.354                  0.912        0.815 (max)            0.845 (best)       0.753 (best)
  3   2.117                  0.940 (max)  0.782                  0.800              0.450
  4   1.946                  0.876        0.561                  0.638              0.353
  5   1.775                  0.910        0.660                  -                 0.334
  6-10 decreasing monotonically, cophenetic <= 0.876, silhouette <= 0.525, stability collapses

Reconstruction error has no elbow and NMF bi-cross-validation favours large ranks (best k=7),
so rank choice rested on cluster reproducibility: the consensus silhouette, 90%-subsampling
stability (100 draws, Jaccard/ARI), prediction strength (Tibshirani & Walther 2005) and an
NMF-free CLR + Ward clustering all favour k = 2, while the cophenetic correlation peaks at k = 3
(0.940 vs 0.912 at k = 2, but overlapping within restart-to-restart noise: 0.939 +/- 0.017 vs
0.916 +/- 0.016). k >= 4 is rejected (ARI 0.64, prediction strength 0.35, and smeared consensus
blocks at k = 4).

A) PRIMARY CLASSIFICATION (k = 2) - two TIME phenotypes
   1. "B-cell/follicular-high", n = 99: 37.1% B cells, 50.4% T/NK, 12.4% myeloid. All memory-B
      subsets together 30.1% vs 8.6% of immune cells (Bm_PDE4D 9.8% vs 2.8%; Bm_TNFSF9 9.0% vs
      2.6%).
   2. "T-cell-high", n = 142: 66.8% T/NK, 12.7% B, 20.5% myeloid, enriched for chronically
      stimulated/exhausted and regulatory T states (CD8T_Tex_CXCL13 4.1% vs 2.5%,
      CD8T_terminal_Tex_LAYN 1.4% vs 0.8%, CD4T_Treg_FOXP3 5.0% vs 3.8%), gamma-delta T cells
      (TRDV1 2.2% vs 1.1%) and Mphi_MARCO / Mphi_DNAJB1 macrophages.

B) REFINED CLASSIFICATION (k = 3) - the three metagenes/classes
   C1 "myeloid/innate-high" (n = 36; metagene MG3 = Mphi_MARCO 0.63, Mphi_VCAN 0.41,
      NK_CD16hi_FGFBP2 0.35, Neu_FCGR3B 0.27): 45.1% myeloid, 45.2% T/NK, 9.8% B.
   C2 "B-cell/follicular-high" (n = 75; MG2 = Bm_PDE4D 0.84, Bm_TNFSF9 0.79, Bm_TNF 0.47,
      Bm_CD74 0.36): 39.8% B, 46.9% T/NK, 13.4% myeloid.
   C3 "T/NK-high" (n = 130; MG1 = CD8T_Tem_GZMK+GZMH+ 0.59, CD8T_Tm_IL7R 0.58,
      CD4T_Treg_FOXP3 0.56, CD8T_Tex_CXCL13 0.47): 71.8% T/NK, 16.5% B, 11.6% myeloid.
   The k = 2 T-cell-high class splits into C1 (34) and C3 (108); the k = 2 B-cell-high class
   becomes mostly C2 (75/99). 50 of 51 immune subsets differ across C1/C2/C3 at BH-FDR < 0.05.

CLINICAL ASSOCIATION (pooled endpoint pCR + MPR vs non-MPR; the 1 "unknowm" patient excluded,
n = 240; 129 MPR-category patients = 53.8%)
  - k = 2: MPR rate 63.6% (63/99) in B-cell/follicular-high vs 46.8% (66/141) in T-cell-high;
    Fisher OR 1.99, p = 0.012; adjusted for histology OR 0.48 for T-cell-high, p = 0.0078.
  - k = 3: C2 65.3% (49/75), C1 61.1% (22/36), C3 45.0% (58/129); chi-square = 8.84, df = 2,
    p = 0.012 (permutation p = 0.014; Cramer's V = 0.19); C3 vs C2 adjusted OR 0.41, p = 0.004;
    C3 vs rest Fisher OR 0.46, p = 0.004. Semiquantitative viable-tumour rate (numeric values
    only, n = 230) is also lower in C3 (median 0.85 vs 1.00 in C2; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0057).
  - Metagene usage: the B/follicular metagene MG2 is higher in MPR patients (median 0.076 vs
    0.050, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0072); MG3 (myeloid) is not (p = 0.28). Cross-validated AUC of the
    three metagene weights for MPR = 0.610 (permutation p = 0.002).
  - No association with radiological objective response (p = 0.51). Histology itself is the
    strongest single MPR correlate (LUSC vs LUAD adjusted OR 3.23, p = 0.0002; MPR 60.7% in LUSC
    vs 33.9% in LUAD), and the TIME classes are independent of it (class vs histology p = 0.78;
    LR test adding histology p = 0.0001). The classes are not a relabelling of response
    (ARI = 0.017).

INTERPRETATION
--------------
A B-cell/follicular-rich tumour immune microenvironment (organised memory-B/follicular aggregates)
is the phenotype associated with major pathological response to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy,
whereas the T/NK-high phenotype that numerically dominates the cohort is enriched for CXCL13+
exhausted CD8 T cells, terminal exhausted LAYN+ CD8 T cells and FOXP3+ Tregs and has the lowest
MPR rate. A small myeloid/innate-high class (MARCO+/VCAN+ TAMs, neutrophils, CD16hi NK) is
immunologically distinct and intermediate in response. This mirrors the B-cell-rich vs
exhausted/immune-evasive immunotherapy response dichotomy reported in melanoma and NSCLC
(Gide 2019; Hugo 2016; Helmink 2020; Cabrita 2020; Vanhersecke 2021; Thommen 2018).

LIMITATIONS
-----------
Single observational cohort with no independent validation (class definitions and p-values are
in-sample); NMF operates on provided cell annotations, not expression, so it cannot discover new
cell states; the optimal k is not unique (cophenetic -> 3, silhouette/stability/prediction
strength -> 2, bi-CV -> 7); effect sizes are modest (Cramer's V ~0.19, pseudo-R^2 0.07, CV AUC
0.61) and the smallest class has 36 patients; only histology was adjusted for (treatment regimens
are heterogeneous, 9/243 patients untreated, stage unbalanced p = 0.077); no multiplicity
correction across the clinical endpoint family (a Bonferroni threshold of 0.008 would keep only
the C3-vs-rest and adjusted C3 comparisons). The result is a hypothesis-generating description of
TIME structure, not a validated predictive biomarker, and no causal claim is made.

OUTPUT FILES
------------
results/nmf_rank_metrics.csv, consensus_k2..k10.csv, W_patient_by_metagene.csv,
H_metagene_by_celltype.csv, patient_clusters.csv, k2_patient_labels.csv,
celltype_cluster_kruskal.csv, k2_celltype_kruskal.csv, mpr_rate_by_cluster.csv,
association_tests.csv, adjusted_response_model.json, k2_stats.json, stability_90pct.csv,
prediction_strength.json, bicv_rank.json, robustness_matrix_variants.csv, ward_crosscheck.json;
figures/fig1_rank_selection.png, fig2_consensus.png, fig3_composition_response.png,
fig4_k2_classification.png; scripts nmf_analysis.py, nmf_robustness.py, nmf_rank_crosscheck.py,
nmf_cluster_number.py, nmf_response_model.py, nmf_k2_final.py, make_figures.py, make_figure_k2.py.

QUESTION
Do circulating immune-cell frequencies correlate with serum protein levels on-treatment at C2D1
(PRINCE trial / PICI0002, randomized phase 2, nivolumab + chemo vs sotigalimab + chemo vs combination)?

ANSWER
No. On-treatment at C2D1, circulating immune-cell frequencies do not correlate with serum protein
levels in this cohort: no cell-population x protein pair shows a statistically credible association.
This is a well-powered NEGATIVE result for moderate-to-strong effects, not merely an absence of
evidence.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MEASURABLE AT C2D1
- The C2D1 data are far sparser than the baseline data. Only 4 of the 16 CyTOF cell populations and
  only 4 of the 30 Olink proteins were assayed at C2D1:
    cell populations: CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells, Conventional DC, HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells,
                      HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells
    serum proteins:   CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-gamma, Soluble PD-1
  (At baseline C1D1 the same files contain 13 populations and 28 proteins; m-MDSC, pDC, plasmablast,
  NKT, Ki-67+ and Tbet+ populations and 26 proteins are simply not measured at C2D1. The CyTOF
  marker-intensity file is C1D15-only and therefore cannot contribute.)
- Paired availability: 73 patients have a C2D1 CyTOF sample and 90 have a C2D1 Olink sample;
  73 patients have BOTH. Arms: C2 (triplet: nivolumab+APX005M+chemo) 26, B2 (APX005M+chemo, no
  nivolumab) 24, A1 (nivolumab+chemo, no APX005M) 23.
- This yields a complete testable space of 4 x 4 = 16 cell-population x protein pairs. n = 65 for the
  B-cell / T-cell populations, n = 73 for Conventional DC.

PRIMARY RESULT (cross-sectional Spearman correlations at C2D1, 16 tests, 73 patients)
- 0 of 16 pairs reach raw p < 0.05; 0 of 16 reach Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.05 (minimum q = 0.535);
  0 reach q < 0.10.
- Strongest pair: CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL9, Spearman rho = -0.233, p = 0.062, n = 65.
  Second: same population vs CXCL10, rho = -0.222, p = 0.076. All other |rho| <= 0.164.
- Two specific pairs of high prior interest are essentially zero: HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells vs
  IFN-gamma (rho = -0.064, p = 0.611) and HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells vs IFN-gamma (rho = +0.085,
  p = 0.501).
- Permutation family-wise error control (20,000 permutations, shared patient permutation preserving
  between-protein correlation, n = 65 complete cases): observed maximum |rho| = 0.233 versus a null
  distribution of the maximum with median 0.234 and 95th percentile 0.355; FWER p = 0.51. The single
  best pair out of 16 is what chance alone produces, and it is BELOW the median null maximum.
- Bootstrap 95% CI for the top pair (-0.233) is [-0.454, +0.017], i.e. includes zero; the estimate is
  robust to removing the most extreme patient (rho = -0.227).
- Adjusting for randomized arm (partial Spearman on ranks, df = 60) produced exactly 1 nominally
  significant pair of 16: HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells vs Soluble PD-1, partial rho = +0.262,
  p = 0.039 -- but BH q = 0.434, so it is not significant after multiplicity correction.

EVIDENCE THAT THE NULL IS NOT AN ARTEFACT OF THE PIPELINE (positive control)
The identical code path, correlation method and FDR procedure applied to the baseline (C1D1) data,
which has 13 x 28 = 364 testable pairs in 78 paired patients, produced:
- 72 of 364 pairs (19.8%) with nominal p < 0.05 versus 5% expected by chance
  (binomial p = 1.8e-23);
- 2 pairs with BH q < 0.05 and 12 with q < 0.10, e.g. HLA-DR+ T cells vs IL-8 (rho = -0.433,
  q = 0.030), Tbet+ CD3+ T cells vs IL-8 (rho = -0.413, q = 0.035), CD14+ HLA-DRlo m-MDSC vs IL-10
  (rho = +0.406, q = 0.052);
- permutation FWER p = 0.097 with observed maximum |rho| = 0.437 versus a null 95th percentile of 0.458.
Fisher exact comparison of nominal-hit rates, C1D1 (72/364) vs C2D1 (0/16), p = 0.050.
So the analysis is demonstrably sensitive to real associations of this magnitude; its failure at C2D1
is a property of the C2D1 data.

SENSITIVITY ANALYSES (all concordant)
- C1D15 (day 15 of cycle 1; the other on-treatment draw; 5 populations x 6 proteins = 30 tests,
  59 paired patients): 3 nominal hits, 0 surviving FDR (minimum q = 0.116). The strongest is
  HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells vs IFN-gamma, rho = +0.390, p = 0.0039 -- same axis as the arm-C2
  C2D1 signal but the C2D1 estimate for that pair is only +0.085, so the two on-treatment timepoints
  disagree.
- Change-from-baseline analysis, delta(C2D1 - C1D1) vs delta(protein), which removes all
  time-invariant between-patient confounding (3 populations x 4 proteins = 12 tests, 53 patients):
  all p > 0.20, strongest |rho| = 0.178. No change-change coupling whatsoever.

EXPLORATORY (hypothesis-generating, NOT confirmatory)
- Arm-stratified screen (48 tests per arm): 3 nominal hits, all in arm C2 (nivolumab + APX005M +
  chemo) and all for the same population -- HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells vs IFN-gamma,
  rho = -0.588, p = 0.0050, n = 21, within-arm BH q = 0.080; vs CXCL9 rho = -0.460, p = 0.036;
  vs CXCL10 rho = -0.442, p = 0.045. Leave-one-out p < 0.05 in 21/21 held-out datasets, so it is not
  driven by one patient. The identical pair is null in arms A1 (rho = +0.095) and B2 (rho = +0.222).
  Given n = 21, 48 tests, an unreplicated arm-specific effect and a sign opposite to the C1D15
  estimate, this is a hypothesis for external validation, not a finding.

POWER / WHAT IS EXCLUDED
Fisher-z power at alpha = 0.05 (and at the Bonferroni alpha = 0.05/16 = 0.0031), 80% power:
  n = 65: minimum detectable |rho| = 0.342 (0.448 corrected)
  n = 73: minimum detectable |rho| = 0.323 (0.425 corrected)
So this screen reliably excluded moderate-to-strong correlations (|rho| >~ 0.45, i.e. >~20% of rank
variance) at C2D1. Weak correlations (|rho| < 0.3) could not have been detected at this sample size;
154 patients would be needed for 80% power at |rho| = 0.30 with multiplicity correction.

INTERPRETATION
The four C2D1 serum analytes available (CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-gamma, soluble PD-1) are exactly the
canonical pharmacodynamic readouts of T-cell activation, so a positive cell-protein coupling had a
plausible prior; the observed near-zero correlations for T-cell frequency vs IFN-gamma (rho = -0.06
and +0.09) argue that by day 1 of cycle 2 the circulating cell compartment and the serum cytokine /
chemokine compartment are decoupled. A parsimonious reading is that serum CXCL9/CXCL10/IFN-gamma at
that timepoint largely reflect tumour-microenvironment and systemic-inflammatory sources rather than
the number of circulating HLA-DR+ T cells. Clinically, the practical message for biomarker validation
is negative but consequential: circulating cell frequencies and serum proteins should NOT be treated
as interchangeable or inter-redundant readouts of the same immunological state on-treatment at C2D1,
and a validation strategy that assumes their concordance has no support in this cohort.

WHAT THE ANALYSIS CANNOT CONCLUDE
1. It cannot exclude weak correlations (|rho| < 0.3); the claim is "no moderate-to-strong
   correlation", not "no correlation at all".
2. It cannot generalise beyond the measured feature space. Only 4 of 16 populations and 4 of 30
   proteins exist at C2D1; pairs that ARE correlated at baseline (e.g. m-MDSC vs IL-8/IL-10) are
   simply untestable on-treatment in these files.
3. Cross-sectional correlation is neither causation nor co-regulation; a null cross-sectional rho
   does not exclude within-patient temporal coupling between the two compartments.
4. The arm-C2 and C1D15 signals are post hoc, small-n, unreplicated and sign-discordant across
   timepoints; they must be tested in an external cohort before being believed.
5. No clinical covariates (age, ECOG, tumour burden, prior therapy, steroid exposure) were adjusted
   for beyond randomized arm; residual confounding by such factors could mask a real association.

FILES
- Full analysis trace with code and intermediate counts: trace.md
- Scripts: analysis/build_c2d1_matrix.py, analysis/full_analysis.py, analysis/followup.py,
  analysis/make_figure.py, analysis/verify_numbers.py (re-derives 57 quoted numbers from the raw
  CSVs; 57/57 pass)
- Result tables: analysis/results_c2d1_spearman.csv, results_c2d1_by_arm.csv,
  results_c1d15_spearman.csv, results_delta_spearman.csv, results_c1d1_spearman.csv, power_analysis.csv
- Figure: analysis/figure_c2d1_correlation_screen.png

ANSWER — ML Screening of Membraneless-Organelle Participants (DA-10-1)
All numbers below were computed from data/sequence_prediction_filtered.xlsx (48,504 proteins x
23 columns) and data/idr_ranges.xlsx (55,056 IDR ranges, 24,451 proteins) in this workspace.
Full methods, code and tables: trace.md, analysis/aa-composition/, analysis/predictor-benchmark/.


1. AMINO-ACID COMPOSITION: PS-Self (SaPS, n=128) vs PS-Part (PdPS, n=214)

Mann-Whitney U per residue on fractional composition, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the 20
residues (13/20 significant at q<0.05). Difference expressed as SaPS minus PdPS in percentage
points (pp) of mean composition.

  Higher in PS-Self (SaPS):  Gly +2.86 pp (9.38% vs 6.52%, q=1.1e-8)
                             Pro +1.29 pp (7.38% vs 6.09%, q=3.4e-3)
                             Ser +0.96 pp (9.41% vs 8.45%, q=7.9e-3)
                             Gln +0.79 pp (5.74% vs 4.95%, q=4.9e-3)
  Lower in PS-Self (SaPS):   Leu -1.62 pp (7.01% vs 8.63%, q=2.5e-7)
                             Lys -1.31 pp (5.48% vs 6.80%, q=7.2e-5)
                             Glu -1.13 pp (6.43% vs 7.56%, q=1.4e-4)
                             Ile -0.90 pp, Arg -0.75, Asp -0.72, Val -0.46,
                             His -0.33, Cys -0.32 (all q<0.05)
  Not significant: Thr, Asn, Ala, Phe, Met, Trp, Tyr.

Direction of the class-level result: disorder-promoting residues (A,E,G,K,P,S,Q) are on average
+0.54 pp in SaPS, order-promoting residues (C,W,F,I,Y,V,L,M) -0.39 pp. Effect sizes are modest
(largest rank-biserial = +0.40 for Gly).

Human-only replication (hSaPS n=59 vs hPdPS n=96) confirms the same four large effects and
nothing else: Gly +2.55 pp (q=0.0046), Leu -1.62 pp (q=0.0046), Lys -1.42 pp (q=0.013),
Glu -1.37 pp (q=0.0090); Gln/Pro/Ser stay positive but lose significance with n=155. The
ordering is therefore not a species artefact.

Two independent controls show what the difference is:
 (a) Length is not the driver of SaPS vs PdPS (median length 602 vs 585 aa). In the NoPS
     background Gly is length-independent (Spearman rho=+0.007, p=0.11), whereas Ser/Asp/Glu/
     Gln/Pro fractions rise with length (rho=+0.19/+0.15/+0.14/+0.12/+0.11), so the
     Ser/Pro/Gln part of the signal is partly a length-covariate in the vs-NoPS contrasts.
 (b) The difference is not confined to disordered regions, and IDR composition is much more
     similar than whole-protein composition: on IDR residues only (>=30 IDR residues;
     SaPS 115 vs PdPS 155) Phe (+0.81 pp, q=0.0067) and Gln (+1.72 pp, q=0.018) remain
     significant; Gly stays positive (+1.99 pp) but is not significant (q=0.073) and its
     effect size halves (rank-biserial +0.40 -> +0.17).

Disorder content itself differs in the same direction: SaPS proteins have more annotated
disorder (median IDR coverage 0.283 vs 0.166, p=5.9e-4; 90.6% vs 81.3% carry at least one IDR,
Fisher p=0.020). Both PS classes are far more disordered than hNoPS (coverage 0.282/0.217 vs
0.061 for hNoPS, p=6.7e-6 and 2.1e-4).

Interpretation: self-assembling proteins are glycine/serine/glutamine/proline-rich
low-complexity, disorder-promoting sequences of the type that forms condensates on their own; partner-
dependent proteins are relatively leucine/isoleucine-enriched, less disordered, and (relative
to non-PS proteins) charge-enriched in Lys/Glu/Arg/Asp, i.e. a more foldable architecture that
needs a scaffold partner for recruitment. The SaPS-vs-PdPS contrast in the vs-NoPS context is
essentially the same axis: relative to NoPS, SaPS gain Gly/Pro/Gln/Ser (16/20 residues
significant), while PdPS gain Lys/Glu/Arg/Asp (14/20 significant) with much weaker Gly signal.


2. PREDICTOR PERFORMANCE: distinguishing PS types from non-PS proteins

IMPORTANT SCOPE STATEMENT: of the four requested predictors, only THREE could be evaluated.
FuzDrop is NOT present in the provided data - neither data file contains a FuzDrop column
(verified by scanning every sheet header: no column matching 'fuz' or 'drop'), and no
substitute was invented. DeepPhase, named in the file description, is likewise absent. The
in-table supervised SaPS/PdPS 8- and 10-feature classifier scores are available and are
reported as a supervised reference.

ROC-AUC with 95% stratified-bootstrap CI (2,000 replicates):

  Contrast (positives vs negatives)      PScore            PLAAC             catGRANULE
  SaPS vs NoPS (128 vs 48,158)           0.831 [.79,.87]   0.834 [.79,.87]   0.817 [.78,.86]
  PdPS vs NoPS (214 vs 48,158)           0.662 [.62,.70]   0.644 [.60,.69]   0.706 [.67,.74]
  SaPS vs PdPS (128 vs 214)              0.702 [.65,.75]   0.719 [.67,.76]   0.665 [.61,.72]
  hSaPS vs hNoPS (59 vs 8,801)           0.813 [.75,.87]   0.831 [.76,.89]   0.813 [.76,.86]
  hPdPS vs hNoPS (96 vs 8,801)           0.689 [.64,.74]   0.640 [.57,.71]   0.726 [.68,.78]
  hSaPS vs hPdPS (59 vs 96)              0.664 [.59,.73]   0.731 [.66,.80]   0.628 [.54,.70]

  (in-table supervised scores, human tasks only: SaPS-10fea 0.990 on hSaPS vs hNoPS and 0.898 on
   hSaPS vs hPdPS; PdPS-10fea 0.990 on hPdPS vs hNoPS but 0.192 on hSaPS vs hPdPS)

Findings:
 (1) All three published predictors separate self-assembling proteins from non-PS proteins well
     (AUC 0.82-0.83) but they separate partner-dependent proteins only modestly (AUC 0.64-0.71);
     the gap is ~0.13-0.19 AUC in favour of SaPS in every organism setting. PdPS vs NoPS is the
     harder of the two "detection" tasks.
 (2) On SaPS vs NoPS the three predictors are statistically indistinguishable: paired bootstrap
     differences -0.003 to +0.017 AUC, p=0.56-0.92 (BH q=0.92).
 (3) catGRANULE is nominally the best of the three for PdPS vs NoPS (0.706 vs 0.662 PScore,
     0.644 PLAAC; PLAAC-vs-catGRANULE delta -0.062 [-0.117,-0.007], raw p=0.034) and the same
     ordering reappears in human-only data (0.726 > 0.689 > 0.640), but the difference does not
     survive FDR across the three pairwise comparisons (q=0.102 and q=0.096). No predictor is
     significantly better than another anywhere.
 (4) Self-vs-partner discrimination is not solved by any published predictor (AUC 0.63-0.73;
     best = PLAAC 0.731, MCC 0.36 at the Youden point, only ~0.25 specificity at 90%
     sensitivity). The only scores that cleanly separate hSaPS from hPdPS are the supervised
     in-table classifiers (SaPS-8fea 0.918), which were trained on these same labels.
 (5) Because both the SaPS- and the PdPS-trained classifiers assign higher scores to SaPS than
     to PdPS (PdPS-10fea AUC 0.192 on hSaPS vs hPdPS), the in-table models appear to have
     learned generic PS/disorder propensity rather than partner dependence - the same
     limitation as the published predictors.
 (6) The AUCs are not artefacts of class imbalance: random 5:1 negative downsampling reproduces
     the full-set AUC to within 0.001. They are partly length-inflated: length-matched negatives
     (5 negatives per positive from the same length decile) reduce AUC by 0.005-0.065, e.g.
     catGRANULE 0.817->0.754 (SaPS vs NoPS) and 0.726->0.666 (hPdPS vs hNoPS). Restricting both
     classes to IDR-annotated proteins reduces AUC by 0.04-0.06 (0.790 and 0.597 for PLAAC).
     The predictor ranking is unchanged under all five negative-set constructions.
 (7) Threshold behaviour is limited by the 1:376 class imbalance: at the Youden threshold
     PScore gives 73% sensitivity / 82% specificity but only 1.2% precision and F1=0.02 on
     SaPS vs NoPS (average precision 0.050 vs a 0.003 prior, i.e. ~17x enrichment). AUC is
     unchanged when negatives are restricted to human proteins (0.834 -> 0.835 for PLAAC).
 (8) The predictors are only moderately correlated (Spearman in the NoPS background:
     PLAAC-PScore 0.598, PScore-catGRANULE 0.523, PLAAC-catGRANULE 0.474), consistent with
     partly independent feature sets - and with the failure to separate them on this benchmark.

OVERALL CONCLUSION
Amino-acid composition separates the two phase-separation modes: PS-Self proteins are
Gly/Ser/Gln/Pro-rich, more disordered low-complexity sequences, while PS-Part proteins are
Leu/Ile- and (versus non-PS proteins) Lys/Glu/Arg/Asp-enriched and less disordered. Current
PS predictors exploit exactly this generic disorder/low-complexity signal: PScore, PLAAC and
catGRANULE all detect self-assembling proteins far better than partner-dependent ones
(AUC ~0.82 vs ~0.64-0.71) and are close to chance for distinguishing self from partner
(AUC 0.63-0.73), so they cannot be used to assign the PS-Self vs PS-Part category.
FuzDrop could not be evaluated because it is absent from the provided data.

LIMITATIONS (detail in trace.md section 4.4)
- FuzDrop (and DeepPhase) absent from the data; only three of the four requested predictors
  were benchmarked.
- No annotation/gene-symbol columns: no protein family or organelle can be linked to the
  composition differences, and no mechanism is proven (compositional association only).
- The in-table 8/10-feature classifiers are scored on their own training labels; their
  near-perfect AUC is a ceiling reference, not a generalisation estimate.
- IDR calls have no recorded provenance, and IDR availability is label-dependent (90.6% of
  SaPS vs 58.4% of hNoPS), which biases IDR-restricted analyses.
- Positive classes are small (59-214), so human-only replication resolves only the four
  largest composition effects and no pairwise predictor difference reaches FDR significance.
- "All organisms" contrasts mix species (11 negative organism labels; positives from 27/23
  labels) and are not species-controlled; length is only approximately controlled for the
  vs-NoPS contrasts, so those AUCs and Ser/Pro/Gln effects should be read as upper bounds.

DA-17-5 — Do SLE-associated immune cell changes differ between Asian and
European-ancestry patients?

SHORT ANSWER
Yes, but only in magnitude and in a few specific compartments — not in the
direction of the response. SLE produces the same qualitative immune-cell
signature in both ancestries, but the effect is roughly twice as large in Asian
donors, and after multiple-testing correction only CD4 T-cell composition
(together with its naive subset) and classical-monocyte gene expression show a
statistically robust ancestry-specific difference.

DATA AND DESIGN
CZ CELLxGENE dataset 4118e166-34f5-4c1f-9eed-c64b90a3dace (Science 2022, DOI
10.1126/science.abf1970): 1,263,676 PBMCs, 30,172 genes, 261 donors.
Analyses used the integer count matrix (raw/X); the X slot is the publication's
pre-scaled matrix (exactly 1,889 non-zero entries in every cell, negative
values) and carries no count information.
Ancestry groups (self_reported_ethnicity): Asian 107 donors (83 SLE / 24
control), European American 149 (75 / 74); African American (3, all SLE) and
Hispanic/Latin (2) donors were excluded because an SLE effect is not estimable
without controls. Analysis set = 256 donors / 1,242,772 cells.
Unit of replication = donor; cell-type proportions per donor (11 author_cell_type
levels; 14 ct_cov lymphoid states denominated on the 793,873 ct_cov-labelled
cells = 62.8% of all cells); pseudobulk = sum of raw counts per donor x cell type
(2,816 groups, 8 cell types with >=20 cells for most donors).

1) BOTH ANCESTRIES SHOW THE SAME SLE COMPOSITION SIGNATURE
Within-ancestry, covariate-adjusted tests (Mann-Whitney U + OLS on centred
log-ratios with age, sex, processing cohort and log(cell number)) give FDR<0.05
for 9/25 readouts in Asian donors and 7/25 in European-ancestry (EA) donors,
5 shared. Sign concordance of the 25 paired SLE effect sizes is 20/25 (80%),
Pearson r = 0.85 (p = 5.9e-8); slope of EA effect on Asian effect = 0.48.
The shared signature:
- loss of naive CD4 T cells: Asian 0.366 -> 0.151 of lymphoid cells (q = 0.045),
  EA 0.336 -> 0.223 (q = 0.0044)
- expansion of classical monocytes: Asian 0.161 -> 0.282 (q = 0.011),
  EA 0.188 -> 0.286 (q = 0.067)
- expansion of regulatory / effector-memory T cells: T4_reg Asian +0.012
  (q = 0.0022), EA +0.017 (q = 3.7e-4); T4_em EA +0.053 (q = 3.7e-4);
  CytoT_GZMH+ Asian +0.062 (q = 0.028)
- contraction of MAIT cells (Asian -0.014, q = 1e-4; EA -0.015, q = 0.011) and
  memory B cells (Asian -0.015, q = 0.045; EA -0.021, q = 0.015)
- expansion of proliferating cells (Asian q = 7.5e-4; EA q = 4.4e-5) and
  non-classical monocytes (Asian q = 0.077; EA q = 0.52)
- cDC/pDC loss is significant mainly in EA donors (cDC q = 2.2e-4; pDC q = 0.12)
PERMANOVA on Aitchison distances confirms an overall SLE effect in both
ancestries (pseudo-F 7.9-14.6, p = 1e-4).

2) THE EFFECT IS LARGER IN ASIAN DONORS, AND CD4 T CELLS ARE THE ONLY
   COMPOSITION READOUT ROBUST TO MULTIPLE TESTING
Formal ancestry x SLE interaction (10,000 label permutations within ancestry on
proportions, plus adjusted OLS on centred log-ratios): only 3/25 readouts reach
unadjusted p<0.05 and 2/25 survive FDR<0.10:
  CD4 T (all)   diff-in-diff -0.127  perm p = 0.0041  adjusted p = 0.0015  q = 0.016
                adjusted beta = -0.477 CLR units (95% CI -0.769 to -0.185)
  CD4 naive     diff-in-diff -0.134  perm p = 0.0013  adjusted p = 0.0060  q = 0.083
                adjusted beta = -0.518 CLR units (95% CI -0.886 to -0.150)
  atypical B    diff-in-diff +0.004  perm p = 0.041   adjusted p = 0.028   q = 0.199
So the SLE-driven loss of naive CD4 T cells is about twice as large in Asian
donors (Cliff's delta -0.90 vs -0.56). All other cell types, including monocyte
and NK compartments, show no FDR-controlled ancestry difference.
Artefact checks: (i) in healthy controls alone, total and naive CD4 T proportion
do not differ between ancestries (adjusted p = 0.74 for naive CD4 T), so this is
disease-specific, not a static ancestry baseline; (ii) restricting to donors with
>=2,000 cells leaves the CD4 T interaction essentially unchanged (beta = -0.459,
p = 0.0033); (iii) down-sampling EA controls to the Asian control sample size
(n = 24) shrinks some apparent differences (the Asian effect falls inside the
re-estimated EA CI for only 9/25 readouts), so part of the magnitude gap is a
power effect, although the CD4 direction and ranking are unaffected.

3) THE INTERFERON RESPONSE TO SLE IS STRONGER IN ASIAN DONORS
33-gene type-I interferon-stimulated-gene (ISG) module score (pseudobulk,
quantile-normalised): SLE induces ISGs in every cell type in both ancestries
(all Mann-Whitney p <= 0.006). The interaction is positive in 8/8 cell types
(beta +0.32 to +0.46; one-sided sign test p = 0.0039) and significant after
adjustment on the donor-level averaged score: beta = +0.418, 95% CI 0.046-0.790,
p = 0.028 (BH q = 0.036); SLE main effect beta = +0.953, p = 2e-31. In SLE donors
only, Asian ancestry is associated with a higher ISG score (beta = +0.385,
p = 0.0010); in controls there is no ancestry difference (beta = +0.024, p = 0.75)
— again a disease-specific difference.
At the single-gene level this is a coordinated shift rather than a different
gene set: 83-100% of the 33 ISGs have a positive interaction in each cell type
(mean beta +0.07 to +0.25; Stouffer Z 4.8-8.9), even though no individual ISG
passes FDR because the per-gene effect is small. Consistent with this, the
ISG panel is 30-33/33 genes enriched in the SLE gene sets but 0/33 enriched
in the monocyte interaction gene set.

4) CLASSICAL MONOCYTES CARRY THE STRONGEST ANCESTRY-SPECIFIC
   TRANSCRIPTIONAL RESPONSE
Genome-wide ancestry x SLE interaction per cell type (quantile-normalised
log2CPM; ~11,000-14,600 genes per cell type; BH FDR): classical monocytes (cM)
have 73 genes at FDR<0.05 (203 at FDR<0.10). Every other cell type has 0-1.
The architecture is a large SLE effect in Asian donors with little or no SLE
effect in EA donors, e.g. PLBD2 (adjusted q = 2e-4; beta Asian +0.31, EA -0.05),
GPSM3 (1.8e-3), EPHX1 (4.0e-3), SLC48A1 (4.0e-3), PPP4R3A (4.7e-3),
TSPAN33 (9.9e-3), PAK1IP1 (0.020), KIF20B (0.027), RHOG (0.027), SMG6, FAM50A,
BTN2A2, AOAH. This set is not interferon-related (0/33 ISG enrichment), i.e. it
is a distinct, non-IFN monocyte axis (lipid-antigen handling, small-GTPase and
ubiquitin/proteasome regulation). Robustness: all 73 genes retain p<0.05 when the
cell filter is raised to >=100 or >=300 cells per pseudobulk, and 70/73 overlap
the gene set obtained on plain log2(CPM+1) data (Pearson r = 0.90 between the two
interaction-effect estimates), so the signal is not a normalisation or
low-cell-number artefact.
The SLE responses themselves are large and mostly shared: on quantile-normalised
data 2,608-5,446 genes per cell type are significant in Asian donors and
2,364-5,446 in EA donors, with 1,479-1,962 shared in T cells
(CD4 T: 5,195 Asian / 4,931 EA / 1,962 shared).

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
- The qualitative SLE cell-composition and interferon programmes are shared, so
  there is no evidence for ancestry-restricted selection of the core targets
  (type-I interferon pathway, B/T-cell compartments). Treating Asian and
  European-ancestry SLE as different diseases is not supported.
- The consistent quantitative finding — more severe naive-CD4 loss, higher
  interferon burden and a broader monocyte transcriptional response in Asian
  patients — is a pharmacodynamic / biomarker-stratification signal rather than a
  target-selection signal: it supports measuring baseline IFN activity for
  enrolment or dose decisions in IFN-directed trials, and is compatible with the
  higher SLE incidence, earlier onset and more severe renal disease reported in
  Asian populations.
- Caveat within the data: Asian SLE donors also carry more "flare" labels (9/83
  vs 6/75), so part of the larger effect size may reflect disease activity rather
  than ancestry per se.

WHAT THIS ANALYSIS CANNOT CONCLUDE
- Ancestry is self-reported (HANCESTRO terms); no genotype-based ancestry is in
  the file, so genetic, environmental, healthcare-access and treatment effects
  are inseparable.
- Unequal group sizes (Asian arm 83 SLE vs 24 controls; EA arm 75 vs 74) limit
  power; the Asian arm's control group is small and down-sampling shows part of

DA-16-1 — Can unsupervised clustering of hepatic transcriptomes (GSE135251) stratify NAFLD
patients by disease severity?
=================================================================================================

SHORT ANSWER
------------
Partly, and only after nuisance correction — but the transcriptome structure is a CONTINUOUS
severity gradient, not discrete molecular subtypes.

Unsupervised hierarchical clustering of the 206 NAFLD cases (10 healthy controls excluded) does
produce clusters that differ strongly and ordinally by disease severity, but only once technical
and biological nuisance variation is removed first (RNA quality / % reads assigned to genes,
sequencing batch, library size, inferred sex). Left uncorrected, the dominant axes and the
clusters are technical artefacts that also track sex, and the clustering is NOT a severity
gradient. Even after correction, internal cluster validity is weak (silhouette <= 0.26 at every k;
gap statistic maximal at k = 1) and reproducibility is modest (split-half significant in only 38%
of 200 replications), so these are not demonstrable "molecular subtypes". They are, however, good
enough to enrich a trial for advanced fibrosis, while a supervised expression score would be
better.

DATA AND METHODS (summary; full detail in trace.md)
---------------------------------------------------
- 216 HTSeq count files (64,253 genes after dropping the 5 "__" summary rows each) -> 16,233 genes
  passing >=10 counts in >=25% of samples. 206 NAFLD cases (51 NAFL, 34 NASH_F0-F1, 53 NASH_F2,
  54 NASH_F3, 14 NASH_F4) + 10 controls; fibrosis stage 0-4 = 46/48/54/54/14; NAS 1-8 among cases;
  stage = early (F0-F2, n=138) / moderate (F3-F4, n=68). No sex or age in the GEO metadata, so sex
  was inferred from XIST/Y-chromosome expression (123 male, 93 female).
- Normalization: edgeR TMM + log2 CPM (prior.count=1); DESeq2 VST as sensitivity.
- Pipeline: top-2,000 most variable (MAD) genes -> PCA -> Ward.D2 on Euclidean distance in PC1-5.
- Correction (primary solution): limma::removeBatchEffect on batch (file-name C-prefix proxy),
  % reads assigned to genes, log10 library size and inferred sex, then the same pipeline.
- k selected by silhouette/dendrogram/clinical interpretability (checked, not assumed: k = 2-8
  and 13 further pipeline variants reported).

KEY RESULTS
-----------
Severity is NOT on the first principal components before correction:
  PC1 (17.7% of variance): % reads assigned rho = +0.83, batch rho = -0.48, library size +0.47
                           (technical axis; fibrosis rho = -0.19)
  PC2 (9.2%):  fibrosis rho = +0.60, NAS rho = +0.47  BUT also sex score rho = +0.44
The unadjusted k = 3 clusters were confounded (batch p = 2.7e-12; <70% assignment p = 7.0e-08;
agreement with inferred sex ARI = 0.215; one cluster contained 0 of 85 female cases) and were
not ordinal (NAS Kendall tau = -0.045, p = 0.43).

After correction the severity axis is clean (adjusted PC3: fibrosis rho = -0.62, p = 3.5e-23;
NAS rho = -0.39; sex rho = -0.09, batch rho = 0.01, %assigned rho = 0.02) and k = 3 gives:

  cluster        n    median F   F3-F4    median NAS   NAS>=5   moderate   female%
  mild          89       1       15.7%        4         47.2%     15.7%      41.6
  intermediate  77       2       36.4%        4         46.8%     36.4%      39.0
  severe        40       3       65.0%        6         80.0%     65.0%      45.0

Cluster vs clinical feature (206 cases), Fisher exact Monte-Carlo for the r x c tables,
Kruskal-Wallis for NAS, Kendall tau for the ordinal trend, ordinal logistic LR test for ordering:
  - Fibrosis stage (F0-F4), 5x3                     p = 6.0e-06
  - Early vs moderate grouping, 2x3                 p = 2.0e-07
  - NASH group (NAFL / NASH_F0-F1 / _F2 / _F3 / _F4) p = 4.0e-06
  - NAS score (1-8), Kruskal-Wallis                 p = 1.0e-06
  - Ordered cluster vs NAS, Kendall tau = 0.210     p = 3.0e-04
  - Ordered cluster vs fibrosis, Kendall tau = 0.275 p = 4.2e-06
  - Ordinal logistic LR, fibrosis ~ cluster          p = 2.4e-06 (OR 1.68 intermediate, 5.79 severe
                                                     vs mild)
  - Ordinal logistic LR, NAS ~ cluster given fibrosis p = 8.2e-05 (clusters add NAS information
                                                     beyond fibrosis)
  - Nuisance balance across clusters: batch p = 0.30, inferred sex p = 0.82, library size p = 0.09,
    % reads assigned p = 1.0e-08 but only a 2.2 percentage-point median difference (83.5 vs 81.3%),
    and %assigned does not correlate with fibrosis (rho = -0.09) or NAS (rho = +0.007).

Trial-enrichment value of the "severe" cluster (n = 40):
  advanced fibrosis (F3-F4) 26/40 = 65.0% vs 33.0% cohort-wide and 25.3% in the remaining cases;
  OR = 5.48 (p = 4.0e-06; conservative Bonferroni over scanned solutions x clusters p = 1.7e-04);
  sensitivity 0.38, specificity 0.90, PPV 0.65, NPV 0.75. For NAS >= 5: 80.0% vs 63.6% overall
  (OR 4.51). Moderate-stage (F3-F4) grouping: identical to advanced fibrosis (same labels).

Biology of the severe cluster (limma severe vs mild, 227 genes at BH p < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1;
sex-chromosome genes excluded): up = AKR1B10 (log2FC 2.78), CCL20 (2.46), LUM (1.67), THY1 (1.54),
CLDN11 (1.47), MMP7 (1.44), SPP1 (1.39), SAA1 (1.13), CXCL10 (1.00), IGFBP7 (0.97), ITGA2 (0.94),
MMP2 (0.92), COL1A2 (0.90), IL32 (0.88), KRT7 (0.84), COL1A1 (0.72), COL3A1 (0.67), CXCL9 (0.67),
CCN2/CTGF (0.63), ACTA2 (0.63), DCN (0.59), AFP (0.44); down = CYP2C19 (-1.37), IGFALS (-1.44),
ZBTB16 (-1.31), CD163 (-0.99), MARCO (-1.24), TGFB1 (-0.50), CYP2E1 (-0.37), ALB (-0.29).
This is the canonical activated hepatic-stellate-cell / myofibroblast + ductular + chemokine
(fibro-inflammatory, matrix-remodelling) programme with reduced differentiated-hepatocyte genes.
The mild cluster is the NAFL / F0-F2 state; the intermediate cluster is a mixture.

WHY THIS IS NOT (YET) A SUBTYPE CLASSIFICATION
----------------------------------------------
1. No statistical support for a discrete number of clusters: mean silhouette <= 0.26 at every k
   (k = 2-6), gap statistic maximal at k = 1, no gap in the dendrogram. k = 3 is a pragmatic
   discretization of a continuum, chosen for clinical interpretability.
2. Modest reproducibility: in 200 random 50/50 split-half replications (cluster one half, assign
   the other by nearest centroid) the held-out fibrosis association was significant in only 38% of
   splits at k = 3 (median p = 0.17; k = 4: 69%, median p = 0.010). Bootstrap Jaccard stability of
   the k = 3 partition: 0.64 / 0.39 / 0.72. A partition that changes in most random halves is not a
   fixed classifier.
3. Choice sensitivity: 8 of 13 pipeline variants keep a significant fibrosis/stage association
   (incl. VST normalization, PC1+PC4 removal, complete linkage, top-500 genes, PC1-3, PC1-20), but
   average/single linkage produce degenerate splits (199/5/2, 203/1/2; p > 0.3), k-means does not
   reproduce it (fibrosis p = 0.14), and top-1000 / top-5000 variable genes or 10 PCs lose it.
4. Quality dependence: dropping the 19 cases with <70% reads assigned weakens the association to
   borderline (fibrosis p = 0.13 at k = 3; stage p = 0.027, tau = -0.13 at k = 2). Reassuringly,
   the severity gradient survives removal of the residual technical PC1 (k = 2: fibrosis p = 1e-05,
   early/moderate p = 3.8e-10, tau = 0.45), so the clinical signal is not the technical axis.
5. No sex or age data: sex was inferred from expression and used as a covariate (XIST appears among
   the down-regulated genes in the severe cluster because it is 55% male vs 58% male in mild); age
   could not be adjusted at all. Controls (n = 10) do not form their own cluster (7/10 fall in the
   intermediate cluster), consistent with a continuum rather than distinct healthy/disease states.
6. Cluster-defining and cluster-testing used the same data; the split-half and sensitivity analyses
   mitigate but do not remove this, and no external validation cohort was available.
7. Cross-sectional design: nothing here predicts progression, and bulk tissue composition
   (steatosis, inflammatory infiltrate, biopsy sampling) cannot be separated from true
   disease-severity biology.

PRACTICAL CONCLUSION FOR CLINICAL-TRIAL ENRICHMENT
--------------------------------------------------
- Unsupervised transcriptome clustering is only usable after explicit correction of RNA quality,
  batch and sex; the naive analysis would have enriched trials for technical artefacts.
- The corrected 3-cluster solution gives a severe subgroup with 65% advanced fibrosis (OR 5.5,
  specificity 90%) but low sensitivity (38%), and the subgroups are not reproducible enough to be
  treated as molecular subtypes.
- The transcriptome nevertheless carries strong severity information: a supervised model on the
  same adjusted PCs reaches cross-validated AUC 0.875 (SD 0.005) for F3-F4 (and 0.758 for NAS >= 5),
  versus AUC 0.698 for the NAS score itself and 0.625 for the unsupervised cluster-ordering rule.
  Recommendation: use a continuous supervised transcriptomic severity score (with external
  validation) rather than unsupervised clusters for trial enrichment; treat "NAFLD molecular
  subtypes" in this cohort as a gradient of fibro-inflammatory activity, not discrete classes.
grader_notes: The agent performed a thorough, rigorous analysis that meets most criteria at the highest level, with the only shortfall being lack of multiple-testing correction for the primary cluster-vs-feature association tests.

shared, directionally concordant programme. Genes significant in at least one week: 657/766 female (85.8%),

3) THE FOUR PREDOMINANT TEMPORAL PATTERNS
(a) LATE-ONSET / PROGRESSIVE (largest class): female 287/766, male 315/766 genes significant only at 4-8w.
    251/766 male transcripts (32.8%) are significant ONLY at 8w (females: 84/766 = 11.0%); 36 of those 251 are
    never significant in females at any week (male-exclusive late module: Cfi +2.41, Myl6bl1 +1.92, F2 +1.74,
    Lipg +1.23, Herc6 +1.04, Lyplal1 +0.97, Tenm2 +0.94, plus down: Itm2a -0.49, Col5a2 -0.49, Casp7 -0.46).
(b) SUSTAINED FROM 1w (female-rich): pattern 1111 (sig at all four weeks) in 132 female vs 29 male genes;
    class "sustained (early+late)" 329 female vs 145 male.
(c) EARLY-ONLY / TRANSIENT (small in both sexes, female-shifted): 41 female vs 47 male genes, e.g. Mki67
    (+1.05 at 1w p=0.025, +2.11 at 2w p<1e-4, then non-significant).
(d) SEX-OPPOSITE PROGRAMMES: 255 female-only and 105 male-only genes; ~40-45% of these point in the direction
    OPPOSITE to the other sex. The canonical example is the ECM/collagen module (see 4).

4) BIOLOGICAL MODULES CARRYING THE SIGNAL
- Mitochondrial OXPHOS (41 transcripts: Nduf*, Sdhb, Cox*, Atp5*, Idh2, Idh3b): the archetypal SHARED LATE,
  FEMALE-DOMINANT module. Nothing significant at 1w in either sex; at 4w 41/41 significant in females vs 18/41
  in males (8w: 41/41 vs 10/41). Module mean log2FC +0.32 (F, 4w) / +0.26 (M, 4w). Examples: Cox4i1 F +0.34
  (p=0.0002) / M +0.26 (p=0.062); Atp5mc1 F +0.50 (p<1e-4); Ndufb4 F +0.30 (p=0.0015).
- Apelin/angiogenesis, FEMALE-BIASED AND EARLY: Apln F +0.60 (p=0.035) at 1w, +1.07 (p=0.0003) at 2w, +0.96,
  +0.93 (pattern 1111) vs M +0.38/0.43/0.82/0.66 (significant only at 8w). Receptor Aplnr female-significant
  from 2w (p=0.0006), never in males (sex-difference FDR 0.015 at 2w). Vegfb female-only, late (+0.44 at 4w,
  p=0.0001; male +0.16 n.s.).
- Myoglobin, SHARED LATE with earlier female onset: Mb F +0.21 (p=0.090) -> +0.33 (p=0.012) -> +0.76 (p<1e-4)
  -> +0.70 (p<1e-4); M -0.07 -> -0.08 -> +0.30 (n.s.) -> +0.67 (p=0.027). Same endpoint, ~4 weeks earlier in females.
- ECM/collagen, SEX-OPPOSITE (the clearest sex-specific result): module (12 genes, Col1a1/5a1/5a2/6a1/6a6/8a2/
  11a1, Lox, Fbln1, Cilp, Emilin3, Tnmd) mean log2FC female +0.65 (1w), +0.83 (2w) vs male -0.90, -1.35, -1.55
  (1w, 2w, 4w). At 4w 10/12 genes significant in males, 0/12 in females. Individual: Col11a1 F +2.02 (p=0.0045)
  vs M -1.73 (p=0.0034), sex-difference p=0.0001; Tnmd F +1.73 vs M -2.13 (p=0.0002); Lox female n.s. (p=0.34)
  vs male -1.10/-1.72/-1.71 across 1-4w; Col8a2, Fbln1, Pla2g2a, Cilp, Col5a1/5a2, Meox1 behave the same way.
- Sarco(endo)plasmic reticulum, LATE SEX-OPPOSITE at 8w: Sln (sarcolipin) M +2.44 at 8w (p=0.001, pattern 0001)
  vs F -0.83 (p=0.131); sex-difference p=0.0005. Casq1 (F -0.38 p=0.0003 vs M n.s.) and Pvalb (F -0.52
  p=0.0005 vs M n.s.) follow the female; Kcnma1 (+0.62 F / +1.09 M) and Smtnl1 (+0.59 F / +1.00 M) rise in both.
- IEG/stress, SHARED EARLY SUPPRESSION (flat, not progressive): Fos down at every week in both sexes (F -1.18 to
  -1.61, p<=0.0003; M -1.02 to -1.48, p<=0.033, pattern 1111 in both); Egr1 down (F -1.12 at 8w; M -1.63 at 4w,
  p=0.0001); Hspb1 modestly down in both.
- Muscle/metabolic markers: Ckmt1 is the largest shared up-regulated gene (F +2.10/1.79/3.29/2.46; M +4.09/4.94/
  4.33/3.75), with Ckmt2 (F 1111, M 0011). Fhl1 rises late in both (F +0.90, M +0.89 at 8w). Hspb6 rises from 1w
  in females (all p<=1e-4) but only at 8w in males. Slc2a4 (GLUT4) significant at 8w in females and from 2w in
  males; Tbc1d1 is early and sustained in both (pattern F 0111, M 1110).
- Unsupervised confirmation (k-means on z-scored 8-value trajectories, k=5 chosen by silhouette 0.287 and the
  inertia elbow): cluster 3 = ECM/collagen (9/12 panel genes), cluster 4 = OXPHOS (39/41; significant in 154/154
  females vs 83/154 males), cluster 2 = female-early/male-late convergence (203 genes incl. Fhl1, Flt4, Acads,
  Ier3), cluster 1 = female early/progressive down + male late down (226 genes), cluster 0 = sex-opposite with
  late male up (104 genes incl. Tnfrsf12a, Prg4, Btg2).

5) DIRECT SEX-DIFFERENCE TEST (z = dlog2FC / sqrt(SE_F^2 + SE_M^2), BH within week)
Genes differing between sexes at FDR<0.05: 11 at 1w, 47 at 2w, 0 at 4w, 0 at 8w (nominal p<0.05: 116, 184, 71, 77).
Sex divergence is therefore an EARLY phenomenon; the sexes converge in direction by 4-8w. The only large 8w
exception is Sln (female -0.83 vs male +2.44, p=0.0005) plus the unmapped transcript ENSRNOG00000053790
(female ~0 vs male +3.53/+4.99; sex-difference FDR<0.004).

6) ROBUSTNESS OF THE "FEMALE IS EARLIER/BROADER" CLAIM
At MATCHED effect size (|log2FC| >= 0.4) the number of such genes is female 143/180/283/203 vs male 134/155/155/212
(1w-8w), and the fraction of them that are significant is female 0.706/0.778/0.834/0.877 vs male 0.664/0.574/0.606/
0.774. Females therefore have both more large-effect genes at 2-4w AND a higher detection rate at 2-4w, so the
pattern is not explained by their smaller SEs alone; the male deficit narrows but does not vanish at 8w.

ANSWER (one paragraph)
Endurance training remodels the SKM-VL transcriptome biphasically. In females, the response is broad and early:
220 transcripts at 1w rising to 501 by 4w and then saturating (532 at 8w), with the largest mean effect at 4w, an
apelin/angiogenesis and myoglobin signal starting in weeks 1-2, an early ECM/collagen-induction, and a late
(4w) mitochondrial OXPHOS induction that is nearly complete in females (41/41 genes). In males the response is
narrow and late: essentially flat for 4 weeks (145/134/176), then a 2.2-fold expansion at 8w (379), 32.8% of
male transcripts being regulated only at 8w; the male OXPHOS module is only ~half as complete (18/41 at 4w) and
male ECM/collagen genes are coordinately SUPPRESSED (-1.35 to -1.55 mean log2FC at 2-4w) where females are
induced. Predominant shared patterns are (i) late-onset/progressive, peaking at 8w, and (ii) sustained
first-week-onset (female-rich) plus (iii) a shared early, flat suppression of immediate-early/stress genes
(Fos, Egr1, Hspb1). Predominant sex-specific patterns are (iv) the early sex-opposite ECM/collagen programme and
(v) late sex-opposite sarcolipin at 8w, with (vi) transient early proliferation (Mki67) female-shifted. Sex
overlap is minimal at 1-2w (Jaccard 0.09-0.10; shared log2FC correlation ~0 at 2w) and maximal at 8w (Jaccard
0.41; 265 shared genes of which 264 move in the same direction; cross-sex log2FC correlation 0.63), and direct
sex-difference testing finds no FDR-significant sex difference at 4w or 8w versus 58 genes at 1-2w. The two
sexes therefore reach a largely shared 8-week adaptive end-state (mitochondrial biogenesis, oxygen transport,
apelin signalling) by different routes and at different speeds, with a small set of genuinely opposite
exceptions, most notably extracellular-matrix/collagen and sarcolipin.

LIMITATIONS
- Only differential-analysis summary statistics are distributed (one log2FC/SE/p per gene x sex x week); there is
  no per-sample data, so the original models, sample sizes and covariates cannot be re-fitted or verified.
- The input list is pre-filtered to genes with training_q < 0.05 (omnibus, pooled over sexes); genes regulated in
  only one sex may be absent from the table, biasing sex-specific counts downwards and shared counts upwards.
- Pattern calls use nominal p<0.05; under within-week BH FDR the counts fall (e.g. shared 8w genes 265 -> 146)
  but all qualitative conclusions are unchanged.
- Sex-difference testing is a normal approximation using the published SEs (assumes independent, Gaussian sex-
  specific contrasts) and cannot replace the design-based sex x training interaction; the "0 genes at 4w/8w"
  partly reflects the conservative male SE.
- No multiple-testing-corrected pathway enrichment was attempted (the pre-filtered input invalidates the standard
  background); module assignments are small hand-curated symbol-based sets (n = 3-41) and are descriptive.
- Rat treadmill endurance training, one muscle, transcript level only; no protein/phospho/metabolite corroboration
  for SKM-VL was used, and no causal or human clinical claim is warranted.
- 72/766 transcripts (9.4%) could not be mapped to a gene symbol (retired Ensembl rat IDs), including two of the
  largest-amplitude genes (ENSRNOG00000057456, +2.79 F / +2.21 M at 8w; ENSRNOG00000000768, -2.01 F / -4.80 M at 8w).
