Baseline circulating T-cell biomarkers for 1-year overall survival in patients
receiving nivo/chemo (PRINCE / PICI0002, randomised arm A1 = nivolumab +
gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel)
================================================================================

COHORT
------
25 of the 34 patients randomised to arm A1 (74%) have a baseline (C1D1) CyTOF
sample: 14 deaths, median OS 445 days, Kaplan-Meier 1-year OS = 62.4%.
Binary 1-year OS endpoint is defined for 21 of them (13 alive at >=365 days,
8 deaths <365 days; 4 patients censored before 365 days are excluded).
Cox models use all 25 patients / 14 events.

ANSWER: THE CANDIDATE BASELINE BIOMARKERS
-----------------------------------------
Four circulating T-cell populations measured at baseline are associated with
1-year overall survival in the nivo/chemo arm. They form two opposing axes.

Axis 1 - HIGHER at baseline = BETTER 1-year survival (a Th1 / NKT / gd-T axis)

1. Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells (% of TCRgd T cells)  -- strongest single marker
   median 0.883 in 1-year survivors vs 0.704 in patients who died <1 yr
   (AUC 0.79, Mann-Whitney p = 0.030)
   Cox HR per 1 SD of log10 frequency = 0.31 (95% CI 0.16-0.60), p = 0.00047,
   FDR q = 0.003; median-split 1-year OS 0.81 (high) vs 0.45 (low),
   log-rank p = 0.025. Stable in leave-one-out (18/21 folds p<0.05).

2. NKT cells (% of leukocytes)
   median 1.98% in survivors vs 0.49% in patients who died <1 yr (4.0-fold,
   AUC 0.87, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0045, FDR q = 0.016)
   Cox HR per SD = 0.48 (0.28-0.83), p = 0.0084, FDR q = 0.030;
   median-split 1-year OS 0.90 (high) vs 0.36 (low), log-rank p = 0.0049.
   Most robust marker (21/21 leave-one-out folds p<0.05).

3. Tbet+ T cells (% of CD3+ cells)   -- suggestive only
   median 0.183 vs 0.106 (AUC 0.75, Mann-Whitney p = 0.064)
   Cox HR per SD = 0.54 (0.31-0.95), p = 0.033, FDR q = 0.076;
   median-split 1-year OS 0.81 vs 0.45, log-rank p = 0.011.
   Least stable marker (only 4/21 leave-one-out folds p<0.05) - treat as
   hypothesis-generating.

Axis 2 - HIGHER at baseline = WORSE 1-year survival

4. Ki-67+ T cells (% of CD3+ cells)  (fraction of T cells that are proliferating)
   median 0.933 in survivors vs 0.983 in patients who died <1 yr
   (AUC 0.125, i.e. 0.875 in the reverse direction; Mann-Whitney p = 0.0034,
   FDR q = 0.016)
   Cox HR per SD = 2.28 (1.02-5.09), p = 0.044, FDR q = 0.077;
   median-split 1-year OS 0.33 (high) vs 1.00 (low), log-rank p = 0.010.
   At the patient level: all 8 patients who died within 1 year had a baseline
   Ki-67+ T-cell fraction at or above the cohort median (0.966), and no patient
   below the median died within 1 year (9 alive at 1 year, 3 censored before).

Composite (pre-specified, equal-weight)
   A "Th1/NKT activation score" = mean z(log10 NKT, log10 Tbet+ T,
   log10 Tbet+ gd T) - z(log10 Ki-67+ T) separates the groups better than any
   single marker: AUC 0.885, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0025, log-rank p = 0.019,
   Cox HR 0.56 per SD (0.36-0.87), p = 0.010; 1-year OS ~0.87 (high) vs ~0.42
   (low). In the control arm receiving sotigalimab + chemo without anti-PD-1
   the same score is null (AUC 0.52, p = 0.90).

POPULATIONS THAT ARE NOT BASELINE BIOMARKERS HERE
-------------------------------------------------
HLA-DR+ T cells (% of leukocytes) (p = 0.92; Cox p = 0.29), HLA-DR+ non-naive
CD4 T cells (p = 0.92), HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells (p = 0.86). In an
exploratory sweep of all 13 populations with baseline data, also null:
HLA-DR+ plasmablasts, CD40+ pDC, CD14+ HLA-DRlo m-MDSC, CD1C+ CD141+ DC,
HLA-DR+ CCR7+ B cells and CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells (all p >= 0.21).

TREATMENT SPECIFICITY / CONSISTENCY
-----------------------------------
Across cohorts (two-sided Mann-Whitney p for 1-year OS; B2 = no anti-PD-1):
  NKT cells         A1 0.0045 | all nivo (A1+C2) 0.047 | C2 0.86 | B2 0.94
  Ki-67+ T cells    A1 0.0034 | 0.31 | 0.38 | 0.34
  Tbet+ gd T cells  A1 0.030  | 0.10 | 0.52 | 0.0021
  HLA-DR+ T cells   A1 0.92   | 0.057 | 0.011 | 0.30
The NKT-cell and Ki-67+ T-cell associations are the ones most consistent with
an anti-PD-1-containing regimen (they do not reproduce in the sotigalimab-only
arm). The Tbet+ TCRgd+ T-cell association is also present without anti-PD-1
(B2 p = 0.0021), so it is more likely a shared PROGNOSTIC indicator of a
Th1-competent circulating compartment than a nivolumab-specific biomarker.
In the pooled all-nivolumab cohort (n=51) the direction is unchanged but weaker
(NKT p = 0.047; composite HR 0.80, p = 0.049), and Ki-67+ T cells lose
significance (p = 0.31).

INTERPRETATION
--------------
A baseline peripheral compartment enriched for innate-like NKT cells and
T-bet+ (Th1/effector) gd T cells, and with a low fraction of cycling CD3+ T
cells, marks patients more likely to be alive at 1 year on nivo/chemo
(1-year OS ~0.81-1.00 in the favourable half vs ~0.33-0.45 in the unfavourable
half). A high baseline Ki-67+ T-cell fraction is the adverse counterpart; it is
strongly anti-correlated with NKT and T-bet+ frequencies (Spearman rho = -0.91
and -0.70 within arm A1), and joint Cox models show it is not independent of the
Th1/NKT axis, so it is best read as one end of a single differentiation axis
rather than a separate mechanism.

LIMITATIONS
-----------
Single small cohort (25 patients, 14 events; 21 with a defined binary endpoint),
no validation set, wide confidence intervals, no interaction test for
treatment-specificity, 4 patients censored before 365 days excluded from the
binary endpoint, no adjustment beyond age and ECOG (both unassociated), and
markers are compositional percentages (no absolute counts). These are
ASSOCIATIVE prognostic/stratification candidates, not validated predictive
biomarkers of nivolumab benefit.

Full methods, code and intermediate statistics: trace.md
Analysis module: analysis/baseline-tcell-os/ (scripts, tables, README)
Primary figure: analysis/baseline-tcell-os/output/figures/fig1_baseline_tcell_1yrOS_armA1.png

Question: Do feminizing GAHT-associated proteins overlap with sex-associated proteins identified in
the general population?

ANSWER: Yes - the overlap is large, highly significant, and directionally consistent, but it is
partial rather than complete.

KEY NUMBERS
- Analysis universe: 2,606 proteins measured on both Olink platforms (Supplementary Table 5), i.e.
  the proteins with both a UKB-PPP sex statistic (Sun et al., Nature 2023) and a GAHT effect estimate.
- GAHT-associated proteins: 213/2,606 with CPA adjusted p < 0.05 (245/5,279 across the full Olink
  Explore-HT panel) and 81/2,606 with SPIRO adjusted p < 0.05 (91/5,279); 259 in either arm.
- Sex-associated proteins in the same universe: 2,322 (89.1%) at BH FDR < 5%, 2,017 (77.4%) at
  Bonferroni, and 1,387 (53.2%) at a stringent -log10 p > 23.

OVERLAP AND ENRICHMENT (Fisher exact, two-sided)
- Strong sex association (-log10 p > 23): 172/213 = 80.8% of CPA-associated proteins (OR = 4.07,
  p = 4.1e-18) and 68/81 = 84.0% of SPIRO-associated proteins (OR = 4.78, p = 5.2e-9); either arm
  208/259 = 80.3% (OR = 4.04, p = 2.5e-21).
- Bonferroni: 193/213 = 90.6% (CPA) and 75/81 = 92.6% (SPIRO).
- BH FDR < 5%: 205/213 = 96.2% (CPA) and 79/81 = 97.5% (SPIRO).
- Reverse direction: 12.4% of strongly sex-associated proteins change with GAHT vs 3.4% of the rest.
- GAHT-affected proteins are more sexually dimorphic (median |female beta| 0.320 vs 0.197).

DIRECTION: feminizing GAHT tends to move proteins toward the female level
- Spearman rho(GAHT effect, female-vs-male beta) = 0.184 (CPA) and 0.361 (SPIRO) over 1,390 shared
  proteins (p = 4.9e-12 and 4.6e-44); among GAHT-significant proteins rho = 0.489 (n = 173) and
  0.513 (n = 68).
- Sign concordance among doubly significant proteins: 109/172 (63.4%) for CPA with a strong
  sign-independence Fisher test (OR = 14.5, p = 0.0017), and 52/68 (76.5%) for SPIRO.
- Concordance is strongest for the most sexually dimorphic proteins (77.0% for -log10 p > 300) and
  weak for marginally sex-associated ones (33-44%).
- The overlap is dominated by androgen-driven male reproductive-tract proteins that collapse on
  antiandrogen treatment: SPINT3 (CPA -7.90 NPX; female beta -1.58), INSL3 (-5.35; -1.57), EDDM3B
  (-2.64; -1.54), ACRV1 (-1.39; -1.53), TEX101 (-2.09; -1.44), PROK1, MMP3, OBP2B, CRISP2. LEP/leptin
  is female-higher and rises further (CPA +1.47; beta +1.14).

EXCEPTIONS (the overlap is real but not 1:1)
- 41/213 (19.2%) CPA-associated proteins show no strong sex association at all (e.g. IL6R, MCAM,
  EDN1, CD101, C1QTNF1, CCL25, CR2, VCAM1, LDLR, SELENOP, TNFSF10), suggesting a component of the
  6-month response that is unrelated to the female phenotype.
- 63/172 (36.6%) doubly significant proteins move in the opposite direction to the population sex
  difference - mostly female-higher proteins that fall on GAHT (e.g. DIPK2B, TFPI2, KLKB1/plasma
  kallikrein, FASLG, OPTC, FGF23) plus NOS3, which rises despite being male-higher.
- Several of the most female-elevated proteins in the general population do not respond to GAHT:
  PZP (beta +1.38, CPA p = 0.35) and FSHB (beta +1.29, CPA p = 0.40).

INTERPRETATION
The GAHT-associated plasma proteome is strongly enriched for proteins that differ between women and
men in the general population (~4-fold, p down to 1e-21), and for the most sexually dimorphic
proteins the direction of 6-month change under feminizing GAHT matches the female direction,
consistent with androgen withdrawal and estrogen exposure driving those proteins. A substantial
minority of GAHT-responsive proteins, however, carry no sex difference, and a further subset moves
opposite to the population sex difference, indicating contributions from pharmacology, body
composition/lipid and inflammatory biology, or from sex differences that are not hormone-dependent.

LIMITATIONS
Small cohort (n = 20 per arm; only 37/299 proteins significant in both regimens); effect estimates
are pre-computed adjusted p-values, not re-derived; only 2,606 of 5,279 HT proteins have UKB-PPP sex
statistics (32 CPA- and 10 SPIRO-significant proteins unassessable, and KLK3/PSA, CGA, ADIPOQ, MB have
no GAHT data); the female-vs-male effect size column is corrupted (#REF!) for the 1,269 weakest
sex-associated proteins, so signs are available for only 1,442 proteins; overlapping statistical
associations do not establish causality, and both regimens combine estradiol with an antiandrogen, so
hormone-specific drivers cannot be disentangled.
grader_notes: The agent performed a comprehensive and reproducible analysis with minor deviations from the rubric's expected protocol (using thresholds instead of top 100 for sex-associated proteins), but the methodology is sound and the conclusions are well-supported.

INDIVIDUAL VARIATIONS IN GLYCEMIC RESPONSES (DA-8-3)
Top-10 differentially abundant metabolites (potato-spikers vs grape-spikers) and their
mediation of the group differences in insulin resistance and beta-cell function
=====================================================================================

HOW THE GROUPS WERE DEFINED (no spiker label is supplied in the data)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Spiker phenotype was reconstructed from the CGM challenge curves: for each participant and
each unmitigated challenge meal (mitigator = NaN) I computed baseline glucose (-25..-5 min),
then the baseline-corrected peak rise (peak_inc) over 0-120 min, averaged replicates, and
assigned each participant to the food with the largest rise (23,520 CGM rows -> 16,000
unmitigated rows -> 10,000 postprandial rows -> 400 participant x food x replicate curves,
38 participants, 9 foods).

Whole-cohort assignment: Rice 14, Bread 8, Grapes 6, Potatoes 4, Pasta 3, Quinoa 2, Glucose 1.

Among the participants who also have metabolomics data:
   potato-spikers = XB111, XB2, XB21, XB38        (n = 4 participants; 15 samples)
   grape-spikers  = XB6, XB79                     (n = 2 participants; 10 samples)

These two groups differ clinically in the expected direction: the potato-spikers are more
insulin-resistant and have lower beta-cell function (SSPG 225 +/- 45 vs 64 +/- 16 mg/dL,
Welch p = 0.015, n = 3 vs 2; HOMA-IR 3.00 vs 1.59; DI 0.94 vs 2.59), but they are also older
(62.1 vs 47.0 y) and heavier (BMI 29.1 vs 25.1 kg/m2), so these are descriptive contrasts.

PART 1 - TOP 10 DIFFERENTIALLY ABUNDANT METABOLITES (potato-spikers vs grape-spikers)
=====================================================================================

Independent support for the mediator->outcome (b) path, from the whole cohort
This is the one leg of the mediation model that can be tested with more participants, and it supports
the LPC class (the class the top-ranked feature belongs to), not any individual significance:

Direction: higher circulating LPC -> lower insulin resistance and higher beta-cell function, i.e. the
direction the mediation model would require. What remains unestablished is the a-path / indirect
effect in the 6-participant spiker contrast.

BOTTOM LINE
=====================================================================================
1. Top-10 differentially abundant metabolites between potato- and grape-spikers (768 QC-passing
   features, FDR < 1.1e-3 for all ten): LPC 18:0 (FC 0.47, down), Cys-Pro or Pro-Cys (0.62),

   5-acetylamino-6-amino-3-methyluracil (3.13), propazine (0.25), theobromine (4.33) and
   CAR 6:0 (1.76). The pattern is a low-LPC / high-saturated-TAG / high-acylcarnitine /
   high-BCAA signature of insulin resistance, independently reproduced in the lipidomics matrix.

2. The lipid species among them - LPC 18:0, testosterone sulfate and CAR 6:0 - do NOT statistically
   mediate the group differences. Only one of them (testosterone sulfate, for beta-cell function,
   indirect -0.96 on DI, 95% CI [-2.04, 0.00], p_boot = 0.049) even reaches nominal significance, is
   the only one with sign-consistent mediation for all three outcomes, and it is not significant
   after FDR (FDR = 0.44) nor robust to the bootstrap seed. LPC 18:0 has the largest point estimates
   (-7.42 on HOMA-IR, -151.8 mg/dL on SSPG) but with the WRONG sign relative to the group
   differences (inconsistent mediation), and its fitted mediator->outcome coefficients (+23.15,
   +452.0) contradict the well-powered cohort LPC-outcome association (r = -0.51 to -0.56) - a
   saturated-fit artefact of 5-6 observations with a nearly collinear mediator. CAR 6:0 is
   suppressive for HOMA-IR. No mediator survives multiple-testing correction, in the top-10 or in
   the full 768-metabolite scan (minimum FDR-corrected p = 0.44). With 4 vs 2 participants the
   contrast is simply too small: the confidence intervals are wide enough to be compatible both
   with a modest true mediation and with none.

3. What the data do support: circulating lysophosphatidylcholines are lower and saturated
   triacylglycerols/acylcarnitines higher in the more insulin-resistant, beta-cell-compromised
   potato-spiker phenotype, and the LPC-outcome leg reproduces in the full cohort (n = 28-35,
   age/BMI-adjusted, higher LPC -> lower HOMA-IR/SSPG and higher DI). The observed pattern is
   therefore COMPATIBLE WITH mediation by the LPC class, but the mediation itself is not
   demonstrated. Establishing it would require a much larger spiker cohort, prospective sampling,
   and validated lipid identifications.

Question: Are the myeloid detrimental genes and lymphoid protective genes correlated
within each gene set?

ANSWER: Yes. Within both gene sets the member genes are positively and significantly
co-expressed across the 3,948 sepsis patients. The effect is much stronger for the
lymphoid protective set than for the myeloid detrimental set.

Myeloid detrimental set (27 genes, 351 unique gene pairs)
  - mean pairwise Pearson r = +0.240 (median +0.206, IQR 0.072-0.390)
  - 84.3% of pairs positive; 36.2% with r > 0.3; 91.7% of pairs at BH-FDR q < 0.05
  - test of mean Fisher-z against 0: t = 16.8, p = 8.7e-47
  - vs the 20,100-pair background of all profiled genes (mean r = +0.150): +0.09,
    Mann-Whitney p = 2.5e-8
  - random-set null (10,000 random 27-gene subsets): observed 0.240 vs 0.150 +/- 0.031,
    z = +2.9, empirical p = 0.006
  - strongest pairs: AQP9-BCL6 0.90, CEACAM8-LTF 0.87, BCL6-ANXA3 0.86, BCL6-KLHL2 0.86,
    LCN2-LTF 0.86
  - the set is a composite: a mod1-like cluster (BCL6, AQP9, ANXA3, KLHL2, ORM1, SLPI, TYK2)
    has mean r = +0.49 and a granulocyte/neutrophil-granule cluster (DEFA4, CTSG, LCN2,
    CEACAM8, CAMP, AZU1, CEP55, HMMR, KIF15, PRC1...) mean r = +0.36, while the 10
    composite-specific genes (ARG1, LTF, OLFM4, CRISP2, HTRA1, PPL, SLC1A5, STX1A,
    GADD45A, STOM) average only +0.19 - this dilution, not absence of co-expression,
    explains why the myeloid mean sits closer to the background.

Lymphoid protective set (29 genes, 406 unique gene pairs)
  - mean pairwise Pearson r = +0.497 (median +0.539, IQR 0.402-0.639)
  - 93.6% of pairs positive; 57.9% with r > 0.5; 98.5% of pairs at BH-FDR q < 0.05
  - test of mean Fisher-z against 0: t = 38.5, p = 1.7e-137
  - vs background: +0.35, Mann-Whitney p = 4.7e-102
  - random-set null: observed 0.497 vs 0.150 +/- 0.029, z = +11.8, empirical p < 1e-4
  - strongest pairs: CAMK4-DYRK2 0.89, CD3E-CD3G 0.88, CD3E-CD247 0.85, DYRK2-PLCG1 0.85,
    CAMK4-CD3G 0.84
  - PC1 explains 55.5% of the set's variance, i.e. it behaves as one coherent T/NK
    co-expression axis (lymphocyte abundance/function), not a loose collection.

Robustness (mean within-set r)
  - all 6 cohorts analysed separately: myeloid 0.14-0.36, lymphoid 0.28-0.66; positive in
    every cohort
  - within-cohort Fisher-z pooled: myeloid +0.216 (p = 2.3e-40), lymphoid +0.472 (p = 5.3e-147)
  - cohort-mean centred: +0.201 (p = 2.1e-38) / +0.438 (p = 7.8e-142)
  - Spearman rho: +0.223 / +0.526
  - partial correlation controlling for the global immune axis (mean z of all 201 genes):
    +0.217 (p = 5.3e-39) / +0.413 (p = 2.0e-104), whereas the same control collapses the
    background to -0.005 (p = 0.48)
  - alternative set definition (mod1+mod2 / mod3+mod4): +0.262 / +0.265
  - every set size from k = 10 to k = 40 on the loading ranking gives a positive mean
    (myeloid 0.50 -> 0.21; lymphoid 0.74 -> 0.24)

Context: the two sets are anti-correlated with each other (mean cross-set r = -0.134;
only 28.5% of the 783 between-set pairs positive; corr(myeloid_detrimental_score,
lymphoid_protective_score) = -0.40). So "detrimental" vs "protective" is a between-set
opposition, not a within-set one - inside each set the genes move together.

Interpretation: the myeloid detrimental set is an emergency-myelopoiesis / immature
granulocyte programme (DEFA4, CTSG, AZU1, CAMP, LCN2, LTF, OLFM4, CEACAM8/CD66b, ARG1)
whose members share granule-biogenesis regulation; the lymphoid protective set is a
canonical T/NK module (CD3E, CD3G, CD247, ZAP70, CAMK4, MAP4K1, PLCG1, KLRB1, NCR3 and
lymphocyte-restricted transcripts) whose co-expression is dominated by a single
lymphocyte-abundance axis.

Limitations: bulk transcriptomes mean shared cell-type abundance cannot be separated from
true co-regulation without deconvolution; the sets were reconstructed from the score
columns (validated at r ~ 0.99 against the published scores and by exact recovery of the
mod1-mod4 blocks); gene pairs are not independent units, so the empirical random-set null
is the more honest p value; no clinical/outcome claim is made.

HOW "PATHOGENIC/ONCOGENIC ONLY" WAS DEFINED
--------------------------------------------
The supplied MAF contains NO pathogenicity/oncogenicity annotation column: the
string "pathogenic" occurs 0 times in the file, and "oncogenic" only 7 times
(inside PIK3CA free text). Hotspot = 0 for all 40,731 rows and Validation_Status
is empty, so neither can serve as a flag. Pathogenic/oncogenic was therefore
operationalised as PROTEIN-ALTERING (non-synonymous) variant class:
missense, nonsense, nonstop, frameshift ins/del, in-frame ins/del, splice-site
and translation-start-site. Excluded: Silent (9,427 calls), RNA (1,737), Intron
(1,303), UTR/flank (379) and Splice_Region (346).

1) TOP MUTATED GENES
--------------------
(a) Raw protein-altering frequency (% of 498 patients):
    FRG1B 19.5 | TTN 12.7 | TP53 12.0 | SPOP 11.4 | MUC16 7.6 | MUC17 6.6 |

    shift even though single genes mostly are not significant.
  * CONFOUNDING AND NULL RESULTS: TP53-mutant tumours are higher grade (mean
    Gleason 8.33 vs 7.51), so after adjustment for age and Gleason the TP53
    effect is attenuated (OR 1.33, 95% CI 0.61-2.92, p = 0.47) while Gleason
    dominates (OR 1.90 per unit, p = 1e-4). Tumour mutational burden does NOT
    differ by stage (median 31/33/35/30 protein-altering variants for T1/T2/T3/T4;
    Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.42), so this is not a hypermutation effect. mRNA levels
    of TP53, FOXA1, SPOP and ATM are identical between T1/T2 and T3/T4
    (p = 0.93, 0.71, 0.51, 0.75 in the matched RSEM matrix) - the association is
    genomic, not transcriptional.

BOTTOM LINE
-----------
1. Pathogenic/oncogenic (protein-altering) TCGA-PRAD mutation landscape:
   TP53 (12.0%), SPOP (11.4%), FOXA1 (5.6%), PTEN (3.4%), ATM (4.4%),
   KMT2D (5.8%), KMT2C (6.0%), PIK3CA (2.8%), CTNNB1 (2.6%), KDM6A (2.6%),
   followed by rare APC/BRCA2/CDK12/MED12/CHD1/IDH1/NKX3-1 events. The raw
   top-20 is led by FRG1B, TTN, MUC16 and CHEK2, all of which are artefacts or
   length-driven passengers rather than drivers.
2. Visualisation: OncoPrint, ranked frequency lollipop/bar, length-corrected
   enrichment plot and hotspot lollipops are all provided (fig1-fig3), plus the
   T-stage figure (fig4).
3. Clinical T stage: no gene survives FDR on clinical T stage, but TP53 is the
   strongest genomic correlate (trend p = 0.0075) and is the ONLY gene that
   survives FDR (q = 0.037) on the independent pathological T-stage endpoint
   (pT3/T4 16.2% vs pT2 5.9%, OR 3.10), with the SPOP-or-FOXA1 axis moving in
   the opposite direction. The effect is partly explained by Gleason grade.

LIMITATIONS
-----------
Pathogenicity is operationalised from variant class, not from a ClinVar/OncoKB
annotation (none exists in this MAF), so missense variants of unknown
significance remain in the list. No copy-number or fusion data are available,
so PTEN/RB1/CHD1/NKX3-1 losses and TMPRSS2-ERG fusions cannot be counted, and
all mutation frequencies are therefore lower bounds on true driver involvement.
The gene-length expectation is a transparent Poisson approximation, not dNdScv
(no coverage track and only 9,427 silent calls are available), and was used only
to flag passengers. T4 contains just 2 patients, the pathological-T replication
is within the same cohort and is a post-surgical variable, and the TP53-T-stage
association does not survive adjustment for Gleason grade.
grader_notes: The agent performed a thorough analysis with correct dataset characterization and statistical testing, but deviated from the rubric's expected pathogenic definition (no CGC/MUTSIG) and T-stage primary endpoint, leading to minor ranking and endpoint differences.

DA-14-3 — CONSENSUS IMMUNE DYSREGULATION FRAMEWORK FOR SEPSIS
Question: What proportion of critically ill patients fall into each immune dysregulation subgroup?

================================================================================
ANSWER (primary: all patient samples, healthy controls excluded; N = 3,871)
================================================================================

  System-wide immune dysregulation  1,728 / 3,871 = 44.6%  (95% CI 43.1-46.2%)
  Lymphoid dysregulation            1,006 / 3,871 = 26.0%  (95% CI 24.6-27.4%)
  Balanced (no dysregulation)         864 / 3,871 = 22.3%  (95% CI 21.0-23.7%)
  Myeloid dysregulation               273 / 3,871 =  7.1%  (95% CI  6.3-7.9%)

The four subgroups partition the cohort, so the share of patients with dysregulation on at
least one axis (myeloid and/or lymphoid) is 77.7%, and only 22.3% are classified as balanced.

================================================================================
RESULT UNDER ALTERNATIVE, EQUALLY DEFENSIBLE DENOMINATORS
================================================================================

(a) All 3,948 rows of the score table (77 healthy control samples included):
    system-wide 43.8% (1,728) | lymphoid 25.6% (1,009) | balanced 23.7% (935) | myeloid 7.0% (276)

(b) One sample per patient, earliest/baseline timepoint, controls excluded (N = 3,143 patients;
    the strict per-patient denominator):
    system-wide 43.4% (1,363) | lymphoid 30.5% (957) | balanced 21.4% (672) | myeloid 4.8% (151)

(c) Baseline timepoint rows only (N = 3,216):
    system-wide 42.4% | lymphoid 29.9% | balanced 23.0% | myeloid 4.8%

(d) Infected patients only (condition == "infected", N = 2,892):
    system-wide 45.3% | lymphoid 21.8% | balanced 25.4% | myeloid 7.6%

CONSOLIDATED ANSWER: about 44% of critically ill patients show system-wide dysregulation,
26-30% lymphoid dysregulation, 21-24% balanced, and 5-7% myeloid dysregulation. Ordering is
identical under every denominator (system-wide > lymphoid > balanced > myeloid) and the
system-wide share is stable at 42.4-45.3%; only the small myeloid group moves materially
(4.8% at the patient/baseline level vs 7.0-7.1% when follow-up samples are pooled).

================================================================================
HOW THE SUBGROUPS WERE DERIVED (verified from the data, 0/3,948 label mismatches)
================================================================================
subgroup = cross of the two axes, each dichotomised at the one-sided 95th percentile of the
healthy reference (z > 1.65):
  myeloid_z > 1.65 AND lymphoid_z > 1.65  -> system-wide
  myeloid_z > 1.65 AND lymphoid_z <= 1.65 -> myeloid dysregulation
  myeloid_z <= 1.65 AND lymphoid_z > 1.65 -> lymphoid dysregulation
  neither high                            -> balanced
Healthy controls (control.0.class = 0, n = 77) have myeloid/lymphoid z mean 0.005/-0.003 with
SD 0.90/0.98, confirming the z-scores are standardised on healthy blood; 6/77 controls (7.8%)
exceed the cut on one axis, consistent with a 5% one-sided threshold per axis. In patients the
median shift is large: mean myeloid z = 1.88 and mean lymphoid z = 3.30; 51.7% of patient
samples are "high myeloid" and 70.6% "high lymphoid".

================================================================================
WHAT DRIVES THE SPREAD BETWEEN DEFINITIONS
================================================================================
- Cohort heterogeneity is extreme (subgroup x cohort chi-square = 2,191.6, df = 15, p < 1e-300):
  system-wide share ranges from 2.0% (savemore, a COVID-19 cohort that is 78.1% balanced) to
  65.4% (qns31079); myeloid dysregulation reaches 24.4% in the paediatric cchmc cohort.
- 171/3,218 patients (5.3%) change subgroup across serial samples, and follow-up samples
  (day 3/D4/D7/follow_up_1-7) are 77-100% system-wide, so pooling them inflates system-wide
  and myeloid and deflates the lymphoid share.
- A DerSimonian-Laird random-effects pooling across the 6 cohorts (continuity-corrected logit,
  tau^2 from Cochran Q) gives system-wide 38.1% (24.7-53.7), lymphoid 21.3% (13.2-32.4),
  myeloid 7.5% (3.6-15.1), balanced 15.3% (3.7-46.3), with Q = 347/258/179/1087 (df = 5,
  p < 0.001 each): the between-cohort spread is genuine, so the headline percentages are
  sample-mix-weighted proportions within this merged dataset, not population parameters.

================================================================================
CLINICAL PLAUSIBILITY
================================================================================
30-day mortality is 21.4% in system-wide (269/1,259), 10.7% lymphoid (68/633), 5.3% myeloid
(13/244) and 4.9% balanced (37/748); chi-square = 132.3, df = 3, p = 1.7e-28. Subgroup labels
agree with independently deposited endotypes (Sweeney chi-square = 2,023.3; Davenport 2,178.7;
Cano 1,598.3; all df = 6, p < 1e-300): 99.2% of balanced patients are "adaptive", whereas
system-wide patients are 48.5% inflammopathic and 38.1% coagulopathic. The distribution is
therefore consistent with a majority of critically ill patients carrying a measurable,
outcome-relevant immune dysregulation relative to healthy blood, with system-wide
dysregulation as the largest and most lethal subgroup.

LIMITATIONS: proportions are cross-sectional snapshots of a merged, unevenly weighted
multi-cohort table (savemore contributes 78.1% of all balanced samples); the healthy reference
used for z-standardisation and any cohort-specific normalisation could not be re-derived from
the workspace; 26% of rows lack d30_mort and 77.7% lack SOFA, so no severity-adjusted estimate
was possible; groups change over time, so a single "proportion" depends on the chosen timepoint.

Full method, code, intermediate counts and references: trace.md (module record and result
tables: analysis/README.md, analysis/output/tables/).
grader_notes: All criteria are fully satisfied; the work is thorough, reproducible, and well-sourced.

QUESTION: Which genes are differentially expressed between ALS patients and controls in the
cervical spinal cord?

SHORT ANSWER
The cervical spinal cord transcriptome is extensively remodelled in ALS. Using DESeq2 on
20,300 expressed genes from 174 post-mortem cervical spinal cord samples (138 ALS vs 36
non-neurological controls; design ~ sex + age + RIN + library_prep + site_id + disease),
7,826 genes are differentially expressed at BH FDR < 0.05 (3,843 up, 3,983 down), 5,571 at
FDR < 0.01 and 324 at FDR < 1e-10. Because FDR-only lists at this sample size include many
small compositional shifts, a "consensus core" of 2,325 genes (1,340 up, 985 down) was
defined as significant (padj < 0.05) in all six model variants, including a site-balanced
subset (site_7 only, 18 ALS vs 16 control). The signal has two opposite-direction
programmes.

  in ALS (-0.58 log2 CPM, p = 1.7e-12); astrocyte score is higher (+0.65, p = 2.2e-10),

Direction of effect is highly reproducible across methods: gene counts at padj < 0.05 were
7,826 (primary), 6,757 (+genotype PCs), 10,520 (minimal model), 3,207 (site_7-balanced
subset, n = 34), 7,787 (+extra RNA-QC covariates) and 8,170 (limma-voom); Spearman
correlation of per-gene log2FC between the primary model and these alternatives was
0.96 / 0.90 / 0.85 / 0.97 / 0.96 (and 0.80 versus TPM log2 fold changes). 2,325 genes are
significant in all six model-based analyses (1,340 up, 985 down); 1,669 of them also pass
an unadjusted Wilcoxon test on log2(TPM+1) with the same sign.

INTERPRETATION
The dominant, most reproducible molecular signature of ALS cervical spinal cord is
microglial/macrophage activation and innate immune-complement/MHC-II up-regulation
(GPNMB, CHIT1, LYZ, CTSS, MSR1, CD68, TREM2, APOE, C1Q, C3, HLA-DRA, CD163, LGALS3),
with a weaker reactive-astrocyte signal (GFAP, AQP4, C3, SERPINA3, CHI3L1 up but SLC1A2/
EAAT2 down), and coordinate loss of oligodendrocyte/myelin and cholesterol-synthesis
transcripts (MBP, PLP1, MOG, MAG, SOX10, DHCR24, CYP51A1, SQLE, FDFT1) together with
reduced neuronal/axonal markers (NEFH/NEFM/NEFL, SLC18A3, UCHL1, STMN2). Reduced UNC13A/
STMN2/ATXN2 RNA with unchanged TARDBP mRNA is the pattern expected from TDP-43 loss of
function.

LIMITATIONS
Bulk tissue: changes reflect both cell-type proportion shifts and per-cell transcriptional
changes and cannot be separated without single-cell data. The cohort is unbalanced
(138 ALS vs 36 controls) and confounded with tissue-bank site and library preparation
(only site_7 is balanced, 18 vs 16); genes whose effect shrinks in the site_7-only analysis
(e.g. CHI3L1 +1.07 -> +0.10; SERPINA3 +1.09 -> +0.16; NEFH/NEFM) are less certain than the
myeloid core. No proteomics file was provided in the workspace, so the intended orthogonal

ANSWER (BiomniBench-DA da-19-1)

Question: To identify therapeutic targets downstream of CBFbeta-SMMHC inhibition
in inv(16) AML, which genes are most significantly downregulated upon AI-10-49
treatment?

Short answer:
MYC. It is the single most salient downregulated gene in ME-1 inv(16) cells
treated with AI-10-49, and it is the only appreciably expressed gene at the top
of the ranking. Beyond MYC itself, the genes most significantly downregulated are
the coherent MYC-driven proliferative/biosynthetic programme it controls (MYC
target genes, E2F/cell-cycle genes, nucleolar and nucleotide-metabolism genes)
plus the leukemic lineage transcription programme (GATA2, CEBPA, LMO2, MYB).

Key quantitative evidence (Cuffdiff 2.2.1; DMSO = sample_1, AI-10-49 = sample_2;
57,815 rows, 14,385 tested OK, 14,357 with finite fold-change; 3 vs 3 replicates):

1) MYC itself
   FPKM 218.3 (DMSO) -> 22.2 (AI-10-49); log2FC = -3.30 (~10-fold down);
   p = 5e-05 (Cuffdiff floor), q = 2.06e-04 (FDR-significant, "yes").
   Rank among all 14,357 tested genes by fold-change: 15th; among the 7,015
   genes with DMSO FPKM >= 10: 3rd; among significant (q<0.01) expressed genes:
   2nd. The only genes ranked above it are chr15 RPL9 retro-copy pseudogenes
   (RPL9P9 log2FC -10.96, q = 0.031; RPL9P8 log2FC -5.48, q = 0.0011), which are

   and the unannotated clone AC011899.9. No other well-expressed, well-annotated
   gene approaches MYC's combined significance and effect size.

2) MYC target-gene output (orthogonal gene-set evidence, Fisher ORA with the
   14,357 tested genes as background, BH-FDR within library x direction)
   - Hallmark "Myc Targets V2": 20 of 58 genes down at q<0.05 and log2FC <= -1

AI-10-49 releases RUNX1 from CBFbeta-SMMHC, and the dominant transcriptional
consequence in ME-1 cells is collapse of the MYC locus and of the entire
MYC -> ribosome biogenesis / nucleotide synthesis / E2F-cell-cycle output

replicates, gene-level Cuffdiff output only (p floored at 5e-5, q at 2.06e-04, so
3,497 genes are tied at the minimum q and ranking within that tier is by effect
size); no ATAC-seq/ChIP-seq or protein-level data are present in this workspace,
so direct versus indirect regulation cannot be distinguished here.

FINAL ANSWER — DA-15-7
Which individual genes show the strongest correlation with ALS disease duration?

SHORT ANSWER
CHIT1 (chitotriosidase-1) is the strongest and most reproducible gene. Across all three spinal
cord levels, higher CHIT1 expression goes with SHORTER disease duration, i.e. faster
progression:
  - Cervical: n=120, Spearman rho = -0.513 (95% CI -0.63 to -0.37), p = 2.1e-9, FDR = 9.1e-5
  - Lumbar:   n=98,  Spearman rho = -0.450 (95% CI -0.60 to -0.28), p = 3.4e-6, FDR = 0.032
  - Thoracic: n=40,  Spearman rho = -0.487 (95% CI -0.69 to -0.21), p = 1.4e-3, FDR = 0.031
  Linear model on voom log2-CPM adjusted for age, sex, RIN, library prep and bulbar onset:
  logFC = -0.468 (cervical), -0.540 (lumbar), -0.505 (thoracic) per additional year of
  duration; CHIT1 is rank 1 by |rho| among expressed genes in cervical and lumbar cord and
  rank 19 in thoracic cord. It is the ONLY gene among ~13,100 expressed genes in the top 20
  by |rho| in all three spinal levels, one of only 12 genes reaching FDR<0.05 within each of
  the three levels, and survives every sensitivity analysis (no covariates; +site +genotype
  PCs; mutation non-carriers only; leave-one-out; leave-one-site-out) and adjustment for
  microglial/astrocytic/neuronal cell-composition markers. Mean TPM by duration tertile
  (short/mid/long): 14.1/6.8/3.7 (cervical), 9.2/3.7/1.7 (lumbar), 16.6/6.2/4.1 (thoracic)
  - roughly a 3-4x fall from fastest to slowest progressors.

RUNNERS-UP (all higher in short-duration / fast-progressing cases)
Cross-level Stouffer meta-analysis of 19,374 genes tested in all three levels (weighted Z,
BH-FDR) puts HAVCR2 (TIM-3) first (Z = -8.40, meta-FDR = 8.5e-13; rho = -0.34/-0.28/-0.26,
FDR<0.05 in all three levels), then CHIT1 (Z = -8.10, meta-FDR = 5.4e-12), then
SLC29A1 (-7.79), HLA-DMB (-7.65), APOC2 (-7.63), CD37 (-7.60), LILRA2 (-7.50), NCF2 (-7.48),
SYK (-7.48), NCKAP1L (-7.45), CCRL2 (-7.40), APOBR (-7.39), PTGS1 (-7.30), OLR1 (-7.27),
RAB42 (-7.19), PLA2G7 (-7.18), CDCP1, LGALS9, UNC93B1, CD300LF, RNASET2, PIK3CG, BTK, DOCK2.
Other strong per-level correlates: OAS1 (rho = -0.464 cervical), MX2 (-0.431 cervical),
CHI3L1 (-0.375/-0.267/-0.468), GPNMB and PLA2G7 (top-50 by |rho| in all three levels),
MAFB (thoracic, logFC -0.200, p = 8.5e-8).
2,308 of 19,374 genes reach meta-FDR<0.05; 2,181 of them agree in direction across all three
levels; 1,333 are higher in fast progressors and 975 higher in slow progressors.

SLOW-PROGRESSION (positive) GENES
The strongest gene in the opposite direction is IL17D (Z = +7.16, meta-FDR = 8.0e-10;
rho = +0.24/+0.18/+0.33), followed by AGPAT3, B3GAT2, TRIL, IGSF1, OSBPL2, DAAM2, TOB2, FAM84B,
PAH, GOLM1, PHGDH.

BIOLOGICAL/CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
The top of the ranking is a coherent microglial/macrophage activation and lipid-handling
module: CHIT1 (a secreted chitinase of activated microglia, already an established CSF marker
of ALS severity and progression), HAVCR2/TIM-3, SYK, NCF2, BTK, DOCK2, NCKAP1L, PIK3CG, CD37,
LILRA2, CCRL2, CD300LF, LGALS9 (myeloid signalling), and APOC2, APOBR, OLR1, PLA2G7 (lipid
metabolism). This is consistent with the literature in which microglial activation tracks ALS
progression rate. The microglial marker score itself is higher in short-duration cases
(r = -0.40 cervical, p = 4e-6), so part of the signal is a real difference in myeloid tissue
burden; nevertheless CHIT1 remains significant after adjusting for that score, making it the
best-supported candidate biomarker of progression rate in this dataset.

CAVEATS
No proteomics file was present in the workspace, so the planned orthogonal protein-level
validation (Oeckl et al. CSF/spinal-cord proteomics) could not be performed. The three spinal
levels are the same donors, so they are not independent replicates. The design is
cross-sectional (one postmortem time point), duration is a coarse phenotype, and no held-out
predictive performance was measured. Correlation with duration does not establish causality or
prove predictive utility.

QUESTION: Calculate the interaction effect size between baseline insulin resistance status and
the magnitude of peak glucose reduction observed in the protein-preloaded rice experiments
compared to the fiber-preloaded experiments (mitigator challenge data).

SHORT ANSWER
The interaction is real but modest in precision, and it depends on which "insulin resistance"
marker is used. Using the reference-standard peripheral insulin-resistance marker (SSPG, the
Reaven insulin-suppression-test measure; SSPG >= 180 mg/dL = insulin resistant), the
interaction effect size is:

  Difference of differences (DoD) = +22.0 mg/dL  (95% CI +3.1 to +40.9)
  Cohen's d = 1.27  (95% CI 0.29 to 4.83)
  Partial eta^2 = 0.229, F(1,17) = 5.06, p = 0.038  (2x2 mixed ANOVA: preload within-subject
  x insulin-resistance status between-subject; Welch t p = 0.073; bootstrap p = 0.016)
  Continuous dose-response: +8.6 mg/dL per 1 SD of SSPG (0.118 mg/dL per mg/dL SSPG),
  r = +0.45, p = 0.055, R^2 = 0.199, standardized beta = +0.45.
  For the absolute (not baseline-corrected) peak: DoD = +29.8 mg/dL, d = 1.50,
  partial eta^2 = 0.294, p = 0.017; continuous +12.5 mg/dL per SD, r = +0.55, p = 0.016.

DIRECTION OF THE EFFECT
Metric: per-subject peak rise above the pre-meal baseline (mg/dL), protein pre-load minus
fiber pre-load on the rice challenge (positive = protein gives the HIGHER peak, i.e. less
peak reduction).

  Insulin-sensitive (n = 15): fiber 61.0 -> protein 54.0 mg/dL, contrast = -6.97 mg/dL
  Insulin-resistant   (n = 4): fiber 60.5 -> protein 75.5 mg/dL, contrast = +15.04 mg/dL

So in insulin-sensitive people the protein pre-load lowers the post-rice peak more than fiber
does (by 7.0 mg/dL), while in insulin-resistant people the ordering reverses and protein
lowers it 15.0 mg/dL less than fiber — a 22.0 mg/dL difference in the pre-load effect. In the
"magnitude of peak reduction" framing used in the question, the protein-attributable peak
reduction relative to fiber, Dpeak(fiber) - Dpeak(protein), is +6.97 mg/dL in
insulin-sensitive subjects and -15.04 mg/dL in insulin-resistant subjects; the interaction is
-22.0 mg/dL on that scale (equal and opposite to the DoD above).
Absolute-peak numbers: insulin-sensitive protein 152.3 vs fiber 164.8 mg/dL (contrast -12.5);
insulin-resistant protein 170.9 vs fiber 153.6 (contrast +17.3).

DOSE-DEPENDENCE ON THE IR DEFINITION (this is the key caveat)
- SSPG >= 180 mg/dL (n = 4 IR vs 15): DoD +22.0 mg/dL, d = 1.27, partial eta^2 = 0.229. The
  effect is driven by few people (leave-one-out range +16.2 to +27.6 mg/dL, sign stable;
  removing XB68 alone leaves +16.2).
- HOMA-IR >= 2.5 (n = 6 IR vs 17, available for all 23 subjects): NO interaction:
  DoD = -1.8 mg/dL (95% CI -20.0 to +16.3), d = -0.10, partial eta^2 = 0.002, p = 0.84.
  Continuous HOMA-IR: +2.8 mg/dL per SD, p = 0.48 (leave-one-out slope flips sign).
- Also null: HbA1c, BMI and DI as interaction moderators (all p > 0.40).
The two markers are only partly concordant here (SSPG vs HOMA-IR r = 0.64 across the 39
cohort participants with both measures, r = 0.70 in the 19-subject analysis subset; XB68 has SSPG 194
but HOMA-IR 1.26), and SSPG indexes peripheral insulin-mediated glucose disposal under a fixed
insulin infusion, which is the mechanism a pre-load must engage.

ROBUSTNESS (SSPG-based)
Stable point estimate under adjustment: unadjusted +8.6, +baseline glucose +9.1, +BMI/age +8.9,
+sex +10.5 (p = 0.041), +fasting glucose +11.0 (p = 0.045), +all covariates +10.1 mg/dL per SD.
0-120 min restricted peak: +7.5 per SD (p = 0.09); incremental AUC: +6.3 per SD (p = 0.28);
percent-of-baseline peak: +6.9 points per SD (p = 0.12). Bootstrap CI for the continuous slope
+1.0 to +15.2; leave-one-out +6.2 to +9.7 (sign stable). Replicate imbalance is not driving it
(first-replicate-only +9.3 per SD; subjects with >=2 replicates per arm +9.6 per SD).

INTERPRETATION
Fiber blunts the postprandial excursion largely by slowing gastric emptying/absorption, a
mechanism that does not require intact peripheral insulin action; a protein pre-load adds
insulinotropic/incretin-mediated glucose disposal, which is impaired in insulin-resistant
individuals. Hence protein loses its peak-lowering advantage over fiber exactly in the
insulin-resistant group, while the whole-cohort main effect of the mitigator on peak height is
null (protein vs fiber, paired t(22) = -0.89, p = 0.38). Within-subject replicate SD of the
peak rise is 11-16 mg/dL, so the interaction is of the same order as single-measurement noise.

LIMITATIONS
Only 4 of the 19 participants with SSPG are insulin-resistant, so the categorical estimate is
imprecise (Welch p = 0.073; Cohen's d CI 0.29-4.83) and is dominated by 3-4 individuals; the
result is hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Multiple outcomes/definitions were
explored without multiplicity correction. No dose/timing information for the pre-loads is
available, and the plasma proteomics file overlaps only 8 of the 23 paired subjects, so no
mediator can be tested. This is a group-level finding (R^2 ~ 0.2-0.3), not an individual-level
predictor.

ANSWER — DA-20-3
Which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are suppressed by Brefeldin-A (BFA) across cell types?

METHOD IN ONE LINE
For each of the 24 Brefeldin-A DESeq2 contrasts (4 primary human cell types x 6 doses; 5 active
doses 28.5-3000 nM + 9.5 nM), genes were ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic
(log2FoldChange / lfcSE) and tested against the 50 MSigDB Hallmark sets (h.all.v2023.2.Hs) with
GSEA-preranked (gseapy 1.3.1, 1,000 permutations, seed 42). A set counts as "suppressed across
cell types" if its NES is negative with FDR < 0.05 in every (cell type x dose) sample.
Two independent controls were added: a size-matched random-gene-set null (background-corrected
z-score) and a directed Fisher test for strong down-regulation, plus the other two positive
control compounds in the data set (Dexamethasone, Trichostatin A) as specificity controls.

HEADLINE RESULT
BFA suppresses a large, highly reproducible secreted-protein / inflammatory-secretome programme.
Fifteen Hallmark pathways are significantly suppressed (NES < 0, FDR < 0.05) in ALL 20
(cell type x active dose) samples; seven more are significant in 17-20 of 20. Suppression is
essentially identical in all four cell types (cross-cell-type NES range 0.16-0.71 NES units at
300 nM). BFA is NOT a general transcriptional repressor: the unfolded protein response and
mTORC1 signalling are strongly INDUCED.

TIER 1 — suppressed in 20/20 samples (4 cell types x 5 active doses, all FDR < 0.05).
Mean NES across the 20 samples in brackets (more negative = stronger suppression):
 1. HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION   [-2.76]
 2. HALLMARK_UV_RESPONSE_DN                      [-2.32]
 3. HALLMARK_APICAL_JUNCTION                     [-2.17]
 4. HALLMARK_COAGULATION                         [-2.13]
 5. HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB             [-2.10]
 6. HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING                  [-2.10]
 7. HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS                           [-2.06]
 8. HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS                        [-2.05]
 9. HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP                   [-2.02]
10. HALLMARK_IL2_STAT5_SIGNALING                 [-1.96]
11. HALLMARK_APICAL_SURFACE                      [-1.94]
12. HALLMARK_COMPLEMENT                          [-1.88]
13. HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE           [-1.71]
14. HALLMARK_HEDGEHOG_SIGNALING                  [-1.65]
15. HALLMARK_NOTCH_SIGNALING                     [-1.59]

TIER 2 — suppressed in 17-19 of the 20 samples (same programme, dose/lineage dependent):
16. HALLMARK_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE                [-1.97; 19/20]
17. HALLMARK_MYOGENESIS                           [-1.80; 19/20]
18. HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY              [-1.73; 19/20]
19. HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE               [-1.53; 19/20]
20. HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING              [-1.85; 18/20]
21. HALLMARK_HYPOXIA                              [-1.86; 17/20]
22. HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE                    [-1.27; 17/20]  (borderline; largest variance)

Directionally suppressed throughout but weaker / more dose-dependent (significant in 10-16 of 20):
HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING (16/20), HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION (15/20),
HALLMARK_REACTIVE_OXYGEN_SPECIES_PATHWAY (15/20), HALLMARK_MITOTIC_SPINDLE (14/20),
HALLMARK_GLYCOLYSIS (14/20), HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY (12/20), HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT (10/20).

IMPORTANT NEGATIVE RESULT
HALLMARK_PROTEIN_SECRETION is NOT suppressed: mean NES +0.78, NES < 0 in only 5/20 samples and
never significantly negative (0/20 at FDR<0.05; significantly positive in 6/20), Fisher OR 0.53
(depleted, not enriched, for down-regulated genes: 18.9% strongly down inside the set vs 30.7%
background). The reason is composition — the set mixes secretion machinery (COPB1, SEC24D, GOSR2,
USO1, YKT6, NAPA, MON2, ARFGEF1/2, VAMP4 —
all UP under BFA) with secreted cargo (CTSC, CAV2, EGFR — strongly DOWN), so the two halves
cancel. The secretory phenotype is instead carried by the cargo-dominated sets listed above.
Also NOT suppressed (all significantly UP): HALLMARK_UNFOLDED_PROTEIN_RESPONSE (NES +2.40, 20/20),
HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING (+1.96, 20/20), HALLMARK_DNA_REPAIR, HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION,
HALLMARK_MYC_TARGETS_V2. Unchanged: PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING, ADIPOGENESIS, PEROXISOME,
BILE_ACID_METABOLISM, PANCREAS_BETA_CELLS, SPERMATOGENESIS, HEME_METABOLISM, UV_RESPONSE_UP.

SUPPORTING QUANTITIES
- Cross-cell-type concordance: for the Tier-1 sets at 300 nM, NES per cell type is e.g.
  EMT -3.11 (AoSMC), -3.01 (fibroblast), -2.42 (melanocyte), -2.85 (SkMM); maximum FDR over the
  15 sets x 20 samples is 0.0496. Median cross-cell-type NES range: 0.46.
- Not a global shift: the transcriptome-wide median log2FC under BFA is only -0.03 to -0.12,
  whereas the size-matched-null z-scores of the Tier-1 sets are -2.7 to -15.0, and 46-65% of
  their genes are strongly down-regulated versus 30.7% background.
- Gene-level drill-down: secreted cargo down (IL6 -5.3, CXCL8 -5.0, SERPINE1 -1.9 to -4.3,
  TIMP1 -1.3 to -2.8, COL1A1/COL3A1/SPARC down), while ER chaperones and transport machinery go
  up (HSPA5 +3.6 to +4.7, DDIT3 +4.0 to +5.4, HERPUD1 +2.9 to +4.6, XBP1/ATF4 up; COPB1, COPA,
  GBF1, SEC61A1 up) — the canonical signature of an ER-to-Golgi cargo-export block.
- Dose: suppression is saturated from ~95 nM upward (3,770-4,776 genes significantly down per
  sample at every dose >= 95 nM; at 28.5 nM the range is 944 (melanocyte) to 3,631 (AoSMC)). At
  9.5 nM only AoSMCs (20 of the 50 sets significantly suppressed) and partly fibroblasts (10/50)
  respond; melanocytes and SkMMs do not.
- Specificity vs the other positive controls in the data set: Trichostatin A never reproducibly
  suppresses the Tier-1 sets (0-10 of 20 samples per set, vs 20/20 for BFA) and instead suppresses
  the proliferation sets (G2M_CHECKPOINT 19/20, E2F_TARGETS 16/20, MYC_TARGETS_V1 15/20).
  Dexamethasone suppresses 0/20 of 13 of the 15 Tier-1 sets (KRAS_SIGNALING_UP 5/20,
  ANGIOGENESIS 1/20) and has almost no effect in 3 of 4 cell types (0-1 significantly down genes).
  The BFA signature is therefore compound-specific, not a generic drug/stress response.
- Rank-metric and filtering robustness: rerunning with raw log2FoldChange ranking, or excluding
  the independent-filtering (padj = NA) genes, leaves 14-15 of the 15 Tier-1 sets significant in
  4/4 cell types at 300 nM (non-NaN Wald: 15/15; raw log2FoldChange: 14/15, only
  HEDGEHOG_SIGNALING drops to 2/4).

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
Brefeldin-A inhibits ARF1-dependent COPI recruitment, blocking ER->Golgi export and collapsing the
Golgi. The suppressed Hallmark programme is exactly the cargo of that pathway and its
transcriptional amplifiers: secreted ECM and matrix-remodelling proteins (COL1A1, COL3A1, SPARC,
FBN1, LOX/LOXL1/2, TIMP1, TIMP3, SERPINE1, PLOD2), secreted cytokines/chemokines/growth factors
(IL6, CXCL1/3/6/8, CCL2, CSF1, VEGFA, VEGFC, FGF2, PTX3, GREM1, DKK1, TGFB1), and junction /
adhesion / cortical-cytoskeleton proteins that must traffic to the plasma membrane (CDH2/6/11,
NECTIN2/3, CLDN11/14, ITGA2/5, SDC1/3/4, CD44, ACTB/ACTG1, ACTN1, VCL, MSN, MYH9). Simultaneously
the cell mounts the unfolded protein response and up-regulates the secretory machinery itself.
This is precisely the transcriptional signature expected of a secretory-pathway disruptor and
therefore confirms BFA's mechanism of action at the pathway level.

WHAT THIS CANNOT CONCLUDE
Only pre-computed per-gene statistics were available (no raw counts, no expression matrix), so
DESeq2 could not be refitted, replicate structure could not be checked, and sample-level
enrichment methods (ssGSEA/GSVA) were not possible. Significance is FDR within each sample plus a
cross-sample reproducibility count, not a single genome-wide family-wise test. The Hallmark sets
overlap heavily, so the 15-22 hits represent one secretome/inflammation programme seen through
overlapping lenses rather than 15-22 independent functions. The analysis shows transcriptional
consequences consistent with ER->Golgi blockade but does not by itself prove direct inhibition,
nor exclude contributions from ER stress, growth arrest and translational attenuation. Coverage is
limited to four primary human cell types and three compounds; "across cell types" holds rigorously
at doses >= 28.5 nM (Tier 1) or >= 95 nM (Tier 2), with melanocytes the weakest responder.
grader_notes: The agent performed a thorough and well-documented analysis, but the primary ranking metric deviated from the rubric-required log2FoldChange, and the quantitative validation for the three target pathways was not presented with the full specified detail.

QUESTION: What is the cumulative frequency of MAPK pathway alterations in post-hormonal-therapy HR+HER2- tumors?

ANSWER: ~21% (21.4%; 151 of 705 post-hormonal-therapy HR+/HER2- tumors).

Details
-------
Cohort (n = 705 samples; 656 patients): HR+/HER2- by the sequenced sample's receptor status
(HR_STATUS = Positive, OVERALL_HER2_STATUS = Negative) AND post-hormonal therapy, defined as any
sequenced tumor that is not a treatment-naive primary, i.e. 629 metastases + 40 post-treatment
primaries + 36 post-neo-adjuvant primaries. (Comparison set: 657 treatment-naive HR+/HER2- primaries.)

MAPK pathway alteration = >=1 non-synonymous/splice mutation OR high-level copy-number event
(amplification = 2, deep deletion = -2) in a 19-gene canonical MAPK (RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK) set:
KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, RIT1, BRAF, RAF1, ARAF, MAP2K1, MAP2K2, MAPK1, MAPK3, NF1, RASA1, SOS1, PTPN11,
CBL, SPRED1, DUSP4, ERBB2. Frequency is the sample-level union (each tumor counted once).

Result: 151/705 = 21.4% of post-hormonal HR+/HER2- tumors carry at least one MAPK pathway
alteration (129 tumors with 1 alteration, 20 with 2, 2 with 3).
Leading genes: NF1 5.96% (37 mutations, 5 deep deletions), ERBB2 5.67% (38 mutations, 2
amplifications, 1 deep deletion), RIT1 1.99%, KRAS 1.70%, RASA1 1.42%, MAPK1 1.13%, RAF1 0.99%.

This is about twice the rate in treatment-naive HR+/HER2- primaries (10.4%, 68/657;
Fisher exact OR = 2.36, p = 2.4e-8), and the post-hormonal label is internally validated by the
ESR1 positive control (20.9% post-hormonal vs 2.0% treatment-naive; p = 5.8e-31).

Sensitivity / robustness of the headline number
-----------------------------------------------
- Metastases only (n = 629): 22.1%.
- Receptor status taken from the primary tumor instead of the sequenced sample (n = 762): 22.6%.
- Patient-level (one sample per patient, n = 656): 20.1%.
- NF1 restricted to loss-of-function/deep deletion ("activating-only"): 19.7%.
- Excluding ERBB2 from the gene set (16 regulators + core only): 16.7%.
- Adding FGFR1 amplification (RTK-driven MAPK): 35.0%; full RTK-RAS pathway: 49.1%.
- Post-treatment primaries only (n = 40): 15.0% (small, unstable subset).
- Sum of the individual per-gene frequencies (double-counts multi-hit tumors): 24.8%.

Bottom line: roughly one in five (approximately 21%, 20-23% across defensible cohort definitions)
post-hormonal-therapy HR+/HER2- tumors harbours a MAPK pathway alteration, most commonly NF1 loss
(5.96%) or an activating ERBB2 mutation (5.67%), consistent with MAPK pathway activation as a
recurrent endocrine-resistance mechanism.
grader_notes: The agent performs a thorough analysis with clear cohort selection, alteration identification, union computation, and source grounding. However, it uses a broader/different MAPK gene set than the rubric's expected full-score set, omits ESR1-stratified MAPK frequencies and formal mutual exclusivity testing, and does not fully report the ESR1-wild-type frequency or exclusivity relationship.

ANSWER — DA-24-3: Shared genetic factors among neonatal metabolites (GWAS summary statistics)

BOTTOM LINE
The 13 metabolite/ratio traits in discovery.summary.gz and replication.summary.gz (20,474 SNPs x 13
traits per cohort) contain 592 genome-wide significant (GWS, p<5e-8) variant-trait signals that
collapse into 12 independent loci (250 kb gap clumping). Only ONE locus is genuinely shared between
different metabolites and survives independent-cohort replication:

  *** chr1:75.64-75.96 Mb (hg38) — ACADM (medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase) ***
  Shared by 4 traits: C6, C8, C8/C2 and (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10.
  Lead variant chr1:75727547:A:G (effect allele G, EAF 0.70; inside the ACADM gene body,
  hg38 chr1:75,724,430-75,787,575). p = 2.85e-13 (discovery), 1.90e-13 (replication).
  Per-allele effects (alt allele G): C6 -0.00193, C8 -0.00270, C8/C2 -1.69e-4, (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 +0.0842.
  The same allele coordinately lowers the medium-chain acylcarnitines C6 (hexanoylcarnitine) and
  C8 (octanoylcarnitine), lowers their ratio to acetylcarnitine, and raises the composite ratio
  (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 (consistent with lowering its denominator C10, a metabolite present in
  metabolite.gz but not among the 13 GWAS traits).
  Evidence that this is ONE shared factor and not several nearby signals: across the 121 significant
  SNPs of the region the z-profiles of C6, C8 and C8/C2 correlate r >= 0.999 and the profile of
  (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 is their exact mirror (r = -0.998) in discovery; in the independent replication
  cohort |r| >= 0.995 with the identical sign pattern. The four traits' lead SNPs lie within 37 kb of
  each other, all inside ACADM.
  Interpretation: a common variant acting on the ACADM / mitochondrial medium-chain beta-oxidation
  axis (KEGG hsa00071/hsa01212) shifts the whole C6-C10 acylcarnitine axis — the same analytes used
  for newborn-screening detection of MCAD deficiency (C6, C8, C8:1, C10, C10:1 and their ratios).

A SECOND shared locus was detected but does NOT replicate and is therefore reported as a
cohort-specific artefact rather than a shared genetic factor:
  chr5:50,145,974-50,280,106 (hg38, intergenic 5p13.2; no annotated protein-coding gene within
  +/-1 Mb). Lead chr5:50161448:T:C (EAF 0.496): GWS for C10:1 (p=9.6e-9, z=+5.74) and C6DC
  (p=4.6e-10, z=+6.23) in discovery, but z = +0.12 and -0.08 (p = 0.11 and 0.07) in the replication
  cohort at the same alleles. The same is true of the chr15:78,086,842:G:A signal for C0
  (p=2.2e-8 discovery, p=0.66 replication).

QUANTIFICATION OF SHARING
- 57 variants are GWS for >=2 traits (51 for >=3; maximum 4 traits) versus 7.35 expected under
  independence from the per-trait significance rates = 7.8-fold enrichment; 52 of the 57 sit in the
  ACADM peak and 5 in the chr5:50.15-50.28 Mb cluster.
- Region-level permutation test (2,000 permutations placing each trait's loci at random among the
  panel's SNPs): 2 shared regions observed vs 0.058 expected, p = 0.0015.
- Sub-threshold support: ACADM-linked pairs share 103-145x more variants at p<1e-5 than expected
  (C6~C8 124 observed vs 1.0 expected; C8~C8/C2 87 vs 0.6; C6~C8/C2 95 vs 0.8;
  C6~(C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 167 vs 1.6), while pairs with no shared locus share none
  (C4DC+C5-OH~C6 0 vs 1.2; C6DC~PRO 0 vs 0.06).
- Cross-cohort (discovery z of A x replication z of B) sharing index, which cannot be inflated by
  sample overlap: strongest pairs C6~C8 +0.251, C8~C8/C2 +0.241, C6~C8/C2 +0.203,
  (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10~C8 -0.255, (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10~C6 -0.234 (negative = the ratio runs opposite to its
  C10 denominator's partner), C4DC+C5-OH~C6 +0.188. Decomposition shows 68% of the C6~C8 statistic
  comes from the 121 SNPs of the ACADM peak (0.6% of the panel) and only 2% from the 19,705 SNPs
  >1 Mb away from any significant locus.

TRAIT-SPECIFIC LOCI (no sharing): C4 -> ACADS (chr12:120.73 Mb, lead inside gene, p=5.4e-25/2.2e-23);
C6DC -> CPT2 (chr1:53.19 Mb, lead 4 kb upstream, p=8.0e-10/9.5e-10); TYR -> HPD (chr12:121.86 Mb, lead
inside gene, p=9.5e-34/5.5e-11); PRO -> PRODH (chr22:18.92 Mb, p=9.1e-42/4.0e-9); C8:1 ->
ACSM2A/ACSM2B (chr16:20.47-20.60 Mb, p=2.8e-12/2.2e-6); C0 -> CPT1A region (chr11:68.62-68.64 Mb,
lead 114 kb upstream of CPT1A, p=3.6e-20/4.6e-13); C4DC+C5-OH -> CRAT/DOLPP1 (chr9:129.08-129.21 Mb,
p=1.3e-63/8.7e-92, the strongest signal in the data set); C10:1 -> CYP4A11/CYP4A22 (chr1:46.92 Mb,
p=1.8e-10/5.2e-15). 12 of 16 trait-locus pairs replicate (p<0.05, same direction). One notable
replicated but sub-threshold multi-trait pattern: at the CPT2 lead, C6DC is up (+6.1/+6.1) while C0,
C4, C6 and C4DC+C5-OH are consistently down in both cohorts (z = -2.6 to -5.4).

METHODOLOGICAL WARNING (important for interpreting any "shared factor" claim here)
Within-cohort cross-trait z-score correlations are NOT evidence of genetic sharing: both metabolites
are measured in the same individuals, so correlated phenotypic residuals create a genome-wide,
locus-free correlation. In this data set the within-cohort z-correlation matrix is essentially the
phenotypic correlation matrix (R^2 = 0.895 in discovery, vs Spearman phenotypes from metabolite.gz),
and it stays that way on SNPs >=1 Mb from every significant locus (R^2 = 0.969, intercept 0.005),
whereas the cross-cohort statistic on those same background SNPs collapses to ~0 (mean |S| = 0.0067).
Only replication-based statistics (independent cohort) and locus-level colocalisation are used above.

LIMITATIONS
- No LD reference panel and only a locus-enriched 20,474-SNP panel (6.6 SNPs/Mb genome-average vs 203
  SNPs in chr1:75 Mb) means LD-score regression / GREML genetic correlations cannot be computed; the
  numeric sharing matrix above is an attenuated, locus-weighted index, not r_g.
- Only 13 of the ~75 metabolites are present in the summary statistics (the dense, non-significant
  windows at chr6:32, chr16:53, chr5:46, chr6:31, chr12:61, chr8:4 Mb etc. most likely belong to the
  missing traits), so the shared-factor structure is right-censored.
- Colocalisation is assessed by peak z-profile concordance, not by a formal LD-based colocalisation
  test; candidate genes are assigned by hg38 position (UCSC knownGene/GENCODE v50) plus enzyme
  plausibility.
- Ratio traits share factors with their constituent metabolites partly by construction (Petersen et
  al. 2012); the biologically informative pleiotropy is the coordinate effect on the two directly
  measured species C6 and C8.
- Implied effective sample sizes (from SD in metabolite.gz and median SE) are ~6,350 (discovery,
  range 4,900-6,900) and ~7,600 (replication, range 6,550-8,800); power is therefore limited for
  weak pleiotropy, and two of the apparently significant signals failed replication.

KEY REFERENCES: ACADM/MCAD deficiency newborn screening — Grosse et al. Genet Med 2006;8:205-12
(PMID 16617240); ratio-trait statistics — Petersen et al. BMC Bioinformatics 2012;13:120
(PMID 22672667); metabolite-GWAS framework — Shin et al. Nat Genet 2014;46:543-50 (PMID 24816252);
sample-overlap bias — Burgess et al. Genet Epidemiol 2016;40:597-608 (PMID 27625185);
LDSC/genetic correlation — Bulik-Sullivan et al. Nat Genet 2015;47:291-5, 1236-41
(PMIDs 25642630, 26414676); pleiotropy framework — Solovieff et al. Nat Rev Genet 2013;14:483-95
(PMID 23752797); gene coordinates — UCSC hg38 knownGene API, GENCODE v50.

q=3.7e-02). Not significant: PKHD1 (q=5.2e-02), LPA, SPAG17, DNAH2 (q=0.13-0.14).

======================================================================
3. GENES SIGNIFICANTLY ENRICHED IN NON-RESPONDERS (NR)
======================================================================
 gene      R/21   NR/17   background   p-value    adjusted p (Holm)   BH q
 CLEC14A     0      5      19/469      7.9e-04     2.9e-02           2.0e-02
 TRPM2       1      6      34/469      1.3e-03     4.7e-02           2.0e-02
 ITGAX       0      5      23/469      1.7e-03     5.7e-02           2.0e-02
 PLEKHA7     1      5      27/469      3.2e-03     1.0e-01           2.9e-02
 DGKI        1      5      31/469      5.4e-03     1.7e-01           3.9e-02
 UNC5D       1      5      37/469      1.1e-02     3.3e-01           6.5e-02  (ns)
 BCLAF1      0      5      57/469      5.3e-02     1.0               2.4e-01  (ns)

Two genes pass the study's Holm threshold (CLEC14A, TRPM2); five pass BH q<0.05.

======================================================================
4. THE CLINICALLY INTERPRETABLE HIT: BRCA2
======================================================================
BRCA2 is the headline biologically meaningful result: 6/21 responders (28.6%)
carry a BRCA2 missense variant versus 1/17 non-responders (5.9%); odds ratio
against the background prevalence = 6.3; Fisher p = 0.0018; Holm-adjusted
p = 0.0437; BH q = 0.0050. The seven variant carriers are Pt1 (NR, S1792F),
Pt3 (S2522F), Pt4 (H2361Y), Pt19 (E2115K), Pt21 (H2537Y), Pt27 (P2505S) and
Pt28 (V950L) - seven distinct heterozygous missense variants, no recurrent
hotspot. BRCA2 is a core homologous-recombination DNA-repair gene, and the
study's own S1B sheet independently flags exactly these carriers
("BRCA2mutant?" column), confirming the count from S1D. Loss of homologous
recombination is expected to increase genomic instability and neoantigen load,
which is a plausible route to better response to PD-1 blockade.

======================================================================
5. IMPORTANT CAVEATS / WHAT CANNOT BE CONCLUDED
======================================================================
(a) The p-values above test recurrence of a gene in one response group against a
    469-sample melanoma background prevalence - they are NOT a responder-vs-
    non-responder comparison. In a direct R vs NR Fisher test over all 9,877 genes
    in S1D, NO gene is significant after BH correction (smallest unadjusted
    p = 0.0099 for FREM1, 10 R vs 1 NR; BH q = 1.0 for every gene). With 21 R and
    17 NR the cohort is simply underpowered for arm-vs-arm inference, so "gene X
    is enriched in responders" must always be qualified as "relative to melanoma
    background frequency".
(b) The background prevalence drives the result and is not fully reproducible from
    the supplied auxiliary files: BGhit (Table 1E, documented as Hodis + TCGA,
    n=469) is ~3x the Hodis-only per-gene patient counts (121 Hodis samples,
    58,818 non-synonymous calls) and ~1.2x the TCGA S2A "npat" values. Using the
    Hodis-only background weakens BRCA2 to p = 0.049; using Hodis + TCGA counts
    over 469 gives p = 0.005. Directions never change.
(c) MUC12's extreme p-value (2.9e-09) is an artifact risk: MUC12 is an enormous,
    repeat-rich mucin gene with a ZERO background count in the provided data, so
    its p-value rests entirely on an empty background cell. It is not a credible
    driver candidate.
(d) The strongest signals (FREM1, LPHN3, UTRN, DNAH2, SPAG17, LPA, CDH23, PKHD1,
    CNGB3, MYOM3) are long, rarely-mutated genes that accumulate passenger
    mutations in proportion to gene length under the dominant UV mutational
    process (C>T/G>A transitions; 85% of all calls). No gene-length, coverage or
    sequence-context normalization was applied, so these are probably proxies for
    mutational load, not gene-specific effects.
(e) Related context: median non-synonymous SNVs 495 (R) vs 281 (NR), trend in the
    expected direction but not significant (Mann-Whitney one-sided p = 0.15).
(f) Robustness: restricting to the 34 pre-treatment biopsies (excluding the 4
    on-treatment cases Pt11, Pt16, Pt17, Pt26) leaves the responder set intact
    (BRCA2 p = 0.0014, q = 0.004; 23/25 genes retained; CACNA1S and CNGB3 drop out)
    and keeps TRPM2, CLEC14A, PLEKHA7, UNC5D and ITGAX significant on the
    non-responder side (DGKI and BCLAF1 drop out).
(g) Enrichment is statistical, not causal: these data cannot separate driver from
    passenger mutations, and no adjustment was made for tumor purity, BRAF/NRAS
    status, prior MAPK-inhibitor therapy or HLA type.

======================================================================
6. BOTTOM LINE
======================================================================
Using Supplementary Table 1D, responders are significantly enriched for mutations
in MUC12, OR13C5, FREM1, ZNF534, FMO1, UTRN, SP140L, ITGA9, AMER3, LPHN3, ABCA7,
OR10J1 and BRCA2 (Holm-adjusted p < 0.05, up to 25 genes at BH q < 0.05), and
non-responders are enriched for mutations in CLEC14A and TRPM2 (and, at BH
q < 0.05, ITGAX, PLEKHA7, DGKI), all tested against a 469-sample melanoma
background. The single biologically interpretable finding is BRCA2: 6/21
responders vs 1/17 non-responders, p = 0.0018, Holm-adjusted p = 0.044, BH
q = 0.005. No individual gene differentiates the two arms of the trial
significantly when responders and non-responders are compared directly.

GENOMIC LANDSCAPE ACROSS BREAST CANCER RECEPTOR SUBTYPES
(MSK-IMPACT targeted-panel cohort: 1,918 sequenced breast cancers, of which 1,814 in 1,678 patients
were classifiable into the four receptor subtypes)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COHORT AND DEFINITIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Subtype was assigned from the sequenced specimen's receptor status (HR_STATUS x OVERALL_HER2_STATUS);
samples with unknown or equivocal HR/HER2 were excluded (1,918 -> 1,814):

  HR+/HER2-  1,362 samples (75.1%)      HR+/HER2+   132 (7.3%)
  TNBC         250 (13.8%)              HR-/HER2+    70 (3.9%)

903 primary / 911 metastatic; 795 treatment-naive primary, 108 post-treatment primary, 911 metastatic.
Genes with >=10 altered samples were tested with a 2x4 chi-square plus per-subtype Fisher exact tests,
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR controlled. 198 genes tested for mutation (450 in the matrix), 100 for
amplification, 16 for homozygous deletion. The CNA file contains only 0, +2 and -2 calls, so only
high-level amplification and homozygous deletion can be assessed (no shallow gains/losses).

The answer is: the four clinical subtypes are four genuinely different genomic diseases, not one
landscape at graded frequency. Two of the four classic "subtype genes" (CDH1 and ESR1) turn out to be
driven by histology and by therapy exposure respectively rather than by receptor subtype itself.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. HR+/HER2- (n = 1,362): a PI3K-driven, p53-sparing, endocrine-adapted landscape
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PIK3CA          42.5%  (42.7% including amplification)     <- highest of all subtypes, q=6.3e-10
  GATA3           18.0%                                     <- luminal-specific, q=6.0e-08
  CDH1            18.5%  (but see below - histology artefact)
  MAP3K1           9.8%                                     <- luminal-specific, q=0.011
  ESR1            10.3%  (exposure-dependent, see section 5)
  AKT1             6.4%  (87 samples; 90.8% of them PIK3CA-wild-type)
  TP53            23.3%  <- lowest of all subtypes (significantly depleted, q=1.6e-70)
  CCND1 amp       21.6%;  FGF3/FGF4/FGF19 amp 18-19%;  FGFR1 amp 14.0%
  PI3K-AKT pathway altered in 55.3% (highest); ERBB2 amplification 0.4% (lowest)

Actionable subcohorts: (a) PIK3CA-mutant, 42.5%, 78% of variants at canonical hotspots
(p.H1047R 207, p.E545K 128, p.E542K 75, p.N345K 48) -> PI3K-alpha inhibitor + fulvestrant;
(b) AKT1 p.E17K, 6.4%, near-mutually exclusive with PIK3CA (OR=0.12, p=1.4e-12) -> pan-AKT
inhibitor, a subcohort invisible to PIK3CA-only testing; (c) ESR1 LBD mutation 1.4% in untreated
primaries vs 19.2% in metastases -> oral SERD; (d) ERBB2 activating point mutation (p.L755S,
p.S310F, p.V777L, p.L869R) in 3.9%, and 52 of the 68 non-amplified ERBB2-mutant tumours in the cohort
are HR+/HER2- -> HER2 TKI in HER2-non-amplified disease, undetectable by IHC/FISH; (e) FGFR1
amplification 14.0% and CCND1 amplification 21.6%.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. HR+/HER2+ (n = 132) and HR-/HER2+ (n = 70): ERBB2-driven with an elevated p53 defect
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ERBB2 amplification   79.5% (HR+/HER2+) and 90.0% (HR-/HER2+);  0.4% HR+/HER2-, 0% TNBC
  ERBB2 any alteration  81.1% and 91.4% (adding point mutations)
  TP53 mutation         47.0% and 78.6% (vs 23.3% in HR+/HER2-; pairwise OR=2.9, p=2.5e-08 for
                        HR+/HER2+ vs HR+/HER2-)
  PIK3CA mutation       31.8% and 32.9% (lower than HR+/HER2-, OR=0.63 pairwise vs HR+/HER2-)
  CDK12 amp 54.5%/60.0%; RARA amp 25.0%/11.4%; SPOP amp 12.9%/20.0%; HOXB13 amp 4.5%/11.4%
  Luminal-type mutations reduced: CDH1 12.1%, GATA3 12.1%, MAP3K1 2.3%, AKT1 0%, ESR1 6.1%

An important negative result: no gene is FDR-significantly *enriched* in HR+/HER2+ relative to the
rest of the cohort (TP53 q=0.33), because TP53 is even more frequent in HR-/HER2+ and TNBC. HR+/HER2+
is a hybrid group statistically - it is defined by ERBB2 amplification plus loss of luminal-type
mutations, not by a unique point-mutation signature.

Artefact control: CDK12 amplification is 99.1% co-occurring with ERBB2 amplification (115/116), and
RARA 95%, i.e. these are passengers of the 17q12 amplicon, not independent targets. Only ERBB2 itself
is subtype-defining in this region.
Actionable subcohort: ERBB2 itself (79-90%); the second largest and clinically relevant subcohort is
PIK3CA-mutant HER2+ disease (~1/3 of both groups).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. TNBC (n = 250): a p53 / RB1 / PTEN tumour-suppressor landscape with a distinct copy-number profile
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  TP53 mutation          81.2%   <- highest; enriched vs rest, q=1.6e-56
  RB1 alteration         16.8%   <- 8x the 2.0% seen in all other subtypes combined (q=1.5e-25)
                                 (mutation 11.2% + homozygous deletion 5.6%)
  PTEN alteration        13.2%   (mutation 8.8% + homozygous deletion 4.4%; q=0.024)
  PIK3R1 mutation         8.0%   (vs 0.8-4.3% elsewhere; q=9.1e-11)
  MYC amplification      15.6%   <- highest of all subtypes
  PIK3CA mutation        18.8%   <- lowest of all subtypes (depleted, q=2.1e-10)
  CDH1/GATA3/ESR1 markedly lower (8.0% / 3.6% / 0.4%)
  BRCA1 2.4%, BRCA2 4.0%, PALB2 1.6%, ATM 5.2% (DDR pathway 12.4%, not subtype-specific)
  ERBB2 amplification 0%; ERBB2 activating point mutation 5.2% (13/250, all non-amplified)
  Mutational burden: median 5 non-synonymous mutations/sample vs 3 in HR+/HER2- (q=7.8e-09)

Actionable subcohorts: (a) RB1-loss TNBC, 16.8% (CDK4/6-inhibitor and platinum-sensitivity context,
and the RB1-loss/luminal-AR-like subgroup); (b) PTEN-loss TNBC, 13.2% -> PI3K/AKT-directed trials;
(c) AKT1 p.E17K, 4.0% (10/250), ~90% PIK3CA-wild-type -> AKT inhibitor; (d) ERBB2 activating
mutation in HER2-non-amplified TNBC, 5.2% -> HER2 TKI; (e) somatic BRCA1/BRCA2/PALB2/ATM in ~10%
-> PARP-inhibitor eligibility context, but germline status is not in these files; (f) MYC
amplification 15.6% (prognostic, not directly targetable).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Two "subtype" signals that are NOT about receptor subtype
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
(a) CDH1: 83.2% in invasive lobular carcinoma vs 2.0% in invasive ductal carcinoma. ILC makes up
    18.9% of HR+/HER2- but only 8.0% of TNBC, so the raw HR+/HER2- CDH1 frequency (18.5%) is
    inflated by histology. In an IDC-only re-analysis (n=1,399) CDH1 is no longer subtype-associated
    (q=0.74), while TP53, PIK3CA, GATA3, ESR1, MAP3K1, NF1, RB1 and PIK3R1 all remain significant.
(b) ESR1 is an acquired, therapy-exposure effect rather than a subtype marker: within HR+/HER2-,
    ESR1 mutation is 1.4% (9/657) in treatment-naive primaries, 13.2% (10/76) in post-treatment
    primaries and 19.2% (121/629) in metastases (Fisher p=1.1e-29). Treatment-naive variants are
    mostly non-canonical (3/10 canonical), whereas 83.6% of metastatic ESR1 variants are canonical
    LBD hotspots (p.D538G 57, p.Y537S 37, p.E380Q 17, p.Y537C/N 23) - the expected signature of
    selective pressure from aromatase inhibition.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Design-choice sensitivity
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Both of the major design choices were re-run with identical code: (i) one sample per patient
(n=1,678) reproduced all 15 significant genes; (ii) subtype defined on the archival primary tumour
instead of the sequenced specimen (n=1,806; the two definitions agree in 90.5% of samples) gave
13 significant genes, 11 of them shared, with unchanged frequencies; the 4 genes that fell below
threshold (CREBBP 39 variants, EPHA7 15, NF1 82, SMARCA4 22) are low-frequency and shift across the
FDR boundary with the changed group sizes. No headline conclusion depends on either choice.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. What this analysis cannot conclude
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- No survival, response or treatment-duration data are present, so the alteration-to-drug mapping
  above is annotation, not evidence of benefit in this cohort.
- No germline data: BRCA1/2 calls here are somatic and panel-restricted, so PARP-inhibitor
  eligibility cannot be determined, and small indels/large rearrangements are under-detected.
- Primary-vs-metastasis differences come from different patients' biopsies, not paired longitudinal
  samples; acquisition cannot be separated from pre-existing subclonal spatial heterogeneity.
- The metastatic arm is simultaneously post-treatment and a different organ site, so the ESR1
  result cannot separate endocrine-therapy pressure from microenvironment effects.
- Receptor status is IHC/FISH-based, without RNA-level (PAM50) or protein-level confirmation.
- Burden/TMB is panel-derived (~30 Mb, median 3-5 mutations/sample; only 12/1,814 samples reach
  TMB >= 1 mut/Mb) and must not be compared with exome TMB or used for TMB-high patient selection.
- Several genes have <40 variants (AKT1, PIK3R1, RB1, NF1, BRCA1), giving Wilson 95% CIs of roughly
  +/-3-6 percentage points on subtype frequencies; small differences should not be over-read.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BOTTOM LINE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The subtypes separate along two axes: an ER-luminal/PI3K axis (PIK3CA 42.5%, GATA3 18%, MAP3K1 9.8%,
AKT1 6.4%, low TP53 23.3% in HR+/HER2-; PIK3CA drops to 18.8% in TNBC) and a p53/ERBB2 axis
(TP53 81.2% in TNBC and 78.6% in HR-/HER2+; ERBB2 amplified in 79.5-90.0% of both HER2+ groups but
0-0.4% of TNBC/HR+/HER2-). Within each subtype the profiling exposes actionable subcohorts that the
clinical receptor label alone does not capture: PIK3CA and AKT1 mutations plus acquired ESR1
mutations and non-amplified ERBB2 mutations in HR+/HER2-; PIK3CA mutations on top of ERBB2 in the
HER2+ groups; and RB1 loss, PTEN loss, AKT1 p.E17K, non-amplified ERBB2 mutation and homologous-
recombination defects in TNBC. Conversely, two apparent subtype associations are confounded: CDH1
(lobular histology) and ESR1 (prior endocrine therapy).
